P162278-A1.text: national georeferenced cadastral platform consolidating municipal and multi-agency data. A national GIS platform consolidates municipal and multi-agency cadastral data, integrating disaster risk maps to produce hazard exposure information for planning. Practices: national cadastral information system consolidating municipal cadaster data; georeferenced land information system for risk and land-use planning; national data platform consolidating urban cadaster data; Cadastral data integrated with disaster risk maps for hazard exposure; Centralized GIS cadastral database integrating multi-agency data; National Urban Cadaster platform for urban management information. (iii) the development and implementation of a national level cadastral information system; 21. The generation of cadastral information will enable the creation of a geographically referenced land information system that will be used for resilient land use and disaster risk management planning. For example, the combination and aggregation of use of different types of imagery and other data with the municipal cadasters produced by the Project could inform risk mitigation efforts as well as climate change adaptation scenarios for land use planning and infrastructure investments.
P162278-A1.name: national georeferenced cadastral platform consolidating municipal and multi-agency data

P158418-A1.text: GIS-enabled SUTEM irrigation MIS rollout for water user associations. The project scales a GIS-enabled irrigation management information system to 378 water user associations, with tablets, hardware, training and registry links for water and land decisions. Practices: SUTEM irrigation information system for WUA water management; Web-based GIS-enabled participatory water monitoring system for WUAs; GIS-enabled SUTEM MIS for national WUA performance monitoring; Nationwide SUTEM MIS rollout after field trials; SUTEM irrigation MIS mainstreamed across 378 Water User Associations; SUTEM irrigation MIS mainstreamed in 378 WUAs; GIS-enabled SUTEM irrigation MIS integrated with land and civil registries; SUTEM irrigation management software for water user associations; Tablet-based GIS field data collection for SUTEM rollout. Beneficiaries also include approximately 100 staff from DSI’s regional offices and 600 staff from 378 WUAs, who will be equipped and trained in the use of the SUTEM irrigation information system, which will strengthen WUA’s capacity for O&M, water conservation, financial management, governance, M&E, and communications. The project will be monitored through DSI’s existing Management Information System (MIS), which will be further enhanced by the implementation of the national, web-based and GIS-enabled participatory water monitoring system for the WUAs (Subcomponent 2A). Component 2: Innovation and Institutional Support (US$2 million): This component will provide direct design and implementation support to DSI in the following areas: (a) Subcomponent 2 (A) -Designing and Piloting a National Program for WUA Capacity-Building (GEF, US$1.29 million): This GEF funded activity will provide support to DSI for the mainstreaming, at the national level, of their newly developed irrigation Management Information System (MIS), called SUTEM[1]. The MIS, which is GIS enabled, is designed to support smart-decision making and increase the WUAs operational efficiency by centralizing data related to physical (irrigation network condition, type of water source and availability, etc.), socio-economic (total number of water users/farmers, crop types and cropping patterns, etc.) and managerial (assessment and collection of service charges, investment needs, etc) aspects of the targeted irrigation schemes.
P158418-A1.name: GIS-enabled SUTEM irrigation MIS rollout for water user associations

P162302-A3.text: climate budget coding and tracking system. TA operationalizes a climate budget coding and tracking system within the MTBF. This would involve efforts to integrate a climate change lens in the Medium-Term Budgetary Framework (MTBF), including an amendment in the Budget Call Circular (BCC), capacity building for climate change expenditure tracking, operationalizing a climate budget coding and tracking system and promoting climate adaptation and mitigation in the planning process.
P162302-A3.name: climate budget coding and tracking system

P163679-A1.text: hourly simulation and AI virtual power plant for storage absorption. The project uses an hourly production simulation model and a possible AI-enabled virtual power plant pilot to quantify and raise renewable energy absorption with battery storage. Practices: hourly production simulation model to quantify battery-enabled RE absorption; AI-enabled virtual power plant pilot with demand-side management. In the study conducted at the national level, the China power system is divided into eight regions to estimate the incremental RE absorption, defined as the difference of RE dispatched in simulations of ‘with’ and ‘without’ battery storage cases. The simulations were conducted using an hourly production simulation model. The model has been used to support the State Grid Corporation to conduct the 2017 and 2018 annual review of RE integration in China and to support NEA in its studies to analyze RE integration in China. A concept of ‘virtual power plant’ may be piloted with advanced IT and artificial intelligence technologies and demand-side management measures.
P163679-A1.name: hourly simulation and AI virtual power plant for storage absorption

P162599-A1.text: open-access PPP reverse-auction subsidies for rural broadband connectivity. Uses competitive least-cost reverse auctions and open-access PPP contracts to subsidize wholesale broadband in climate-vulnerable unserved white areas. Practices: MFD criteria-based selection of climate-vulnerable unserved 'white areas' for connectivity subsidy; Open Access People-first PPP wholesale broadband subsidy; Reverse-auction least-cost subsidy tender for fiber network; Open Access PPP for rural ICT coverage extension; technology-neutral open-access PPP bidding for rural connectivity; low-cost microsite third-party rural access model; Competitive tender selecting most economically advantageous coverage offer; Open-access PPP contracts with claw-back for rural broadband; Competitive transparent process for subsidized rural wireless infrastructure; Reversed-auction PPP for Parakou metropolitan fiber network. This component is designed around the Maximizing Financing for Development (MFD) approach (Figure 4) to leverage private investments and optimize the use of public funding. A set of criteria (see Annex 2) was established for: (i) the identification of target areas; and (ii) infrastructure financing. The selection criteria for the target areas will include susceptibility to climate changes, and the design will incorporate multiple levels of redundancy to ensure high availability of service to the vulnerable zones. • For target areas, workshops with public stakeholders and private operators led to the identification of geographic unserved or underserved “white areas” in which the supply of ICT connectivity is nonexistent or insufficient, have high susceptibility to climatic changes and may not be reached under pure market terms because the inherent profitability of investment is too low (“market failure”). • For project design, Component 1 will first focus on improving the legal and regulatory framework (and support related capacity building initiatives for public agencies) to address the market failure and bring about positive incentives for additional infrastructure roll-out. Sub-Component 1.2 – Supporting the extension of ICT coverage in rural areas using Open Access People- first Public-Private Partnership (PfPPP) arrangements.
P162599-A1.name: open-access PPP reverse-auction subsidies for rural broadband connectivity

P162599-A2.text: digital payment and savings products for women's groups and merchants. Digitizes women's saving groups and value-chain payments, linking mobile money to bank accounts and subsidizing merchant payment devices. Practices: Digitization of women's informal saving groups; Cost-shared MIS upgrades for FI-MNO interoperability; mobile savings and transaction-history credit scoring products; co-financed digital payment infrastructure for value chain buyers; bundled digital payments with commitment savings and insurance; merchant vouchers for digital payment devices with bookkeeping; Two-way mobile money to bank/MFI account linkage; Digital payment equipment grants for value-chain associations and MSMEs; Apps mirroring women's tontine saving group processes; Merchant vouchers subsidizing digital payment acceptance devices; tiered risk-based KYC for women's tontine groups. To ensure the sustainable growth of financial services in rural areas, the project will support (i) the digitization of services offered by financial institutions serving rural areas; Component 2 will catalyze the uptake of digital financial services in rural areas, with a focus on women in the agriculture sector. Embracing opportunities offered by mobile technology to advance financial inclusion requires various efforts from financial institutions including partnering with mobile network operators (MNOs), adapting their own management information systems (MIS), products and processes in order to create new solutions. To support these efforts that are costly and sometimes unbearable for some financial institutions (FIs), especially microfinance institutions (MFIs) and small banks, the project will finance: (i) the evaluation and upgrade of the information systems of selected financial institutions to allow interface with MNOs and improve data security by covering up to (a maximum of) 50 percent of the costs of the upgrade for banks and 75 percent of the costs for MFIs;
P162599-A2.name: digital payment and savings products for women's groups and merchants

P162599-A3.text: interoperability platforms, MIS upgrades and mobile climate advisory apps. Builds shared bank-mobile operator interfaces, upgrades MFI systems, and delivers voice/image literacy and mobile climate information apps to farmers. Practices: shared digital interoperability platform linking banks and mobile operators; apps mirroring tontine processes for first-time low-literacy users; voice and image financial literacy apps with mobile training units; mobile-based climate information systems for farmers; MIS upgrade grants for MFIs to interface with mobile money; MIS-to-mobile-money platform interfacing options; Voice-and-image digital literacy apps for rural users; Digital producer registry delivering real-time climate early-warning to farmers; Mobile climate information apps for smallholder farmers; mobile-phone and NDVI/satellite data for extension advice; Shared common MIS for multiple financial institutions; analytics-linked mobile app for extension agents' location-specific advice. (ii) the creation of a shared digital platform that could be an interface between the information systems of the selected financial institutions and the mobile network operators systems; (ii) the creation of apps or other technologies that could mirror the processes and features of saving groups and are intuitive to first-time users with low levels of formal education; and (iii) the creation of new financial products for women’s groups where digital payments could be bundled with commitment savings, and / or insurance products, together with financial education (based on solutions developed by existing apps in the market or new apps). (iv) improvement of digital skills through large campaigns to raise awareness, training of women’s associations, farmers, and development of apps on financial literacy with adequate content (e.g. using voice and image ). These digital skills trainings will be provided through regional agriculture service centers and Mobile Training Units that will move around the target areas.
P162599-A3.name: interoperability platforms, MIS upgrades and mobile climate advisory apps

P162599-A4.text: digital farmer registry and climate early-warning system. Registers smallholders digitally for service targeting and monitoring, and runs climate and natural hazard early-warning and response systems. Practices: digital registry of smallholder farmers for targeting services; climate and natural hazards early warning and response system; ICT availability mapping for rural policy makers; Digital farmer registration registry for service targeting and M&E baseline. The digital registry of smallholder farmers will be utilized throughout the project to enable needs assessments, communications, and for targeting training and services to smallholder farmers. (iii) support for capacity-building for the MAEP; and (iv) digital registration of the smallholder farmers in the four selected value chains. The project will also implement a climate and natural hazards monitoring, early warning and incidence response system. Technical Assistance to map the ICT availability in the country, and more specifically in the targeted rural areas – The ICT mapping technical assistance will focus on gathering data related to the deployment of ICT services in the targeted areas and presenting them in a friendly manner to policy makers.
P162599-A4.name: digital farmer registry and climate early-warning system

P162599-A5.text: GIS road asset management with smartphone citizen grievance reporting. Uses GIS geo-mapping, roughness and accessibility indices plus smartphone citizen engagement to manage and maintain rural roads. Practices: GIS-enabled road asset management applications (geo-mapping, Road Roughness Index, Rural Accessibility Index) with smartphone Citizen Engagement System for rural road maintenance; GIS geo-mapping and smartphone citizen engagement for rural roads; GIS road asset apps with smartphone citizen grievance system. (ii) implementing digital transport applications; This sub-component will develop GIS-enabled applications for geo-mapping of rural networks, measurement and analysis of the Road Roughness Index and Rural Accessibility Index, and management of public grievances through a smartphone-enabled Citizen Engagement System. These digital applications will be integrated into the Road Asset Management System to help the RC with the maintenance of rural roads. This sub-component will develop GIS-enabled applications for geomapping of rural networks, measurement and analysis of the Road Roughness Index and Rural Accessibility Index, and management of public grievances through a smartphone-enabled Citizen Engagement System.
P162599-A5.name: GIS road asset management with smartphone citizen grievance reporting

P162599-A6.text: ICT infrastructure and service mapping for rural connectivity targeting. Maps mobile sites, backhaul, 2G/3G coverage, prices and demand to target rural ICT investment It will focus on: (i) infrastructure-mapping and service-mapping, with the current status of the ICT infrastructure itself (i.e. mobile sites, power electricity availability, trackway access, Page 77 of 111 The World Bank Benin Digital Rural Transformation (P162599) backhauling availability) and the service availability (i.e. (ii) demand-mapping, with the demand typology and quantification for ICT services (voice, SMS, data) to address end-users needs (e.g. rural smallholders and local public administrations) and deliver e-Agriculture services in a satisfactory manner; (iii) investment-mapping, with the existing and potentially planned investments in ICT infrastructure by the private and public sector (e.g. fiber backbone extension). • Activity 1.2.2.
P162599-A6.name: ICT infrastructure and service mapping for rural connectivity targeting

P163711-A1.text: integrated IT statistical data system with CAPI collection and open-data warehouse. The project builds an integrated IT statistics system using CAPI tablets, a single data warehouse and open-data dissemination with metadata and user feedback. Practices: Unified IT-based statistical data collection, transmission, processing, storage and dissemination system; Electronic data collection for poverty measurement; Large data warehouses with electronic collection and open-data dissemination; Open user-friendly data dissemination with metadata and manipulation tools; Rolling online and mobile-app user satisfaction survey on NSC website; CAPI-based survey data collection and open-data dissemination; Software automating NSC workflows and digitalizing data collection via Tunduk; CAPI digitization of statistical surveys; CAPI-based digitization of statistical surveys; Tablet-based CAPI data collection replacing paper surveys; Single NSC data warehouse integrating administrative data. It needs to revamp and introduce a unified data collection, transmission, processing, storage, and dissemination system by introducing new information technology (IT)-based data systems. These systems will also support generation of higher data granularity needed to develop evidence-based policies at subnational and municipal levels. The statistical components of the Project will contribute to digitalization and development of e-economy through introduction of electronic data collection for poverty measurement. This component will support the improvement of statistical infrastructure that will enable management of large data warehouses, collection of data via electronic means and secure transmission, storage, and dissemination of the data in open data formats.
P163711-A1.name: integrated IT statistical data system with CAPI collection and open-data warehouse

P163711-A2.text: Use of administrative data for statistics through government systems interoperability. Project supports greater use of administrative data through interoperable government systems for statistics. Areas of Project support on statistics will focus on operationalization of the new Law on Official Statistics, the national statistical system’s progress toward digitalization, greater utilization of administrative data based on the government systems interoperability, streamlining of the system’s institutional relations and settings, improvements in statistical education, and an upgrade of the underlying IT hardware and software infrastructure.
P163711-A2.name: Use of administrative data for statistics through government systems interoperability

P163711-A3.text: risk-based tax administration automation and electronic statistics collection. The project automates tax compliance, VAT refund risk scoring and ISNAK data exchange, while moving statistical surveys to electronic collection and anonymized processing. Practices: Tax compliance management system with risk analysis and business analytics; Risk-based automation of VAT refund claims; automated case management system for tax enforcement; Workflow management system computing statistical process elapsed times; Automated risk-based evaluation of VAT refund claims; Automated data exchange between ISNAK and other entities; Taxpayer portal for electronic filing and multi-channel notification; Risk-ranking algorithms for non-compliance and enforcement priority; Risk-engine algorithms for risk-based audit case selection; VAT gap calculation methodology with automated data collection; Enhanced ISNAK with integrated online taxpayer self-service portal; Open-format data dissemination with metadata and manipulation tools; Replacing paper questionnaires with electronic data collection; Electronic survey questionnaires replacing hard-copy collection; Custom statistical processing software with PII anonymization and data merging; Single NSC data warehouse consolidating administrative and survey data; Anonymization techniques masking PII in survey and census data. It will provide support for: (i) carrying out of business process reengineering to enable institutional, legal and procedural improvements of tax administration; and (ii) implementation of a tax compliance management system, including the development of methodologies and strengthening of the tax administration capacity in functional areas, including, inter alia, taxpayers’ registration, tax return and payment processing, enforcement and compliance, tax audit, risk analysis, appeals process, and business analytics. P163711-A4.text: digitalization of local household registers with automated source validation. The project digitalizes rural and municipal household registers and applies GAMSO-based automated validation so local staff correct data at source. Practices: Digitalization of the Rural Household Register; GAMSO-based centralized automated data validation at source; Digitalization of municipal Household Books into statistics warehouse. (iii) digitalization of the Rural Household Register (RHR); The benefit of eliminating the oblast level would be two-fold: • Improve and strengthen the statistical system at the ground level, including staff who collect and compile statistics on municipalities and in rural households, thus empowering them with access to centralized automated software tools to check and correct data collection and data entry at source. • Strengthen the top, or central, level of the NSC, where statistical methodologies are developed to aggregate data, mash-up data on different topics to produce newer insights using data-analytics tools and prepare socio-economic indicators of interest to the Government and the public. It will be achieved by introducing GAMSO. The immediate need is to continue working on digitalization of the Household Book (HB) and improving the capacity of municipal civil servants responsible for collecting statistics at the Ayil Okmotu (local self-governments) level.
P163711-A4.name: digitalization of local household registers with automated source validation

P163711-A5.text: Tunduk-based inter-agency data exchange protocols for statistics. The project sets up electronic data-exchange protocols and agreements linking government registers to statistical registers through the Tunduk system. Practices: Tunduk system for inter-agency information sharing; Automated data exchange protocols and centralized data warehouse; Electronic data-exchange protocols linking government registers to statistical registers; Tunduk interagency information exchange system for statistics. This sub-component will support further development of protocols and agreements to enable sharing of information between the STS and other government bodies and third parties through the existing Kyrgyz Tunduk information exchange system. Advisory support will be provided to develop necessary protocols for data exchange between the STS and other agencies (e.g.: statistical bodies, courts, chambers, ministries, etc.), develop an integration model and protocols for automated data exchange between the STS and other government bodies as well as private sector institutions. Provide consulting support for the continued centralization of data obtained from third parties. xiii. It is important to strengthen the protocols of electronic data exchange with the registers of the State Tax Service, Ministry of Justice and other major data collection institutions (Ministry of Education, Ministry of Health, State Customs Service, National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic and other agencies).
P163711-A5.name: Tunduk-based inter-agency data exchange protocols for statistics

P164336-A1.text: mobile-phone market information and demand aggregation for pastoralists. Mobile apps and decision support systems deliver prices, weather, pasture and conflict data and aggregate producer demand for market decisions. Practices: Mobile-phone demand aggregation and livestock market information system; Mobile-phone livestock market information system; Integrated decision support system for value chains; two-way mobile apps gathering producer and market operator data; Mobile phone delivery of market, weather and conflict information. A third set of activities to be supported includes the piloting of innovative market arrangements such as livestock auctions; the development of product standards, traceability, and certification systems; the use of mobile phones to aggregate demand and conduct other commercial transactions; and scaling up the Livestock Market Information System. A livestock market information system based on mobile-phone applications will improve access in PAP areas to timely and reliable information for decision making, such as prices for different agricultural commodities in nearby markets. Rather than developing a brand-new system, the project will scale up livestock market information systems that have been launched by other projects. In particular, an integrated decision support system could provide access to the following key information: prices of major commodities in nearby markets, condition of pastures, water points, nearby markets, and conflicts.
P164336-A1.name: mobile-phone market information and demand aggregation for pastoralists

P164336-A2.text: digital rangeland monitoring and livestock traceability systems. Satellite, drone and GIS tools monitor rangelands and feed balance, while digital systems trace and certify livestock products. Practices: Integrated pastoral decision support system for rangeland and markets; Drone mapping of rangelands and remote-sensing rangeland monitoring; Mobile-phone integrated decision support system for pastoralists; Digital traceability system for livestock products; Remote sensing for rangeland and feed balance monitoring; PAP livelihoods decision support information system linked to web-based MIS; NDVI/biomass satellite index for rangeland impact monitoring; GIS-based rangeland and pasture monitoring system from satellite imagery; Digital traceability and certification systems for livestock products; Drone mapping of rangelands and grazing units; satellite imagery biomass estimation for rangeland monitoring; satellite imagery and biomass tools for rangeland impact monitoring; digitized resource maps and pictographic rangeland plan tracking; geo-spatial platform with drone imagery of rangeland improvements; Remote sensing rangeland monitoring for management decisions; Animal identification and traceability system for livestock exports. In addition, Subcomponent 3.3 will introduce digital technologies and pilot other innovations to solve critical bottlenecks in PAP value chains. Such technologies could include, for example, an integrated pastoral decision support system (rainfall, pasture, water availability, market price, conflict early warning etc.), certification and traceability systems for livestock products, and geo-spatial monitoring, among others. Examples include the development of an integrated decision support system that relies on mobile phones, use of drones to map rangelands, deploying technology for improving traceability of livestock products to assess the potential for scaling them up across the project geography. Rangeland performance will be monitored through remote sensing.
P164336-A2.name: digital rangeland monitoring and livestock traceability systems

P164336-A3.text: Mobile-phone demand aggregation for livestock commercial transactions. Project finances market arrangements using mobile phones to aggregate demand and facilitate livestock sales (2) rolling out product standards and traceability and certification systems; To spur innovation in the market space, in addition to productive partnerships, the project will finance new innovative market arrangements that include: (1) developing auctions;
P164336-A3.name: Mobile-phone demand aggregation for livestock commercial transactions

P164336-A4.text: crowdsourced mobile-app data collection by pastoralist communities. Communities report rangeland, production and marketing data via mobile-friendly apps into the PAP information system (2) distributed data collection (including crowdsourcing involving PAP communities in the main areas of rangeland management, production and productivity of PAP production system, and marketing through the established links) using technology and tools connecting users at all levels using mobile- friendly apps; The PAP information system will consist of (1) conventional electronic databases residing in cloud servers;
P164336-A4.name: crowdsourced mobile-app data collection by pastoralist communities

P164435-A1.text: geospatial least-cost planning and GIS site selection for PV mini-grids. ESMAP-funded geospatial datasets, GIS analysis and prepaid smart metering identify and de-risk private mini-grid sites for off-grid electrification. Practices: Geospatial least-cost off-grid electrification planning dataset; Geospatial analysis siting PV mini-grids for private operation; GIS-based transparent site selection for mini-grids; Prepaid smart metering required for mini-grid bankability; GIS geotagged building dataset for mini-grid site selection; Geospatial electrification planning platform for grid and off-grid investment. Project design is underpinned by comprehensive, data-driven analytics. With ESMAP support, Burundi is developing a least-cost geospatial plan, off-grid market assessment, public facilities needs inventory, an energy access survey and a clean cooking assessment. These studies are informing project preparation and will strengthen implementation; they will also contribute to the preparation of the Government’s off -grid strategy. A geospatial analysis funded by ESMAP has already identified approximately 150 potential mini-grids for locations that are not expected to be connected to the national grid in the short term and mid-term, with the potential to provide electricity to 90,000 customers and at the same time creating economic opportunities and supporting electrification of public facilities in those communities.
P164435-A1.name: geospatial least-cost planning and GIS site selection for PV mini-grids

P164435-A2.text: In-country GIS monitoring capacity to update least-cost electrification plans. Project establishes in-country GIS capacity to track progress and update plans Key to ensuring the effectiveness, sustainability, and dynamism over time of the geospatial approach is the establishment of GIS monitoring capacity within the country to track progress and facilitate updates of the least-cost plans. Geospatial plans constitute a data-driven approach to planning for the efficient and effective deployment of limited resources, particularly aimed at supporting countries with high access deficits.
P164435-A2.name: In-country GIS monitoring capacity to update least-cost electrification plans

P164435-A3.text: geospatial electrification planning platform with multi-tier access survey. A hosted geospatial planning platform and national energy database, backed by MTF access surveys, guide electrification strategy and investment decisions. Practices: Multi-tier framework survey for nationwide energy access data; geospatial analysis and planning platform for electrification. The multi-tier framework (MTF) survey which applies the multitier framework methodology for energy access and is expected to be completed by mid-2020, will provide detailed information on the energy access situation of households, including quantity and quality of services provided by all available (main and backup) sources of electricity, magnitude and frequency of energy expenditures, and willingness to pay. Besides the project-specific results monitoring, the World Bank is also supporting the Government to establish better data on the nationwide electrification rate which will be helpful for evaluation of the project’s broader impacts on Burundi’s state of electricity access. The baseline and the follow-up survey at the end of the project will allow for the quantification of improvements in energy service delivery in the country and could also be used for impact evaluation of development outcomes. P164967-A1.text: digital tools for agricultural insurance and interest rate subsidy delivery. The project digitizes crop insurance underwriting, policy dissemination and claim settlement, and plans an e-voucher system for interest rate subsidies. Practices: Digitized agricultural insurance underwriting and claim settlement tools; e-voucher/digitalization of the Interest Rate Subsidy Fund for agriculture. This will entail that GoS pays off current premium subsidy arrears due to CNAAS as well as the reinforcement of more upstream activities including: mass awareness campaigns on the benefits of agricultural insurance; capacity-building for collecting rainfall as well as remote sensing data to design index-based insurance products; developing tools for a complete digitization of the whole underwriting process, as well as policy dissemination and claim settlement; and developing an early warning system, including an agricultural observatory. (ii) Improving access to agricultural insurance, with the objective of reaching at least 400,000 farmers and developing this business line with a view to securing sustainability in the long term (an exit plan from the current premium subsidy system should be in place by 2024). P164967-A2.text: Index-based agricultural insurance using rainfall and remote sensing data. Project builds capacity to collect rainfall and remote-sensing data to design index-based insurance products. This will entail that GoS pays off current premium subsidy arrears due to CNAAS as well as the reinforcement of more upstream activities including: mass awareness campaigns on the benefits of agricultural insurance; capacity-building for collecting rainfall as well as remote sensing data to design index-based insurance products; developing tools for a complete digitization of the whole underwriting process, as well as policy dissemination and claim settlement; and developing an early warning system, including an agricultural observatory. (ii) Improving access to agricultural insurance, with the objective of reaching at least 400,000 farmers and developing this business line with a view to securing sustainability in the long term (an exit plan from the current premium subsidy system should be in place by 2024).
P164967-A2.name: Index-based agricultural insurance using rainfall and remote sensing data

P164967-A3.text: Early warning system and agricultural observatory. Project supports developing an early warning system including an agricultural observatory. This will entail that GoS pays off current premium subsidy arrears due to CNAAS as well as the reinforcement of more upstream activities including: mass awareness campaigns on the benefits of agricultural insurance; capacity-building for collecting rainfall as well as remote sensing data to design index-based insurance products; developing tools for a complete digitization of the whole underwriting process, as well as policy dissemination and claim settlement; and developing an early warning system, including an agricultural observatory.
P164967-A3.name: Early warning system and agricultural observatory

P166539-A1.text: Inter-agency data exchange for one-stop business registration. Project builds a data exchange solution linking Registrar General, Revenue Authority, Social Security and Metropolitan Authority into a one-stop e-Registrar. It will also support the inter-connectivity of all agencies related to new business registrations (Registrar General, Ghana Revenue Authority, Social Security, Metropolitan Authority), in order to create a one-stop shop for business registration. This will include development of a data exchange solution, as well as required staff training to effectively support, maintain, and operate this e-Registrar solution. By investing in these tools and capacity building, this support will lead to a more streamlined registration procedure for businesses, leading to the following outcomes: • Reduce the regulatory burden on foreign and domestic businesses to start up a business through reducing time and cost of compliance with business-registration procedures; • Improve the efficiency of business-registration services through simplifying and streamlining procedures for business registration, and automating registry functions; • Shift from the revenue-generating approach for the registration services to a self-sustained model covering cost of provision of registration services;
P166539-A1.name: Inter-agency data exchange for one-stop business registration

P166539-A2.text: Investor relationship management system for investment promotion. Project upgrades GIPC's investor tracking system into an IRMS managing relationships with existing and potential investors. Improving GIPC’s Systems and Tools: This subcomponent project will support the enhancement and/or deployment of the systems and tools to ensure that GIPC is efficient and maximizes its ability to service investors, by providing software, hardware and training as needed, including: • Investor relationship management system (IRMS): GIPC uses an investor tracking system where registered projects are recorded according to parameters such as sector, source country, and region in Ghana where the investment took place. The project will provide for the update and upgrade of the existing system to serve as a real tool for managing the relationship with existing and potential investors and supporting investment attraction and retention. • Investor information system (IIS): the IIS refers to the content, platform and mechanism for storing, updating and disseminating the information that investors request from an Investment Promotion Agency (IPA) such as GIPC.
P166539-A2.name: Investor relationship management system for investment promotion

P165683-A1.text: hydro-meteorological monitoring and water information decision-support systems. The project expands automatic hydro-meteorological and groundwater monitoring networks and upgrades the state water information system with decision-support tools for managers. It will provide support to improve policy instruments regarding water pricing, water allocation and demand management, as well as to expand the hydro-meteorological network and forecasting capacity. (b) Number of hydro-meteorological stations operational and feeding into the water information system; This component will support strengthening the institutional capacity for water resources management and meteorological and hydrological monitoring and forecasting and increasing the resilience of water supply systems to climate-related events. (b) Expansion and modernization of the State’s meteorological and hydrological monitoring, including the installation of automatized stations, computerized systems, and training;
P165683-A1.name: hydro-meteorological monitoring and water information decision-support systems

P165557-A2.text: Accountability dashboard updating learning grant utilization to trigger tranches. Circuit supervisors update learning grant utilization rates in the accountability dashboard to release subsequent grant tranches. Annually, CSs will review utilization of learning grants before updating the utilization rate in the accountability dashboard to trigger the flow of subsequent tranches of the learning grant.
P165557-A2.name: Accountability dashboard updating learning grant utilization to trigger tranches

P165557-A3.text: accountability dashboard opened to parents, students and CSO expenditure tracking. The project opens the accountability dashboard to parents, students and decision makers and links CSO expenditure tracking and satisfaction survey results to it. Practices: Accountability dashboard open to parents and students; CSO expenditure tracking and satisfaction surveys linked to dashboard. The accountability dashboard will also be accessible to decision makers at the school, district, regional, and national levels, as well as to parents and students, to increase efficiency of the system through data-driven decision making and to foster citizen engagement and community-led accountability. The sub-component will build on existing dashboards such as the mSRC and the USAID Partnership for Learning Project dashboard. (d) annual expenditure tracking survey on learning grants by CSOs to validate results; and (e) citizen satisfaction survey by CSOs conducted at mid-term and at the end of the project which would be linked to the dashboard. Such linkages would encourage discussion and monitoring of how beneficiaries’ feedback is addressed.

P166695-A1.text: e-Government Procurement system for competitive public bidding. The project introduces an e-GP system, with readiness assessment, pilot acquisition and adoption, to shift procurement to electronic competitive bidding. Practices: e-Government Procurement (e-GP) system for competitive bidding; e-GP pilot system for public procurement; e-GP adoption to increase procurement competition; e-GP electronic government procurement system; e-GP pilot with strategy, roadmap and change management. The PDO-level results indicators are as follows: • PDO Indicator 1: Value Added Tax (VAT) Gross compliance ratio. • PDO Indicator 2: Aggregate annual SOEs report prepared and published by the centralized oversight agency (SOE Commission). • PDO Indicator 3: Share of competitive biddings for procuring organizations using electronic Government Procurement (e-GP). P166695-A2.text: Integrated Tax Administration System with e-filing, e-payment and data analytics. The project implements a COTS-based ITAS with data warehouse, BI, mobile filing and interfaces to customs and PFM systems, plus online procurement training and ICT mapping. Practices: e-filing and e-payment tax services for taxpayers; Integrated Tax Management System with data warehouse and BI; online public procurement course and certification for procurement professionals; online course certification for procurement professionals; e-filing and e-payment tax administration platform; mobile payment and filing for micro and small taxpayers; interfacing ITAS with ASYCUDA World and IFMIS for data matching; Integrated Tax Administration System with e-filing and e-payment; ICT indicators unit with coverage and infrastructure maps. Objective: This sub-component aims to enhance the GRA’s operational effectiveness and achieving digital transformation, including through widespread adoption of electronic filing (e-filing) and electronic payments (e- payments) to improve taxpayer services and transparency. Online tax services and e-procurement will prepare to support the business continuity in future situations similar to this COVID-19 pandemic. (ii) the selection and implementation of a new Integrated Tax Management System (ITAS) using a Commercial Off-The Shelf (COTS) package. This will include the parametrization and customization of the COTS to the needs of GRA using a turnkey solution14 as an implementation strategy, and Data warehouse and Business Intelligence Systems including Mobile payment and filing option for micro and small taxpayers;

P166820-A1.text: road crash database and road asset management systems. The project builds a national crash database with a Road Safety Observatory and completes a road asset management system with network and condition data. Practices: Road accident reporting and analysis database for Road Safety Observatory; Road asset management system with WIMS, traffic counters and roughness profilers; Traffic accident reporting and analysis database; Road Safety Observatory with accident database and staff training. (iii) Support DSAI, the lead agency for road safety, to develop a Road Safety Strategy and to establish a Road Safety Observatory through provision of technical assistance, equipment, support for the design installation, commissioning and training of staff for a road accident reporting and analysis database, training of key staff in the management and operation of a Road Safety Observatory, and operating costs. The CARs-4 supports the missing elements of the RAMS, including: (i) collection of the national road network (14,000km) data, including geometry, location, condition, traffic volume and natural hazard exposure, (ii) development of asset management modules for bridges and tunnels within the RAMS, (iii) supply of additional data collection of equipment, (iv) technical assistance and capacity building for data analysis, (v) capacity-building for installation and operationalization of the traffic counters, and (vi) construction and operationalization of additional WIMS. The ongoing CARs-2 project laid the foundation for RAMS, including through deployment of Weight-in- Motion-System (WIMS), traffic counters, and roughness profilers. To that end, the project will support development of a National Road Safety Strategy, including education and measures to raise awareness for traffic safety, requirement for road safety audits, definition and treatment of blackspots, development of a traffic accident reporting and analysis database, restructuring the system of training and licensing of drivers, strengthening first-aid stations for traffic accidents; and mechanizing and modernizing the system for registering motorized vehicles.
P166820-A1.name: road crash database and road asset management systems

P166996-A1.text: ICT-based TVET voucher MIS for provider payments and beneficiary tracking. An internet-based TVET voucher MIS handles applications, assessment verification and provider payments, tracking beneficiaries for results-based disbursement. Practices: ICT-based TVET voucher with internet MIS tracking beneficiaries; TVET Voucher System tracking providers and beneficiaries for DLI payments. The project will adopt the voucher mechanism under the existing Ghana TVET Voucher Project to train apprentices and master craft persons, using training providers. The financing mechanism includes an internet-based MIS, which tracks individual beneficiaries and monitors their progress and performance. Specifically, the application process for the program, the assessment verification process, and the payment process are all ICT based. Year 1 refers to the Government’s fiscal year 2021. • Formalized, standardized, and quality-assured apprenticeship training refers to competency-based training as certified by COTVET, consistent with the country’s NTVETQF, and using the existing Ghana TVET Voucher Project’s system to provide payments to training providers and beneficiaries and to track the status, progress, and performance of providers and beneficiaries.
P166996-A1.name: ICT-based TVET voucher MIS for provider payments and beneficiary tracking

P166996-A2.text: Grant management MIS portal for cross-grantee peer learning. Shares grant activity and performance information across grantees via a dedicated portal in the grant management system. Second, the types of activities and inputs that are supported by grants, including on the progress and performance of grant implementation, will be shared across grantees, with the aim of fostering peer learning and positive peer competition. This information will be shared through a dedicated portal integrated into the grant management system.
P166996-A2.name: Grant management MIS portal for cross-grantee peer learning

P166996-A3.text: Unique-ID MIS and grant management systems for trainee and grantee tracking. Unique trainee and applicant IDs in TVET voucher, NBSSI and SDF grant systems track progress, payments and grant receipt for verification. Practices: TVET voucher MIS data sharing to grantee selection; Unique trainee IDs tracked in subcomponent MIS; Grant Management System with unique applicant IDs; TVET Voucher System tracking provider and beneficiary payments and progress; NBSSI subcomponent MIS with unique IDs for trainees and grantees; SDF grant management system tracking grants from application onward. First, information on individuals that underwent apprenticeship training under Component 1 will be shared with grantees under Subcomponent 2.2. This information will be obtained through the TVET voucher MIS, managed by COTVET. P166996-A4.text: Linked labor market and TVET information systems with offline and assistive access. GLMIS links TVMIS, Artisan Directory and Jobs Center databases, with offline capability and assistive technologies, while TVMIS and STI MIS track sector performance. Practices: GLMIS labor market information system with offline and assistive access; GLMIS labor market information system linked to agency databases; TVMIS and STI MIS sector performance tracking systems. The project will finance the development, operationalization, and maintenance of the GLMIS. (e) Development of offline capabilities for use in locations with no internet connectivity; (h) Connection between the GLMIS and other relevant Government databases or MISs that capture information on skills development and jobs, such as the Artisan Directory Platform and the Jobs Center of the Youth Employment Agency, and the Technical and Vocational Management Information System (TVMIS) of COTVET, and with private online job portals; To support overall labor market information collection and use, the Government will fully develop, operationalize, maintain, and use the GLMIS managed by MELR.

P167478-A1.text: integrated EMIS platform with mobile census and decision dashboards. The project builds a national school database fed by tablet and mobile census entry, linked MEN-A databases and web dashboards for decision-makers. Practices: Tablet-based annual school census data collection; Net-accessible dashboards for education decision-making; Integrated portal interlinking MEN-A databases with query functions; Mobile technologies for school-level data collection and quality control; Online information systems with data-driven decision triggers; Mobile-based education data collection with web dashboards; Unique identification codes for staff posts and teachers; Integrated MEN-A information systems built on EMIS databases; Tablet and smartphone real-time decentralized data collection; School-level education database feeding decision-maker dashboards; Mobile-technology school census data entry into national database; tablet and smartphone real-time school data collection; integrated EMIS platform interlinking MEN-A databases; tablet-based school census data entry; internet dashboards for education decision-makers; unique identifier codes for staff posts. While EMIS has been efficient at collecting annual data, the BSD has successfully piloted a more efficient data collection methodology using tablets which allows quicker collection and analysis of data while circumventing lengthy procedural steps at decentralized levels of MEN-A. Harnessing Technology for Effective Teaching, Learning and Systems Strengthening System Level • Tablets for annual school census data collection, entry, and quality control; and net-accessible dashboards for decision-making • Tablets and smartphone memory cards for central, prefectural- and sub-prefectural staff including school inspectors to coach/mentor School Directors and teachers for school-based teacher development School Level • Mobile cash for non salary budget subventions to schools • Tablets and smartphone memory cards for School Directors to support school-based teacher development; and to strengthen school management (planning, financial, reporting) Classroom Level • Tablets and smartphone memory cards with materials for professional development and curriculum delivery, to support school-based teacher development and strengthened play- and teaching- learning practices Page 19 of 86 The World Bank Guinea: Project for Results in Early Childhood and Basic Education (P167478) A. First, all databases generated by MEN-A will be interlinked through a common platform and integrated portal with upgraded reports generators, levels of disaggregation (covering also gender) and query functions. Second, the annual school-level data collection will be strengthened through the provision of mobile technologies enabling school-level data collection, entry and quality control; the revision of the data-collection format to eliminate unneeded fields and fill data gaps; and sample-based verification of data.
P167478-A1.name: integrated EMIS platform with mobile census and decision dashboards

P167478-A2.text: preloaded tablets for teacher coaching and school supervision. The project gives teachers, directors and inspectors tablets loaded with curriculum, professional development and supervision content, piloted before scaling. Practices: Tablets and memory cards for school-based teacher development; Tablet-based digital content platform for school-based teacher development; Piloted classroom tablets for teachers, directors and inspectors; tablets and smartphones as pedagogical support for teachers and inspectors; tablets for teachers and school directors with content; preloaded tablets for trained primary teachers. Harnessing Technology for Effective Teaching, Learning and Systems Strengthening System Level • Tablets for annual school census data collection, entry, and quality control; and net-accessible dashboards for decision-making • Tablets and smartphone memory cards for central, prefectural- and sub-prefectural staff including school inspectors to coach/mentor School Directors and teachers for school-based teacher development School Level • Mobile cash for non salary budget subventions to schools • Tablets and smartphone memory cards for School Directors to support school-based teacher development; and to strengthen school management (planning, financial, reporting) Classroom Level • Tablets and smartphone memory cards with materials for professional development and curriculum delivery, to support school-based teacher development and strengthened play- and teaching- learning practices Page 19 of 86 The World Bank Guinea: Project for Results in Early Childhood and Basic Education (P167478) A. The use of the content through digital technologies as a platform for school-based teacher development and strengthening play- and teaching-learning practices will be first piloted and evaluated in a limited number of schools, prior to the platform being scaled up. Content for the pre-primary and primary levels pertaining to in-service training, pedagogical support and the curriculum will be adapted for use through mobile technologies (e.g. tablets), which will be provided to pre-primary and primary teachers (including School Directors)25, as well as to pedagogical support staff at central, prefectural and sub-prefectural levels. In addition, this project will pilot and evaluate the use of tablets in the classroom (for teachers), school directors and school inspectors (in the school itself) for better support to teaching and learning and ultimately improved learning outcomes before taking the program to scale.
P167478-A2.name: preloaded tablets for teacher coaching and school supervision

P168052-A1.text: MIS with public subproject maps and citizen feedback. NSIFT builds an MIS for monitoring, auto-reporting, public map disclosure and citizen feedback. The component will also finance a management and information system (MIS), which NSIFT will establish and utilize for project monitoring, automatic generation of project reports, project transparency (subproject information will be publicized on maps), and citizen feedback. Feedback and grievances received through the BFM will be included in the semiannual reporting.
P168052-A1.name: MIS with public subproject maps and citizen feedback

P167884-A1.text: scaled ICT citizen engagement tools for participatory budgeting and feedback. Scales up PACV3-piloted tools: national call center with SMS feedback linked to EWRS, OpenSpending budget visualization, and smartphone geo-localized investment data collection. Practices: Scale-up of PACV3-piloted ICT citizen engagement tools: national call center with SMS feedback linked to EWRS, OpenSpending participatory budget visualization, smartphone-based geo-localized investment data collection; OpenSpending platform for participatory budgeting transparency. This sub-component will support scale-up and improvement of citizen engagement and EWRS activities that have been piloted under the PACV3, with strong emphasis on ICT. The sub- component will contribute to the scaling up and mainstreaming of participatory approaches tested under PACV3 by financing technical assistance, capacity building, and peer learning, with provision and adaptation of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) for improved efficiency and accessibility. The subcomponent will also facilitate dialogues with the key stakeholders for institutionalization and transparency of the GRM. o Participatory Budgeting and its data visualization for transparency: the PACV has piloted Participatory Budgeting in 132 LGs in rural Guinea.
P167884-A1.name: scaled ICT citizen engagement tools for participatory budgeting and feedback

P167884-A2.text: national call center, SMS feedback and geo-localized early warning system. Expands the call center for beneficiary surveys and SMS feedback, and scales the EWRS nationwide with real-time geo-localized risk indicators, trained monitors and grievance data. Practices: National call center and SMS platform for citizen feedback/GRM; Real-time geo-localized conflict risk monitoring and response system; Scaled-up EWRS with trained monitors and grievance data feeds; National call center with SMS platform for feedback and early warning. More specifically, the subcomponent will support: o Enhancement of the national-level call center and GRM: the PACV has set up a national-level call center since September 2018, where any citizen can call the dedicated number to provide feedback or to ask questions on the project activities. The project will expand the contract with the call center to strengthen its use, for: a) conducting beneficiary surveys on the project and on key basic services; b) incorporating a SMS platform for better accessibility and for closing the loop (linked to the linked to the EWRS). The project will build on the pilot which is being implemented by the PACV3 in 7 LGs30, refining it and expanding its coverage to the whole country in the course of the SLGP (cf. The EWRS will: (i) ensure real-time monitoring, geo-localization and analysis of specific indicators to monitor potential risk on a diverse range of local conflicts; and (ii) support response mechanisms that are adapted to identified risks31.
P167884-A2.name: national call center, SMS feedback and geo-localized early warning system

P167884-A3.text: smartphone GPS geo-localization of local investments and conflicts. Gives local agents smartphones and training to collect and publish geo-tagged investment data, with plans to map conflicts on the same platform. Practices: Smartphone GPS geo-localization of local investments with public disclosure; Smartphone-based geo-localized data collection by local agents; Geo-localized conflict mapping on infrastructure geo-localization platform. To better incorporate voices of the citizens gathered in the PM&E process, the project will facilitate dialogues and engagement between the LGs and their deconcentrated line ministry focal points on key basic services such as education and health. o Mobile-based data collection and geo-localization of the local-level investments: while the geo- localization of local-level small infrastructures with key management and operational data has already been launched under the PACV3 using GPS devices, the SLGP will provide smartphones and specific training to the ADLs and other key local stakeholders to collect and utilize the data more effectively. This activity aims to facilitate: a) accurate and speedy data collection and supervision of key services and infrastructures at the LG level; b) improved transparency of local- level investments of ANAFIC by disclosing the data on a publicly accessible website, and; c) informed decision-making and development planning for the LGs. b. Mobile-based data collection and geo-localization of the local-level investments: while the geo-localization of local-level small infrastructures with key management and operational data has already been launched under the PACV3 using GPS devices, the SLGP will provide smartphones and specific training to the ADLs and other key local stakeholders to collect and utilize the data more effectively. It is also planned to geo-localize conflicts, using the platform set up for the geo-localization of local-level small infrastructures.
P167884-A3.name: smartphone GPS geo-localization of local investments and conflicts

P168122-A1.text: CAPI, alternative collection methods and modelled welfare indicators for Pacific statistics. Uses CAPI, experimental survey methods, satellite and administrative data, crowdsourcing and phone follow-ups to modernize Pacific household survey data collection. Practices: CAPI replacing paper questionnaires in Pacific household surveys; Alternative data collection methods experimentation component; Harmonization Advisor to build regionally comparable micro-datasets; Harmonized welfare indicators populating Pacific Data Hub portal; Trials of alternative data collection methods with NSOs; Satellite and administrative data models for annual indicator estimates; Crowdsourcing and field enumeration for near real-time indicators; Resident enumerators with CAPI for remote citizenry monitoring; Long-form census module with small area estimation for HIES; Satellite imagery welfare estimation for Pacific islands; Cell-phone follow-up surveys of household survey respondents; Roving supervisors uploading resident enumerator data via sea links. In addition, integrating new technology, such as Computer-assisted Personal Interviewing (CAPI), reduces the need to print and transport paper questionnaires, which has decreased the costs of data collection in certain contexts despite the up-front cost of hardware investment. However, these issues are compounded by outdated methodologies and inefficient use of technology. The SPC project will provide US$4.4 million equivalent in grant financing to SPC-SDD across three components: (1) Support to the PSMB (US$1.13 million equivalent), (2) Institutional Strengthening and Implementation Support (US$1.70 million equivalent), and (3) Alternative Data Collection Methods (US$1.57 million equivalent). P167543-A1.text: digital payment and ERP infrastructure for rural financial services. Deploys one-stop digital centers, cooperative ERP payment systems and contactless merchant devices so rural users transact and pay digitally. Practices: one-stop digital centers for rural e-financial services and digital ID; ERP payment system for agriculture federations and cooperatives; contactless payment devices for rural merchants. Creation of digital centers network in rural areas - The creation of 150 digital centers which will be physical facilities for delivery of e- financial or digital services to rural populations. They will operate as multiple- services-one-stop-shops where remittances, cash-in cash-out and any other financial services, can be undertaken. This could include, for instance, assistance to rural populations in undertaking digital transactions on mobile phone and computer, financial and digital education programs, onboarding of merchants for digitization of their payments, power for mobile-charging, and digital ID registration of rural populations. Digitization of payments made to farmers - This will be done by financing the creation of an ERP solution and other payment infrastructure to enable five agriculture federations to manage the constituency of co-operatives and for the co-operatives in turn to manage the farmers under them.
P167543-A1.name: digital payment and ERP infrastructure for rural financial services

P167543-A2.text: merchant payment incentives and e-KYC for mobile money adoption. Uses vouchers, grants and e-KYC registry to expand merchant mobile money acceptance, with prospects for interoperability, transaction-based credit scoring and handset financing. Practices: vouchers for merchant digital payment device adoption; ERP upgrade and payment devices for agricultural input digitization; e-KYC registry for women's account access; mobile money acceptance grants for rural merchants; Mobile money interoperability and merchant acceptance expansion; mobile transaction traceability for women's credit scoring; Pay-as-you-go mobile-money handset financing pilot. Improving acceptance of digital payments by merchants - The project will provide vouchers to merchants, women groups (“tontines”) and micro-enterprises to cover up to 90 percent of the costs of the acquisition of payment devices in villages such as integrated contactless payment solutions. Preference will be given to merchants, women’s groups and micro-enterprises in the regions and communes around smart villages, without excluding other regions. This sub-component will comprise (i) digitizing payments made and received by farmers; and (ii) promoting new digital financial products for women and farmers. To accelerate digitizing payments made and received by farmers, the project will support: a.
P167543-A2.name: merchant payment incentives and e-KYC for mobile money adoption

P167543-A3.text: alternative-data credit scoring platform with e-KYC for rural producers. Builds a data platform and e-KYC registry aggregating farmer, wholesaler and mobile money data to score creditworthiness and design lending algorithms. Practices: Digital rural data platform with e-KYC registry for credit scoring; digital data platform for wholesaler credit scoring; farmer data center for creditworthiness assessment; Alternative-data credit scoring platform for unbanked producers; Alternative-data credit scoring using mobile money transactions; Credit-scoring algorithms designed for participating financial institutions; Digital financial literacy campaigns and consumer protection programs including related apps. To address the issue related to the scarcity of data and information on rural populations, and the high cost of due diligence and onboarding of rural populations, the project will support the creation of a digital data platform that will collect data on rural populations. The platform will serve two main purposes: including credit scoring, understanding 21 Based on World Bank experience on launching new Fintech products in Sub Saharan Countries. The digital platform will have two outlets: (i) data platform; and (ii) an e-KYC registry. The system would also link to a digital data platform that would capture information for credit scoring purpose for wholesalers.
P167543-A3.name: alternative-data credit scoring platform with e-KYC for rural producers

P167543-A4.text: central-bank-hosted shared e-KYC and credit-scoring platform. Hosts the rural data platform at BCEAO, run by a private e-KYC firm, with prospective linkage to the PASEC farmer registry. Practices: BCEAO-hosted shared rural data platform managed by private e-KYC firm; Interconnection of e-KYC platform with PASEC farmer registry. The digital data platform, to be hosted at the Banque Centrale des Etats de l’Afrique de l’Ouest (Central Bank of West African States, BCEAO) and managed by an independent private company, will be made accessible to financial institutions, existing credit bureau and other service providers, following an operations manual in accordance with the regional Central Bank (BCEAO) regulations and legal provisions governing data protection in Niger. The manager of the data platform shall be selected together by ANSI and the BCEAO, and it shall be a private entity specialized in e-KYC or credit scoring that has no conflict of interest and is fully trusted by lenders to be predictive, independent and reliable given its responsibility to ensure the quality and consistency of data collected. Activities to be financed under this sub-component will include data collection, creation of the platform, interfacing with key stakeholders and technical support for the operationalization of the platforms (see Annex 3) Box 2: The COVID-19 crisis calls for an urgent need to leverage technologies to deliver financial services The project will help Niger respond to the COVID-19 pandemic by accelerating the adoption of mobile payments, thereby reducing the dependence on paper cash, thought to be a powerful agent in the spread of the infection. WURI Regional Integration and Inclusion P161328 • Digital ID will in-turn be used for more secure opening of Program financial accounts in banks and microfinance institutions • Interconnection between the data platform (e- KYC registry and credit scoring) envisaged under Smart Villages and the 20,000 farmers already registered under PASEC will provide PASEC Climate Smart Agriculture Support for enhanced financial infrastructure systems.
P167543-A4.name: central-bank-hosted shared e-KYC and credit-scoring platform

P167543-A5.text: geospatial addressing, mapping and e-KYC data platforms for rural finance. Pilots digital addressing and geospatial data, maps ICT coverage and investment, and builds producer data platforms with e-KYC registries and self-service apps. Practices: Digital addressing systems piloted with financial institutions; Geospatial data to target financial services and cash transfers; ICT availability mapping of targeted rural villages; Integrated infrastructure, demand and investment mapping for digital services; geospatial data to optimize cash transfer delivery; Federation ERP linking cooperatives and farmer mobile app; Agricultural producer data platform with e-KYC registry; Data platform linked to WURI biometric unique ID; Digital data platform with credit scoring and e-KYC; Self-service mobile app for producers to update profiles; Centralized e-KYC registry cutting customer due diligence costs; Central bank-hosted digital KYC record repository for all clients; digital addressing and geospatial data for rural financial service delivery; SMS-issued KYC identification number for financial transactions. Conducting a study to assess the possibility to use digital addressing systems -- such as GEMS, Google plus codes or other solutions -- for populations in rural areas (who do not have formal addresses) and piloting this new system with selected financial institutions. There will also be an initiative to use geospatial data to optimize delivery of financial services and cash transfers during the recovery period of the COVID-19 crisis. Both will be piloted with selected financial institutions. Technical Assistance to map the ICT availability in the country, and more specifically in the targeted rural areas – The ICT mapping technical assistance will focus on gathering data related to the deployment of digital services in Niger and presenting them in a friendly manner to policy makers.
P167543-A5.name: geospatial addressing, mapping and e-KYC data platforms for rural finance

P167543-A6.text: rural digital service centers and agricultural ERP digitization. Sub-grants firms to run 150 rural multi-service digital centers and deploys off-the-shelf ERP at CAIMA to digitize input sales and payments. Practices: network of 150 rural multi-service digital centers; CAIMA ERP digitizing agricultural input value chain payments. Creation of digital centers network in rural areas – It is expected that the project will support the creation of 150 multi services digital centers by providing sub-grants for improvement of existing premises to house the centers, providing working capital (in the form of grants), training for the managers of the centers and helping to develop a business model that could allow the center to be sustainable even after the closing of the project. These centers will complement the existing mobile money agents in the targeted areas and will help fill the gaps while bringing additionality through more intensive support to customers. A competitive process through a call for proposals to be launched by the PIU will allow to select three companies that will have the responsibility to select and manage the centers, and the sub-grants they would receive. Digitization of payments received by the public agriculture input supplier, CAIMA or large input suppliers - Digitizing the agricultural value chain will involve digitizing the back-end processes at the CAIMA using an off-the-shelf ERP solution.
P167543-A6.name: rural digital service centers and agricultural ERP digitization

P168211-A1.text: AMI smart metering with automated data collection, billing and outage management. Two-way smart meters with automated meter data, CRM billing, remote disconnection and outage/complaint management cut losses and raise collection rates. Practices: smart-meter AMI with automated data collection and CRM billing; AMI smart metering with automated data collection and billing; AMI remote disconnection to raise collection rates; IRMS integrated into AMI for outage and complaint response. The AMI will comprise: (a) installation of smart meters (with 2-way remote communication); (b) meter data collection and management (with automated data collection); and (c) billing system (with structured customer accounts and billing procedure based on accurate measured data, including customer relationship management (CRM)). The AMI will comprise: a. Smart meters (with 2-way remote communication); b.
P168211-A1.name: AMI smart metering with automated data collection, billing and outage management

P168926-A1.text: geotagged mobile data and merged databases for health service verification. Uses Kobo Toolbox geotagged data, barcode scans and merged partner datasets linked to DHIS2 to verify health services and drug delivery. Practices: master health service functionality database with verified data; mobile geotagged data via Kobo Toolbox for third-party monitoring; Geotagged images and barcode scans verifying drug delivery; ICRC georeferenced data triangulation for hard-to-reach monitoring; Kobo Toolbox GPS-stamped monitoring of monitors (GEMS); Merged health service functionality database with analytic dashboard. Key monitoring elements will include: (a) Development of a master health service functionality database, capturing development and humanitarian health services across donors; (b) Collection and development of verified data within database to increase confidence in analysis and reported results and provide measures of partner data quality and reporting accuracy; (c) Generation of monthly health service functionality bulletin and implementing partner data performance reports; Innovative technologies such as use of mobile and geotagged data through the Kobo Toolbox platform will be applied to strengthen the quality and comprehensiveness of said third-party monitoring and verification mechanisms.
P168926-A1.name: geotagged mobile data and merged databases for health service verification
