P168613-A2.text: shared online platforms and GIS linking mining agencies, SMEs and land-use data. The project builds inter-agency IT and GIS platforms so ministries share cadastre and land-use data and SMEs reach mining procurement. Practices: Inter-agency IT hub linking mining, budget and related entities; Online platform linking SME/SMIs to mining company procurement; Shared inter-ministerial GIS pooling land-use and cadastre data. (iii) establishment of an IT hub allowing interconnection between the agencies within the MMG, the Ministry of Budget (MB) and other related entities; and (iv) establishment of a transparent procedure to share available geological and mining information with potential investors. This project will help increasing capacities of SME/SMIs to supply mining companies through the Online Platform for Local Content and complement ongoing support to local development by other World Bank projects (local development, and agribusiness). The start of a land-use planning process through the integration of land-use data (mining concessions, agriculture, transport and protected areas) and basic data (geology, ecosystems) must be undertaken to support cross-sectoral land allocation decisions and to resolve conflicts related to land use: a) Shared geographic information system (GIS) pooling sectoral data. The project will develop a GIS shared between the various ministerial departments involved in land use to enable compatible data exchanges between departments, especially MMG (with the mining cadaster) and MEEF (with protected areas and ESIA), but also, as feasible, with other departments – land-use planning ministry (with land titles), agriculture (with agro-industrial concessions and rural agriculture), transport (with roads, railway lines, port) and hydraulics and energy (with dams).
P168613-A2.name: shared online platforms and GIS linking mining agencies, SMEs and land-use data

P168613-A3.text: integrated environmental information, GIS and SMART patrol systems for protected areas. The project strengthens MEEF databases, GIS and SMART patrol tools to monitor protected areas, infrastructure projects and environmental assessments. Practices: Enhanced information system for protected areas and environmental management at MEEF, piloted in target protected areas; SMART patrol-based protected area management system; Expanded environmental and social assessment database mapping infrastructure projects; Joint online GIS unit for forests, land use and emissions monitoring; Electronic database and digital archive of projects subject to environmental assessment. This sub-component will support these needs by: (i) building foundations to support legal, institutional and logistic reform, logistical support including an OGPR and BGACE office building, complementing relevant regulatory reforms, developing a sustainable financing framework, enhancing the information system for protected areas and environmental management, strengthening capacity on climate change and supporting the initiation of a land-use planning process; (ii) improve the ESS MEEF applies; and (iii) provide the appropriate tools for improved management of the country’s protected areas network, and pilot them in target areas (see Annex 1 for details). Technical elements of the proposed project that help generate long-term benefits include the use of: (i) state-of-the-art technologies adapted to the Guinean context to improve mapping, information management and management of protected areas (e.g., innovative patrol-based techniques, SMART57); Modernization and generalization of Capacity of BGACE in National Analysis of the Annual BGACE the database of the environmental and identifying and mapping all database database social assessment database to all relevant ongoing or planned Page 57 of 89 The World Bank Guinea Natural Resources, Mining and Environment Project (P168613) projects infrastructure projects (dams, roads, railways, mines, etc.) to be environmentally and socially monitored Compilation of monthly a.
P168613-A3.name: integrated environmental information, GIS and SMART patrol systems for protected areas

P169718-A1.text: Digitized construction permitting system for development control. Project prepares development control tools including digitization of the manual construction permitting process. (c) prepare development control tools, including digitization of permitting systems; and (d) deliver targeted training to civil servants and appointed officials at the central and local government level with the possible inclusion of community-level organizations, which will ensure that female staff of the municipalities will benefit. Ultimately, the strengthening of urban development control systems and practices, using climate risk maps to inform no- build zones, paired with a public awareness campaign on climate risks also to be supported under the program, is anticipated to contribute to a reduction of citizens settling in high climate and flood-risk zones or ecologically sensitive areas, thereby reducing climate risk in the medium to long term.
P169718-A1.name: Digitized construction permitting system for development control

P169718-A2.text: drone aerial surveys producing terrain models for drainage design. Project uses drone surveys and orthophotos to build topographic maps and drainage models. Detailed aerial surveys of the Project area have already been conducted using drone survey techniques and resulted in high-resolution terrain models and orthophotos of the Greater Monrovia area. In Component 1, this information will enable the creation of detailed topographic maps and will feed into detailed models to be developed during the feasibility study phase to understand drainage systems.
P169718-A2.name: drone aerial surveys producing terrain models for drainage design

P169265-A1.text: satellite, big data and digital platforms for national statistics modernization. The project uses satellite imagery, call records, tablets, online portals and interoperable platforms to modernize how official statistics are collected, compiled and disseminated. Practices: satellite and call-record big data for welfare estimates; ECOBASE regional ACCESS database for harmonized macroeconomic statistics; satellite data and big data handbook for NSOs; labor statistics system with annual light telephone surveys; DSF pre-download for enterprise survey enumeration; Online DSF filing platform for enterprises; Education ministry data collection equipment and software; Tablet-based health district data collection scale-up; Tablet-based electronic data collection for agricultural surveys; Community-level weather data collection combined with household surveys; Satellite imagery and machine learning for poverty tracking; Mobile call record data to supplement official statistics; Online statistics portal with user-calculated summary statistics; Customized BOOST modules for macroeconomic and fiscal forecasting; Electronic budget and results data platform (BOOST-type) with administrative data; Interoperable data platform linking budget, results and administrative data; SDG indicator tracking platform as national repository; Cloud/web-based management information system for NSS; Phone-interview survey samples for public opinion polls; anonymized microdata publication by national statistics offices; online data access portal with user feedback; CAPI transition for household income and expenditure surveys; Regional data platform for archiving and open dissemination; Anonymized core datasets published for open access; satellite imagery and drones to update census/survey data; satellite and call-record poverty tracking. New sources of big data —especially data from satellites and call records from phone companies—that are increasingly available in Africa can complement traditional data sources in a number of ways. Combined with household survey data, they can be used to provide estimates of welfare that are disaggregated in space (e.g., poverty mapping) or time (e.g., SWIFT —Survey of Well-Being via Instant and Frequent Tracking) estimates of poverty between rounds of a household survey. They provide almost real-time data even in emergency situations, allowing for better understanding of how a situation is developing and better planning of responses. ECOWAS has designed a database in ACCESS known as ECOBASE to collect macroeconomic and finance statistics, including national accounts, CPI, public finance, and balance of payments.
P169265-A1.name: satellite, big data and digital platforms for national statistics modernization

P169265-A2.text: web portals for sharing development indicators and anonymized microdata. The project builds web portals that disseminate regional development indicators and share anonymized microdata online through platforms like the World Bank Microdata Catalogue and IPUMS. Practices: STATBASE web portal of regional development and policy indicators; Online anonymized microdata sharing on dissemination platforms. The project will also support ECOWAS in continuing an initiative that started (STATBASE) with the Economic Commission of Africa to create a web portal providing development and policy indicators. The project will also build on experiences from other regional projects on statistics, such as WAEMU in West Africa and the Programa para el Mejoramiento de las Encuestras de Hogares y la Medicion de Condiciones de Vida in Latin America and the Caribbean, to make core data collected under the regional project accessible on a regional platform. The project will engage other regional actors that maintain regional platforms, for instance the African Information Highway, which the African Development Bank maintains to disseminate agricultural statistics, avoid duplication, and consolidate efforts. To meet the demand for data from these groups, the project will support NSOs in building different types of products, including indicators and reports and their comprehensive metadata; sharing data widely on external data dissemination platforms, such as the World Bank Microdata Catalogue, UNData, and the Integrated Public Use Microdata Series; building an online interface to allow users to calculate their own summary statistics; and making available online anonymized microdata sets.
P169265-A2.name: web portals for sharing development indicators and anonymized microdata

P169267-A1.text: interoperable land information system with digital cadastre and geospatial data exchange. The project builds a standards-based, interoperable land information system with digital cadastral maps, georeferenced records and shared geospatial platforms for registration, valuation and public access. Practices: Digitally secured land rights and harmonized geospatial datasets; Interoperable geospatial data-exchange architecture across land and mining agencies; Geospatial integration platform supporting land-use decision-making; New Land Information System with cadastral base maps; Web-map geodata portal and GIS hub for territorial datasets; Digitization and georeferencing of cadastral maps and land registry records; LIDAR and orthophoto cadastral mapping for systematic registration; Integrated Land Information System with online land services; mass property valuation using cadastral geospatial data layer; Geospatial infrastructure and integrated decision support systems for territorial data; Digital cadastre linked to land registry for disaster recovery; Electronic integrated cadastral and registry services; Standards-based centralized Land Information System (LADM); Land information system with public web portal for cadastre data; integrated LIS with public web portal for cadastre access; Web-based cadastral and land information platform (SYCAD); Web-based land and real estate valuation platform (SIEBI); Fit-for-purpose incremental land information system. Digitally securing land rights and providing spatial planning tools including harmonized geospatial datasets and a property valuation system will also support the country in achieving its climate change adaptation and mitigation objectives. It will support the establishment of an architecture for common data interoperability and data exchange including the principles, standards, modularity, scalability, and autonomy useful between relevant land, mining and other sectors domains to reduce cost and enable digital links/exchange of new or existing data systems. (f) establish specific interoperability and data exchanges within ministries in charge of mines (Mining Cadastre, Bureau of Mines and Geology of Burkina Faso [Bureau des Mines et de la Géologie du Burkina Faso, BUMIGEB] and MEMC) and between key ministries involved with land and mining such as the Info-center located at the Directorate General for Taxation (Direction Générale des Impôts, DGI) at MINEFID to enable compliant mineral payments, or connection with MEEVCC regarding the exclusion of classified forests areas from mining licensing; (c) design a platform to integrate geospatial datasets to support decision-making;
P169267-A1.name: interoperable land information system with digital cadastre and geospatial data exchange

P169267-A2.text: online platform matching mining demand and local supply. The project establishes a web platform linking mining companies with local suppliers of goods and services, and monitors GBV and child presence at artisanal sites. Practices: Online platform matching mining goods and services demand and supply; Web-based platform monitoring GBV and child presence at ASM sites; Online platform for local procurement by mining companies. Improve national land and mining administration services (i) Time to register land certificates and titles reduced (days) (ii) Time to register urban occupancy certificates reduced (days) (iii) An online platform matching the demand and supply for goods and services is established (iv) Policy for making mining assets and anomalies discovered during geoscientific investigations accessible to prospective investors is approved B. (e) the establishment of a web-based monitoring platform to monitor GBV and children’s presence in ASM sites together with remediation support and advisory mechanisms including through partnerships with experienced local and international Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) in accordance with criteria and terms of reference (ToR) set forth in the PIM; If Burkina Faso is to succeed with economic integration of the mining sector, a number of developments are required: (a) the adoption of national policies for local content, establishment of an online platform to enable local purchase of goods and services by miners, and support to Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) for supplying miners with the standards required;
P169267-A2.name: online platform matching mining demand and local supply

P169267-A3.text: national geospatial data infrastructure with observatories and reference networks. The project strengthens territorial observatories and acquires LIDAR, drone and satellite imagery, completing a CORS geodetic network to improve national geospatial coverage. Practices: Territorial and urban observatories for local economic and urbanization data; LIDAR and drone orthophotos for national geospatial data; CORS geodetic reference station network for NSDI. (g) strengthen the National Observatory of Territorial Economy to facilitate the collection, sharing, and analysis of economic data at the local and regional levels; and (h) strengthen the National Urban Observatory to support the monitoring and evaluation of urbanization policies. Activities of this subcomponent will enable the collection, management and dissemination of land, mining and other common territorial datasets that will be key for planners and decision makers to enhance climate resilient planning, and for the academia and NGOs to monitor climate change and strengthen early warning systems. The acquisition of images will take into account the precision relevant for the objectives pursued and the adoption of LIDAR technology to produce orthophotos using drone technology for the capture of the information, as well as satellite images of Very High Resolution for covering larger surfaces and wider uses. These geospatial data will enable the development of geospatial information useful to many sectors of the economy.
P169267-A3.name: national geospatial data infrastructure with observatories and reference networks

P169267-A4.text: interoperable mining cadastre with prospectivity mapping and forest exclusion. The project modernizes the mining cadastre, embeds classified forest boundaries to block licensing, digitizes archives and models mineral prospectivity to formalize artisanal mining. Practices: Mining cadastre modernization with forest exclusion and data interoperability; Data-driven prospectivity mapping to formalize artisanal mining sites; Mine prospectivity mapping for green-economy minerals; forestry layers embedded in mining cadastre to exclude protected areas; Interoperable mining databases sharing data across agencies. 2.1.1 Mining Cadastre: This subcomponent will support the ongoing modernization of the mining cadastre and enable its financial sustainability to ensure the continuity of undertaken reforms through activities to: (a) restructure the cadastre to make it financially more sustainable; (d) support IT and connectivity requirements with other government systems, data interoperability, scanning and digitizing of historic physical concession reports and maps, archives and technical information compulsory for maintaining the mining licenses , etc.; and (e) train, equip, and provide tools to the staff in the mining cadastre. (b) exclude approximately 671,000 hectares of classified forests from mining licensing and incorporate other land uses in mining license systems to improve transparency and reduce potential conflicts and unlawful overlaps; This activity will support the MEMC and ANEEMAS in: (a) prospecting specific sites amenable to ASM to gradually drive an orderly, data-driven, and formalized approach to the activity;
P169267-A4.name: interoperable mining cadastre with prospectivity mapping and forest exclusion

P169267-A5.text: national spatial data infrastructure and multi-stakeholder geoportal. The project builds NSDI foundations with common geospatial standards and a geoportal giving multiple stakeholders access to interoperable land and mining data. Practices: Geoportal for multi-stakeholder access to land and geospatial data; National Spatial Data Infrastructure with common geospatial standards. (f) migrate existing data into the new LIS; and (g) develop a Geoportal to allow multiple stakeholders to access land and geospatial information. (e) deploy the LIS to selected offices connected to the RESINA network and develop training materials for the users; In parallel, the Government has started to lay the core foundations of a National Spatial Data Infrastructure (NSDI) in collaboration with the UN Global Geospatial Information Management. The adoption of a geospatial roadmap will help government agencies to agree on common data standards, mutualize investments in geospatial services and infrastructure, and eventually make land and mining information interoperable with other common territorial datasets for better natural resources and land use management, thereby enhancing the possibilities for a climate resilient development.
P169267-A5.name: national spatial data infrastructure and multi-stakeholder geoportal

P169267-A6.text: digital mining procurement marketplace and inter-ministerial data exchange. The project sets up online platforms matching mining demand with local suppliers and a web system sharing land, mining and forestry data across ministries. Practices: digital marketplace (BAL) matching mining demand and local supply; Online platform matching mining demand and supply (Bourse des Achats); Web-based data exchange system across land, mines, environment ministries; web-based data exchange system across land, mining, environment ministries; online platform listing local suppliers for mining procurement. (b) establish a bonded/customs warehouse for local content, a digital market place (Bourse des Achats Locaux, BAL), to match the demand and supply of goods and services to mining operations; Subcomponent 3.2: Local Content and Community Development (US$16 million) 3.2.1 Local Content: This subcomponent will support the implementation of the national strategy for the development and promotion of local supply of goods and services to mining operations through activities to: (a) support the operationalization of Burkina Faso's local content strategy at the national and mining districts levels; RESULTS FRAMEWORK AND MONITORING Results Framework COUNTRY: Burkina Faso Support to Land and Mining Management Strengthening Project Project Development Objectives(s) The Project Development Objective is to improve national land and mining administration services, register land rights in selected municipalities and foster inclusive benefits sharing from the mining sector Project Development Objective Indicators RESULT_FRAME_TBL_ PD O Indicator Name PBC Baseline End Target To improve national land and mining administration services Time to register land certificates and titles reduced (Days) 180.00 90.00 Time to register urban occupancy certificates reduced (Days) 14.00 6.00 Policy for making mining assets and anomalies discovered during geoscientific investigations accessible to prospective investors is No Yes approved (Yes/No) An online platform matching the demand and supply for goods No Yes and services is established (Yes/No) To register land rights in selected municipalities Titles and certificates of occupancy issued (Number) 0.00 329,500.00 Rural land possession certificates issued (Number) 0.00 25,000.00 Urban occupancy certificates issued (Number) 0.00 300,000.00 Page 52 (CRI, Number) Students benefiting from direct interventions to enhance 0.00 100.00 learning - P169698-A1.text: climate-resilient fiber broadband network design with network redundancy. Finances climate-smart digital infrastructure with redundancy to keep connectivity during disasters The Project will aim to build resilience through the design of digital infrastructure that can also be used in case of disaster response,46 by including special design provisions that ensure resilience in the case of natural disasters to minimize the risks of connectivity disruptions, e.g. by introducing network redundancy to improve reliability and ensure continuity of Internet services at times of natural disasters. It will finance digital infrastructure that is climate‐smart and supports climate change adaptation and climate resilience.
P169698-A1.name: climate-resilient fiber broadband network design with network redundancy

P169698-A2.text: open-access wholesale middle-mile broadband network for rural settlements. Finances construction of open-access middle-mile backhaul and points of presence so providers can reach unserved rural settlements. Practices: open-access wholesale middle-mile broadband network for rural settlements; open-access wholesale broadband network for rural settlements; public middle-mile open-access broadband network for rural settlements; open-access points of presence with IRU/leased backhaul. The Government’s ON Program will develop a national infrastructure to offer open access, wholesale broadband telecommunications services. This subcomponent will support construction and activation of high‐ capacity middle‐mile, backhaul networks under the ON Program that will bring high quality, high‐capacity services to selected rural settlements. SPs will then invest to expand their networks to provide services on commercial terms through their own last‐mile infrastructures, to the settlements’ households, enterprises, and organizations. The Project will support Georgia’s Open Net Program to develop national infrastructure to offer open access, wholesale, broadband‐telecommunications services.
P169698-A2.name: open-access wholesale middle-mile broadband network for rural settlements

P170466-A1.text: National forest monitoring system with satellite-based fire and invasive species detection. The project supports the existing NFMS for forest carbon tracking and considers satellite monitoring alongside fire towers for detecting fire and invasive species. Practices: Support for the existing National Forest Monitoring System (NFMS) for forest carbon tracking; Satellite-based monitoring for fire and invasive species. (e) Field vehicles for protected area operations; and (f) Support for the National Forest Monitoring System (NFMS) which was established with the support of the World Bank through the Forest Carbon Partnership Facility readiness mechanism (Uganda FCPF Readiness [P124296]). This will also include consideration of satellite-based monitoring systems. (d) Equipment and construction of fire towers for fire detection and suppression;
P170466-A1.name: National forest monitoring system with satellite-based fire and invasive species detection

P170658-A1.text: integrated 911 platform merging emergency and GBV hotlines. The project integrates firefighter, SAMU and Line 100 GBV hotline systems into one interoperable 911 platform with geolocation, outsourced operation and maintenance. Practices: Integrated 911 platform merging emergency and GBV hotlines; Line 100 digital system integrated into 911 Platform; 911-to-GBV Line 100 call transfer and tracking; private-sector outsourcing of 911 platform O&M; interoperable 911 communications system for multi-agency first response. The proposed project will seek to integrate the three key emergency response numbers mentioned above (NPP, PCVF, and SAMU) as they are the ones receiving approximately 90 percent of the calls and will progressively include the remaining emergency numbers as described in annex 2. The existing emergency response numbers (105, 106, and 116) will be phased out gradually, and all calls made to the First Response Units will be automatically transferred to the 911 system. Lines 100 and 911 will coexist, and all calls made to Line 100 will access the 911 system to benefit from receiving (a) alerts of previous malicious calls, (b) automatic information of previous emergency calls, and (c) the geolocation of calls. The following activities will improve the delivery of services offered by Line 100, as well as a more coordinated and efficient response in case of GBV emergencies or urgencies: (a) the integration of the Line 100 digital system to the 911 Platform, aiming at reducing malicious calls and response times;
P170658-A1.name: integrated 911 platform merging emergency and GBV hotlines

P170658-A2.text: interoperable 911 platform with geolocation, caller profiling and analytics. An open-standards 911 platform auto-geolocates calls, profiles and blacklists callers, links SAMU and early-warning systems, and analyzes call data for planning. Practices: Linking SISMATE early-warning messaging to the 911 system; Automatic geolocation of 911 emergency calls; 911 Platform with automatic geolocation and caller profiling; Data analytics for emergency risk mapping and planning; interoperability between SAMU first-response systems and 911 Platform; 911 Platform built on open standards for replicability; Interoperable integrated 911 platform with automatic call geolocation; Data analytics tool measuring 911 operator response times; Data analytic system generating 911 call reports; Blacklist of malicious callers built from 911/Line 100 data; Interoperable integrated platform linking 911, Line 100, First Response Units; automatic geolocation of 911 emergency calls; automatic geolocation and caller data lookup for 911 emergency calls; interconnection sending geolocated GBV call data to Line 100 specialists; integrated emergency platform linking 911 and Line 100 operators. This will be done by (a) establishing an integrated communications platform, (b) adopting specific and well-coordinated emergency response protocols and procedures, (c) promoting the linking of the recently implemented Early Warning Messaging System ( Sistema de Mensajería de Alerta Temprana de Emergencia, SISMATE) with the 911 system, and (d) providing much-needed capacity building. It will include a geolocation system that will allow automatic geolocation of calls received by the 911 Center. The 911 Platform will receive, categorize, transfer, and perform the traceability of the calls that are sent to the First Response Units. In addition, the platform will, at minimum, automatically (a) geolocate the call;
P170658-A2.name: interoperable 911 platform with geolocation, caller profiling and analytics

P170658-A3.text: interoperability protocols and digital integration linking 911 to first responders. Cooperation agreements and shared protocols connect the 911 platform with Line 100 and first-responder systems for alerts, geolocation and analytics access. Practices: Digital integration of GBV Line 100 with 911 Platform; interoperability protocols linking 911 platform to first responders. In addition, this component will improve the efficiency of the response of GBV Line 100, through the digital integration of the Line 100 system with the 911 Platform. Line 100 will benefit from accessing the 911 Platform by receiving (a) alerts of previous malicious calls, (b) information of previous emergency calls, (c) the geolocation of calls, and (d) access to the data analytics tool. Agreement signed. interoperability between the 911 integrated platform and the systems used by the First Response Units and Line 100, and defining and implementing capacity building activities. Cooperation Agreement signed signed and in accordance to the aims at facilitating at Annual PRONATEL between PRONATEL, the NPP, SAMU, copies sent number signatories of minimum the development PCVF, and Line 100 to the World Cooperation of the protocols, Bank team.
P170658-A3.name: interoperability protocols and digital integration linking 911 to first responders

P170664-A1.text: ICT-based third-party monitoring with geo-enabled integrated M&E system. Project mainstreams third-party monitoring using ICT and geo-enabling technology to verify implementation in hard-to-reach conflict areas To this end, the project will mainstream the use of third-party monitoring including information and communications technology (ICT). Geo-enabling technology will also be used to help enhance accountability and transparency and systematize the analysis of collected field data in an integrated M&E system. Implementation measures have been adapted to accommodate these settings, including for example, the use of third-party monitoring and implementation in hard-to-reach areas.
P170664-A1.name: ICT-based third-party monitoring with geo-enabled integrated M&E system

P170664-A2.text: remote learning platform with digital literacy and mentoring for secondary students. The project uses an online/offline learning platform, LMS, tablets and mobile mentoring to deliver digital literacy and curriculum content to secondary students, especially girls. Practices: Remote learning platform with digital literacy training for secondary students; tablet-based digital literacy training for adolescent girls; offline/online remote learning platform with radio-TV lessons; learning management system with downloadable offline curriculum content; mobile text, chatline and app mentoring for girls; Blended digital literacy training for secondary school students; Offline-and-online remote learning platform with radio/TV lessons; LMS with downloadable offline digital curriculum content. Digital Literacy Training and Remote Learning Platform (US$20 million equivalent) 56. The objective of this activity is to support the provision of basic digital literacy training and to establish a remote learning platform for secondary school students. Specifically, digital literacy training will equip students with digital literacy skills and knowledge that includes: (a) using digital mobile devices; Training will be provided on electronic tablets with relevant applications and an internet connection.
P170664-A2.name: remote learning platform with digital literacy and mentoring for secondary students

P170419-A1.text: AI, satellite and Big Data agricultural advisory and monitoring systems. The project builds digital advisory, data-center and AI platforms using satellite, drone and IoT data to guide farmers and monitor crops, pests and soils. Practices: e-conseil agricole digital agricultural advisory service (ONCA); Pilot call for AI-based precision-agriculture digital platforms; National agricultural advisory data center with regional relays; AI precision-agriculture platform with drone/satellite imagery; Machine-learning satellite crop-area estimation system; Machine-learning plant disease detection from images; E-advisory services with weather and pest alerts; Satellite imagery monitoring of soil regeneration; AI and drone/satellite precision agriculture platform; national Big Data agricultural advisory system with regional relays; tablets and ARDNA platform for agricultural advisors; AI and drone/satellite crop monitoring platform; machine-learning crop area estimation from satellite time series; machine-learning image detection of plant diseases; pest risk forecasting and mapping information system; Big Data and AI/ML analytics on satellite imagery for climate adaptation; Integrated online GIS-based data administration and M&E system; AI-based precision agriculture digital platform; Machine-learning satellite time-series crop area estimation; Image-based machine-learning plant disease detection; Drones for phytosanitary crop treatment; National agricultural advisory Data Center with regional relays; Big-Data platform consolidating existing INRA agricultural databases; IoT kits for irrigation and livestock management. Toutefois, les activités de l’opération aborderont aussi indirectement l’Axe stratégique B (Renforcement du capital humain), étant donné que le Programme vise à développer, renforcer et protéger le capital humain en élargissant les programmes universitaires et en développant les services de e-conseil agricole. Cela impliquerait : (i) la création d’un Data Center national de données de conseil agricole avec des relais régionaux - devant, entre autres, acquérir, stocker et traiter un grand volume de données provenant des exploitations agricoles (collectées à travers des technologies digitales telles que les satellites, les drones et l’Internet des objets [IdO]) - et la fourniture ultérieurement de conseils adaptés et facilement exploitables par les exploitants agricoles en les adaptant en particulier aux besoins des femmes ;

P170419-A2.text: E-commerce platform for small producers' terroir products. The project finances an online e-commerce platform with virtual stores letting smallholders, cooperatives and producer organizations sell local products directly to consumers. Practices: E-commerce platform for small producers' terroir products; e-commerce platform for small cooperatives' local products; e-commerce platform for 300 producer organizations; E-commerce platform for marketing terroir products. (ii) aménagement de quatre marchés de gros : cela inclurait le financement des études techniques et de faisabilité financière, la construction des infrastructures adaptées au changement climatique et écoénergétiques, les équipements, et l’opérationnalisation complète des infrastructures commerciales pour les villes de Meknès, Agadir, Marrakech et Berkane ; les activités préalables consisteraient à mettre en place un nouveau modèle de gestion des marchés de gros, s’appuyant sur des partenariats territoriaux avec les communes concernées et les administrations régionales, à travers la mise en place des Modes de gestion pour les marchés de gros modernisés, et à préparer une Etude d’impact environnemental et social (EIES) du Schéma National d’Orientation des Marchés de Gros au Maroc (version 2018) ainsi que pour chaque marché de gros sélectionné ; la Direction du Développement des Filières de Production (DDFP) superviserait le processus avec l’ensemble des institutions concernées, notamment les Wilayas et les autres collectivités territoriales ; et (iii) développement d’une plateforme d’e-commerce pour les produits de terroirs : cette activité appuierait les petits producteurs agricoles, en particulier les femmes, et leurs coopératives dans la commercialisation de leurs produits à travers un large éventail de magasins virtuels; faciliterait leur intégration aux chaînes de valeur commerciales. Ce sous-programme porte sur la construction de quatre nouvelles plateformes pour la commercialisation des produits agricoles et agroalimentaires résistantes au climat et écoénergétiques et la mise en place d’une plateforme d’e-commerce dédiée aux produits de terroirs. La plateforme d’e-commerce répondrait aux besoins des petites coopératives agricoles de produits de terroirs de différentes régions du Royaume.
P170419-A2.name: E-commerce platform for small producers' terroir products

P170419-A3.text: Open agricultural data-sharing platform for stakeholders. The project supports an open, secure web platform giving startups, researchers and public and private actors validated national agricultural data. Practices: Open, secure agricultural data-sharing platform; open agricultural data platform for startups; open agricultural data platform shared with research, academia, private sector. Parmi les actions prioritaires figurent l’élaboration d’une plateforme de données solide capable de fournir des données validées aux différentes parties prenantes. Cette plateforme devrait être ouverte, sécurisée et protégée. A cette fin, le MAPMDREF peut tirer parti de la collaboration avec l’Agence du Développement du Digital (ADD), mandatée pour diriger l’Initiative de Données Ouvertes du Gouvernement. Cette plateforme devrait offrir un accès ouvert aux différentes parties prenantes et fournir des données aux startups pour développer des solutions digitales locales.
P170419-A3.name: Open agricultural data-sharing platform for stakeholders

P171160-A1.text: satellite imagery, CAPI and machine learning for survey sampling and data quality. Uses satellite imagery, IDP registries and tracking data to build sampling frames, CAPI with GPS for fieldwork, and ML to impute missing consumption data. Practices: Satellite-image sampling frame covering nomadic and IDP populations; M&E dashboard for monitoring NDP9 indicators; Dashboard comparing public program efficacy by NDP9 pillar; Central Business Register compiled from administrative records; governmental M&E dashboard with server and reporting software; CAPI with real-time data monitoring to catch enumerator errors; Satellite-imagery-updated rural sampling frame replacing census; Satellite imagery and IDP registries to build IDP sampling frame; Survey tracking data to construct nomadic sampling frame; Machine-learning imputation of unreported household consumption items; CAPI with GPS tracking and server upload for survey supervision; NADA microdata cataloguing and anonymization tool; Rapid high-frequency monitoring system for near real-time policy data. As such, the SIHBS will make use of an updated sampling frame created from satellite image that will include rural, urban, nomadic and IDP populations. The sample will also feature nomads and IDP households located in the above geographic areas. To achieve this objective, the project will concentrate efforts in i) improvements to the M&E toolkit, ii) developing a dashboard for enhanced monitoring capabilities, and ii) providing specialized training to relevant stakeholders. The NDP9 envisages that the national M&E system will be built around a periodic reporting system based on indicators at the output and outcome levels.

Delivers business, start-up and non-cognitive skills training and coaching at scale via WhatsApp. Business and start-up training and coaching of workers, including non- cognitive skills especially for women entrepreneurs through WhatsApp at scale, will be provided to ensure that communities benefit from the new investment.

P171607-A2.text: Digital marketplace platform enrolling MSMEs for business development services. Sets up online platform where MSMEs enroll and receive training, coaching from vetted providers This MDTF component will set up a digital platform where MSMEs can enroll and receive business development services (i.e. training and coaching). The digital platform will represent a dynamic marketplace for accelerators, incubators and consultancies – eligible service providers will be vetted and selected based on a competitive tender – and will lay the foundation for an improved business development environment for MSMEs, increasing their ability to take advantage of growing markets in manufacturing and export supply chains. Access to the platform will be granted to firms that meet a set of eligibility criteria (will not required formalization) and will specifically target female-owned enterprises and MSMEs that employ refugees.
P171607-A2.name: Digital marketplace platform enrolling MSMEs for business development services

P171793-A1.text: satellite, smartphone and geo-enabled platforms for remote road supervision. Uses satellite imagery, smartphone roughness surveys, GEMS geo-location and RSSAT screening to supervise and design road works remotely. Practices: satellite imagery and smartphone road-condition data for remote supervision; GEMS geo-enabled monitoring and supervision platform; Road Safety Screening and Appraisal Tool for road design. Due to the large project area, the volatile security situation in the Sahelian strip, and the impact of COVID-19, the project will rely on a variety of smart approaches leveraging digital technologies to facilitate the implementation of project activities, consultation process, as well as enhance monitoring and evaluation. The activities will include, but are not limited to: (a) direct remote monitoring using satellite imagery; (b) use of smartphones for road data collection (such as road roughness before and after the civil works); (c) mobile-based iterative beneficiary monitoring mechanisms; and (d) geo-enabling initiative for monitoring and supervision (GEMS).

P171886-A1.text: core banking, supervision and registry IT modernization. The project upgrades DAB's core banking and supervision systems, collateral and credit registries, and deposit insurance payout software to strengthen oversight and financial intermediation. Practices: New core banking system and automated banking supervision at DAB; IT modernization of collateral registry and public credit registry; MIS for insured deposit payout operations; Core banking system modernization for central bank oversight; IT modernization of collateral and public credit registries; Single Customer View depositor data and payout software for deposit insurance; credit registry expansion to utility and telecom payment data. Specifically, DAB plans to install a new core banking system (CBS),and automate relevant aspects of banking supervision, thus strengthening its overall operational and oversight capacity. Further measures aimed at strengthening banking system oversight include upgrades in DAB’s IT infrastructure and capacity building of DAB’s technical directorates. DAB has established a collateral registry (CR) for movable property in 2013 followed by public credit registry (PCR) in 2014 and both systems are due for information technology (IT) upgrade. 6 The World Bank Strengthening Afghanistan’s Financial Intermediation (P171886) enables lenders to effectively use borrowers’ movable property as collateral, and credit information provided by the PCR is a primary factor in evaluating the creditworthiness of banks clients and mitigating credit risk; thus, both registries are essential for facilitating access to finance.
P171886-A1.name: core banking, supervision and registry IT modernization

P172348-A1.text: geocoded data portal linked to beneficiary feedback mechanism. An online peacebuilding and recovery data portal combines geocoded mobile photos, spatial data and a grievance feedback mechanism to track infrastructure progress and civic engagement. Practices: geocoded Data Portal on Peacebuilding and Recovery; online Data Portal on Peacebuilding and Recovery linked to feedback mechanism. The BFM will include options for entering beneficiary data into the MRTOT-housed Data Portal on Peacebuilding and Recovery (https://portal.mtot.gov.ua/), a web-based platform that can include geocoded photographic data from local communities (e.g. submitted from mobile phones) and spatial data to track progress on transport- and agriculture-related infrastructure. (g) A 3R Project beneficiary feedback mechanism (BFM), including a GRM will be established by MRTOT to collect, manage, and respond to feedback related to the 3R Project. Under Component 3, a well-advertised BFM (including a GRM), linked to MRTOT’s online Data Portal on Peacebuilding and Recovery, will be established to collect and respond to complaints and other feedback. Based on the evolving COVID-19 situation, proposed citizen engagement activities will also blend traditional and civic technology through the Data Portal; and utilize virtual formats for engagement.
P172348-A1.name: geocoded data portal linked to beneficiary feedback mechanism

P172226-A2.text: TReDS digital factoring platform for MSME receivables financing. Uses the TReDS electronic platform, interoperable with GSTN and CERSAI, so MSMEs discount invoices and gain liquidity. Practices: digital factoring platform (TReDS) for MSME receivables financing; green tag tracking of greening investments in CGTMSE guarantees; TReDS inter-operability with CERSAI for receivables financing; TReDS invoice marketplace for MSME receivables discounting; TReDS digital factoring platform for MSME receivables; GST invoice verification integrated with TReDS platform; GSTN-TReDS interoperability for input tax credit verification; TReDS electronic platform for MSME invoice receivables financing; TReDS platform using buyer creditworthiness for MSME liquidity. (ii) improved access to finance for women entrepreneurs and greening investments; and (iii) improved access to finance and working capital of MSMEs through (a) well-functioning digital factoring platforms; and (b) strengthened markets for online dispute resolution (ODR) and private sector provision of these services. (ii) Supporting access to finance for MSMEs targeting women-owned/women-headed MSMEs and for greening investments, including operationalizing the ‘green tag’ to track greening investments, expanding CGTMSE’s product offerings and enabling improvements in data and M&E systems. This will be complemented with awareness programs to foster demand for these services • Trade Receivables Discounting System – an “alternative” collateral solution: This is an invoice marketplace for discounting and factoring of payables that provides an alternative to traditional collateral requirements that can inhibit MSME access to finance. Fintech platforms such as the TReDS are digitizing the factoring process, reducing costs and improving efficiency, including the collection of repayments from third parties.
P172226-A2.name: TReDS digital factoring platform for MSME receivables financing

P172226-A3.text: Samadhaan portal online dispute resolution for delayed payments. Embeds ODR in the Samadhaan portal, linking private providers, mediators and case dashboards to resolve MSME payment disputes. Practices: online dispute resolution via Samadhaan portal for delayed payments; ODR integration with Samadhaan portal plus voucher uptake program; ODR integrated into Samadhaan portal for MSME dispute resolution; Samadhan ODR portal for delayed-payment case resolution; Samadhaan portal linking MSMEs to online dispute resolution providers; State portal integration with unified national portal and automatic scheme referrals; Samadhaan portal routing delayed-payment cases to ODR platforms; Samadhaan portal online dispute resolution for delayed payments; Integration of state portals with unified national MSME portal; Champions Portal interoperability integrating MSME service portals; INMDP one-stop MSME portal with service-provider rating system; Unified program management system tracking firms across schemes; ODR platform embedded in Samadhaan portal with private providers; Case-monitoring dashboard and ODR provider guidelines; Automatic conversion of mediation settlements to conciliation consent awards; Standardized dispute resolution clause for ODR platform use; Samadhaan portal online dispute resolution with private ODR providers; Samadhaan portal linking ODR providers, mediators and arbitrators; Samadhaan portal roster of certified mediators/arbitrators; web-based complaint handling mechanism with procurement/FM interface. (ii) improved access to finance for women entrepreneurs and greening investments; and (iii) improved access to finance and working capital of MSMEs through (a) well-functioning digital factoring platforms; and (b) strengthened markets for online dispute resolution (ODR) and private sector provision of these services. (ii) Supporting access to finance for MSMEs targeting women-owned/women-headed MSMEs and for greening investments, including operationalizing the ‘green tag’ to track greening investments, expanding CGTMSE’s product offerings and enabling improvements in data and M&E systems. (v) integration of ODR into the Samadhaan portal and training requirements for service providers. P172492-A1.text: Integrated digital financial, M&E and GIS data platforms for local councils. The project builds web-based financial, M&E and GIS platforms so councils and ministries share real-time budget, project and service-delivery data. Practices: web-based PETRA/PFM Smart financial management system for LCs; automated project database for council public investment programme; Audit Management Information System for local government audits; NaMEMIS integrated M&E data platform linking MDAs, LCs, NGOs; GIS-enabled web portal for LC data posting and central feedback; Automated data platforms for education and health supply inputs; Digitized SOPs and M&E data-flow systems across national, district, community levels; Online/offline data platforms for last-mile commodity distribution tracking; Real-time GIS-tagged service delivery dashboards with citizen input; GEMS field-appropriate digital data collection for M&E; NaMED data platform for monthly local council reporting of textbook, TLM and drug distribution; NaMED/NaMEMIS data platform with web/phone feedback portal for registered users; NaMED platform for monthly textbook and drug distribution reporting; NaMED web/phone portal for user feedback on service data; Live web-based LC financial system for real-time expenditure tracking; Geo-enabled Monitoring and Supervision (GEMS) for beneficiary surveys. (ii) strengthened record management system; and iii) enhanced monitoring and support from central level. • Delivering enhanced, timely, and more transparent LC financial reporting through an updated chart of accounts adapted to LC needs, and the implementation of an upgraded FM system (web-based PETRA/PFM Smart). This sub‐component will focus on strengthening key PFM functions to support basic service delivery , including through improved tools, procedures, and skills building for central- and local-level staff. Project would finance the development of guidelines, templates and related guidance for the preparation of the PIP, the implementation of an automated project database for Councils, and initiatives to promote and facilitate the participation of private sector in public investment and capital projects across all councils. Strengthening ASSL's capacity to undertake timely audits of all local government financial statements through the implementation of an Audit Management Information System (AMIS) and enhance capacity of the IT unit within ASSL to support a more efficient audit process.
P172492-A1.name: Integrated digital financial, M&E and GIS data platforms for local councils

P172492-A2.text: e-Procurement, GEMS monitoring and linked data platforms for accountability. The project rolls out e-GP, open contracting and GEMS feedback tools and links council and ministry platforms to NaMEMIS for two-way data flows. Practices: e-Government Procurement rollout in health and education; e-Procurement and open contracting with supplier database; Linking local and MDA data platforms to umbrella NaMEMIS; e-Procurement system roll-out for health and education; GEMS system for subproject monitoring and citizen feedback; GEMS platform collecting citizen feedback on local investments; e-GP procurement transactions tracked in health and education; E-procurement and framework contracts for council procurement. 12 The overall sub- component objective is to increase the transparency and accountability in government procurement system through the implementation of e-Procurement (e-GP), with the focus of the project delivering results in the key priority sectors of education (textbooks, teaching and learning material - TLM) and health (drugs, medical supplies and equipment). The project-supported activities will be part of the wider e-GP roll out strategy of the NPPA for the strengthening of procurement systems reforms in all ministries, departments, and agencies (MDAs). The sub-component activities will be aimed towards mainstreaming of e-Procurement and open contracting and its operationalization in the education and health sectors through an increased number of procurement transactions using the e-GP system. Key activities would include: • The preparation and implementation of an action plan, including change management, roll-out, and adoption of e-Procurement in the health and education sectors. • E-GP tender process completed and operationalization of the e-Procurement system. • Transitioning existing manual procurement processes (e.g., increased training of procurement practitioners – controllers and suppliers) – developing the supplier database. • E-Procurement training and capacity building of relevant stakeholders in the education and health sectors. • Implementation of e-Procurement awareness and sensitization. • Change management support, including staffing of the e-Procurement Directorate in the NPPA.
P172492-A2.name: e-Procurement, GEMS monitoring and linked data platforms for accountability

P172535-A2.text: Spatial vulnerability targeting and social registry subsidy migration. The project applies spatial tools to the Housing Vulnerability Index for block-level targeting and uses SISBEN registry eligibility to target subsidies, including migrants. Practices: Housing Vulnerability Index spatial micro-targeting of beneficiaries; Migration of housing subsidies onto SISBEN social registry targeting. The HVI will further support municipalities in the process of beneficiary targeting through the application of spatial analytical tools to enable micro-targeting of vulnerable populations within each selected neighborhood at the block level. The migration of both the home improvement and rental subsidy programs to the SISBEN social registry system, as such, reinforces an important GoC strategic focus on efficiency of targeting social assistance. The inclusion of SISBEN as part of the criteria for eligibility is critical to encourage a continued mainstreaming of migrants from Venezuela into the social registry and assistance system. Housing programs use parallel systems and are transitioning to SISBEN.
P172535-A2.name: Spatial vulnerability targeting and social registry subsidy migration

P173757-A1.text: epidemiological surveillance and emergency operations intelligence system. The project uses upgraded surveillance and emergency operations center systems to detect COVID-19 cases, trace contacts, screen points of entry and speed response. Practices: COVID-19 surveillance system with active case detection, contact tracing and point-of-entry screening; Public Health Emergency Operations Center epidemiology intelligence system upgrade. Surveillance activities will include: (a) activating the COVID-19 surveillance system; (b) implementing active case identification and contact tracing; and (c) implementing screening at Points of Entry (i.e. IHR- designated air, land and sea ports). Specifically, support will be provided to the following activities: (a) EOC: Support for expanding the scope and improving the functionality of the Public Health EOC, including, inter alia, upgrading the system for epidemiology intelligence, information gathering and use, and rapid response, improving risk communication and community engagement, and capacity building of DGHS including IEDCR.
P173757-A1.name: epidemiological surveillance and emergency operations intelligence system

P173450-A1.text:
digital data collection and integrated processing across statistical operations. Deploys online, tablet, CAPI and electronic collection plus integrated processing software and open SDG publication to modernize surveys and censuses. Practices: Multi-modal business census via online forms and tablet enumeration; CAPI tablet-based Household Budget Survey with quarterly regional sample; Integrated mahalla summary database linked to social register; Electronic continuous consumer and producer price data collection; Agricultural production monitoring system with census-based sampling frame; Integrated data processing system covering full survey cycle; Mahalla-level digital cartographic data for census; Open-data publication of national SDG indicators on stat.uz. The project will support preparations (but not
implementation) for the SCS’ planned first national business census during the period 2024-5 The business census is
expected to include details on business activities, geocoded location, number of employed (disaggregated by sex and
hours of work), earnings, and ownership. The business census will be multi-modal, collecting data through i) online forms,
or ii) direct enumeration (tablet based). The project will finance the preparation of questionnaires, training, data
processing, and publication of results. First, this subcomponent will finance a comprehensive modernization of the Household Budget Survey (HBS).
P173450-A1.name: digital data collection and integrated processing across statistical operations

P173450-A2.text:
open anonymized microdata access for authorized users. Publishes anonymized survey datasets through an open micro-data library and access policies on the statistics website. Practices: Public anonymized survey datasets for authorized users; Open micro-data library on stats.uz website; Open access policy for anonymized microdata. The project financing will enable the SCS to make the anonymized datasets publicly
available to authorized users. The SCS will also publish the statistical analysis of the data on the official stat.uz website,
complete with gender- and geographical-specific statistics for key indicators. Dissemination practices will be improved by collecting user feedback, supporting open data access, implementing an
open micro-data library, and producing analytical reports, and ensuring compliance with the SDDS. Finally, open access policies for anonymized microdata will be adopted.
P173450-A2.name: open anonymized microdata access for authorized users

                relevant actions taken.
P173450-A3.name: online citizen feedback and public report cards

P173916-A1.text: MojTermin COVID-19 screening, monitoring and contact-tracing modules. Adds COVID-19 screening, home-treatment monitoring and contact-tracing modules to the national MojTermin e-health system, linking primary care for real-time reporting. Practices: MojTermin COVID-19 screening and home-treatment monitoring module; MojTermin surveillance and contact-tracing modules linked to primary care. To facilitate protective measures against COVID-19 by physicians and patients in need of health care, as well as easy recording and analysis of data on patients with COVID-19, the MojTermin team in the Ministry of Health (MoH) has developed a new module, consisting of a COVID-19 screening submodule and submodule for monitoring home-treatment patients with COVID-19. In addition, data are entered in MojTermin for COVID-19 patients as for patients with any other condition (all checkups, results from diagnostic examinations, medication, etc.), creating a unique resource for monitoring and analyzing data on COVID-19 patients once the system is rolled out countrywide. It will facilitate combining the detection of new cases with active contact tracing, by enhancing the surveillance and contact tracing modules of the health system’s current information system (MojTermin) and linking primary care providers to it. Finally, it will help provide on-time and real-time data and information to guide decision-making and response and mitigation activities, by enhancing systems and protocols and building capacity for data reporting, data analysis, and information dissemination.
P173916-A1.name: MojTermin COVID-19 screening, monitoring and contact-tracing modules

P173916-A2.text: Interoperable CBMIS platform for registration, surveys and benefit applications. Uses the interoperable CBMIS beneficiary platform for online and phone registration, repeated phone surveys and a new Employment Agency unemployment benefit application module. Practices: CBMIS-based phone surveys of social assistance beneficiaries; Online and phone registration via interoperable CBMIS platform; New Employment Agency application module for unemployment benefits. Using the beneficiary information from the Cash Benefits Management Information System (CBMIS), the project will conduct several rounds of phone surveys of social assistance beneficiaries to assess the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on vulnerable households and on their needs. Additionally, the project may facilitate citizen engagement activities using the same tool. Registration and intake for new beneficiaries of the temporary cash assistance will be conducted online, by phone, and in the 30 CSWs and 50 offices located primarily in rural areas (while applying social distancing procedures). All the necessary documents for benefit application are available electronically through the interoperable CBMIS platform.
P173916-A2.name: Interoperable CBMIS platform for registration, surveys and benefit applications

P173916-A3.text: online platform for community feedback and grievance redress. Project builds an online platform to collect community feedback and grievances during social distancing To ensure that communities are engaged while social distancing policies are being implemented, the component will support the development of an online platform for all stages of community feedback. In addition, the project will implement a feedback mechanism on the COVID-19 response (temporary cash and in-kind benefits and health activities), to ensure communities can provide just-in-time-feedback to government to ensure that investments respond to local needs and reach vulnerable groups. This will also include a community-based monitoring mechanism and a grievance redress mechanism.
P173916-A3.name: online platform for community feedback and grievance redress

P174067-A1.text: iGOT Karmayogi online learning platform with competency-based pathways. The project builds a modular, India Stack-interoperable online platform that delivers competency-based training, algorithmic learning paths and passbooks to all civil servants. Practices: SPV-owned online learning platform with content marketplace; Integrated open-source online platform for all civil servants; Any-device online training platform for civil servants; iGOT Karmayogi digital training platform with competency scores; Algorithmic learning-path generation from competency gaps; iGOT Karmayogi platform as civil-service learning management backbone; API-driven modular cloud platform interoperable with India Stack; Encoded competency frameworks driving telemetry-based learning pathways; platform tracking of staff learning and training effort; competency passbooks on iGOT platform; iGOT Karmayogi platform competency testing and scoring. A special purpose vehicle (SPV) has been established to own and operate an online learning platform and facilitate a world-class learning content marketplace. This innovative program envisages a comprehensive reform of the framework and incentives for capacity building both at the institutional and individual levels for efficient public service delivery. At the same time, the process democratizes training by developing a comprehensive online platform that can be accessed by all civil servants to support and widen the scope and content of training and capacity development. An integrated, online platform with open-source training modules will provide the necessary framework to allow civil servants to emerge out of narrow ministerial, departmental, and cadre-focused training and develop skills that could make them into more fungible and agile resources across government.
P174067-A1.name: iGOT Karmayogi online learning platform with competency-based pathways

P174067-A2.text: Real-time dashboards and scorecards for institutional performance. The platform generates skills and performance data feeding real-time dashboards, organizational scorecards and transparent postings and promotions decisions. Practices: Real-time monitoring dashboards and organizational scorecards for institutions; scorecards for content, providers and civil servants; platform skills data for postings and promotions. These assessments will include the identification of suitable performance indicators and the development of monitoring dashboards that provide real-time data, as well as organizational scorecards for participating institutions. Subcomponent 3.1: Development of training assessment, monitoring and evaluation mechanisms, and knowledge sharing products and events 41. iGOT Karmayogi will develop inbuilt mechanisms to assess civil service officials on their levels of proficiency across different competencies as defined in the FRAC. With robust auditing and monitoring capabilities, the Mission Karmayogi Program will also institutionalize an architecture for developing scorecards for content and third-party providers, as well as for civil service officials, departments, training institutions, and states. While at the initial stage, NPCSCB will focus on capacity building of civil servants, it is envisaged that the information that the technology platform will provide to the government on skills and capabilities over time will provide the basis for a more transparent and efficient system of postings and promotions.
P174067-A2.name: Real-time dashboards and scorecards for institutional performance

P174067-A3.text: SPV-managed iGOT digital assets and telemetry dashboards. Government-owned SPV owns iGOT platform, digitizes FRAC, runs content marketplace and telemetry dashboards The responsibilities of the SPV include the following: • Own, manage, maintain, and improve the digital assets, that is, iGOT Karmayogi and its underlying infrastructure on behalf of the government. It will digitize FRAC and maintain it for departments and create and operationalize the CBP (content) marketplace. • Management of governance of telemetry data.
P174067-A3.name: SPV-managed iGOT digital assets and telemetry dashboards

P174246-A1.text: national electronic vaccination data system for registration and digital certificates. The EVDS records COVID-19 vaccinations nationally, alerts recipients to doses and issues digital certificates, interoperating across provincial systems. Practices: electronic vaccination data system (EVDS) for vaccination tracking; Electronic Vaccination Data System for COVID-19 rollout; EVDS vaccination registration, alerts and digital certificates; Electronic Vaccination Data System (EVDS) for COVID-19 rollout; Electronic Vaccination Data System for national vaccine rollout; EVDS national interoperable vaccination records across provinces. An important innovation has been the establishment of an electronic vaccination data system (EVDS), which serves a similar purpose to the EU’s digital green pass and an important step toward a robust e-health system (see also Prior Action 4, Section IV). b. Prior Action 4: To improve equitable access to COVID-19 vaccines, the Borrower, through its National Department of Health, has launched the South African COVID-19 Programme Registration, which introduces the use of an Electronic Vaccination Data System (EVDS), compliant with the applicable data protection and privacy legislation, in the rolling-out of the Borrower’s COVID-19 vaccination program, setting the stage for future health emergencies, as further evidenced in the COVID-19 Implementation Guide and Toolkit. The February 2021 shift toward a new electronic vaccine data system (EVDS) has been a critical element in the country’s transformation to a digital health system. Results: The system is designed to: (i) capture the relevant metrics of all South African residents who will be vaccinated;
P174246-A1.name: national electronic vaccination data system for registration and digital certificates

P174246-A2.text: mobile-phone social registry with virtual applications and electronic payments. The SRD grant uses mobile phones to build a beneficiary registry, take applications and pay grants electronically, testing mobile money and vouchers. Practices: mobile-phone social registry with virtual application and e-payments; mobile money and virtual voucher grant payments. The COVID-19 SRD grant, including its extension in August 2021 to March 2022, relies on digital technology to rapidly build a social registry with stringent eligibility criteria, virtual application and registration processes, and electronic cash payments. The program is designed so that all transactions are carried out through mobile phones or computers. Direct deposits to beneficiaries’ bank accounts remain the most used payment method, but mobile money and virtual vouchers are also being tested.
P174246-A2.name: mobile-phone social registry with virtual applications and electronic payments

P174246-A3.text: online grant applications with automated cross-database eligibility checks. Digital applications and monthly automated cross-checks against tax, employment, identity and banking databases verify eligibility and flag duplicate applicants. Practices: online portal for wage-subsidy applications with public recipient transparency website; digital social grant application with automated eligibility cross-checks; monthly real-time database cross-checks for grant eligibility; cross-programme digital cross-checks to detect double-dipping; electronic application and automated cross-checking for social grants. The firms apply for the funds each month through an online portal, receive the grants through direct deposit to bank accounts, and are required to pay out the grant to their employees. It has launched a transparency mechanism—all firm recipients are named through an online website—to provide workers with information to monitor their own receipt of funds and has developed grievance procedures, including independent investigators, to follow up on employee and employer complaints. 681, which introduce the use of electronic means to allow for digital application procedures and automated cross-checking to verify eligibility. The new directive makes it possible to use digital technologies in the identification of beneficiaries, distribution of cash payments, and monitoring to reduce leakages.
P174246-A3.name: online grant applications with automated cross-database eligibility checks

P174246-A4.text: multi-channel digital SRD grant registration with real-time application tracking. Applicants register via WhatsApp, USSD, email, website, Facebook or GovChat and track applications in real time. With the re-introduction of the COVID-29 SRD grant in August 2021, all applicants to the program are required to register through WhatsApp, USSD line, email, the SASSA website, Facebook, or GovChat (an online platform connecting the Government and citizens). Because of the digital enrolment, the application trail was immediately established and gave beneficiaries real-time tracking of their applications at each stage without visiting SASSA offices, using call centers, or dealing with lost reference-number receipts, which provides better customer service and reduces administrative costs. The digital footprint reduces the time and cost of the appeal process as well, allowing for just-in-time cross-checks against live databases that determine eligibility.
P174246-A4.name: multi-channel digital SRD grant registration with real-time application tracking

P174246-A5.text: Open-government dashboard tracking COVID-19 response spending. Bank and OGP help DPME build a dashboard and citizen platform to track COVID-19 spending The World Bank, in partnership with the Open Government Partnership, will help the DPME build a dashboard to monitor select indicators of the Government’s response and support a platform for government to work with citizens, civil society and business, to track spending on the COVID-19 response, so that the resources achieve their intended goals. The WBG and the DPME at the Presidency of the Republic of South Africa have agreed to jointly monitor the result indicators of this operation, as an integral part of the monitoring of the Government’s implementation of its response to the COVID-19 pandemic.
P174246-A5.name: Open-government dashboard tracking COVID-19 response spending

P174170-A1.text: national locust early warning and mobile field surveillance system. The project deploys eLocust3 devices, GPS, satellite data and a mobile-app DLERS feeding RAMSES GIS, linking Yemeni locust data to regional early warning networks. Practices: Desert Locust early warning system linked to regional networks; eLocust3 and GPS field surveillance with satellite data; Mobile-app Desert Locust Early Response System (DLERS); satellite surveillance and eLocust3 field data collection for locust monitoring; national early warning systems for climate-induced locust outbreaks; integrated Desert Locust Early Response System (DLERS) with four subsystems; mobile-device field data entry feeding RAMSES GIS. (ii) livelihood support focuses on protection and restoration in the locust-affected areas; and (iii) strengthened national preparedness systems includes three main elements—establishing a network of DLCCs, establishing an early response system, and connecting Yemeni systems with regional networks to exchange information and data and improve coordination of the locust response. Progress toward the achievement of the PDO will be measured by the following outcome indicators : Outcome 1: Control of desert locust outbreak implemented:  Share of affected pasture/rangeland restored to productivity (percent)  Share of affected agricultural land restored to productivity (percent) Outcome 2: Livelihoods in locust affected areas supported  Affected households (number) supported by social safety nets, of which females (percent) are the direct recipients of benefits  Share of locust-affected farmers (including crop farmers, livestock owners and beekeepers) reporting renewed agricultural activity, of which female-headed farms (percent) Page 12 of 67 The World Bank Yemen Desert Locust Response Project (P174170) Outcome 3: Country’s preparedness against future locust outbreaks strengthened  Yemen’s locust control plan developed (Yes/No)  Early warning system developed and functioning (Yes/No) B. The project will procure inputs for satellite surveillance (satellite maps and meta-data analysis) and equipment for land surveillance (elocust3, GPS, camping kits, dissection kits, 4WD pickup trucks), as well as finance costs associated with locust surveillance and monitoring. Activities under this sub-component aim to provide early warning of locust outbreaks, inform effective control operations, and mobilize assistance (under Component 2) for affected and at-risk communities.
P174170-A1.name: national locust early warning and mobile field surveillance system

P174170-A2.text: satellite imagery and geospatial habitat mapping for locust risk targeting. The project uses satellite imagery, GPS cameras and geospatial habitat mapping of climate and soil variables to assess outbreak risk and target preventive control. Practices: Satellite imagery and habitat mapping for locust vulnerability; satellite imagery and geospatial analysis for locust outbreak risk; habitat mapping of locust vulnerability and impact zones; satellite maps and GPS-enabled cameras for outbreak pinpointing. Satellite images and associated geospatial technologies can provide timely data to assess the risk of impending locust outbreaks. Habitat mapping will apply climate, soil, and other variables to map the susceptibility of land areas in space and time to locust outbreaks (locust vulnerability mapping) and also to highlight areas where locusts have already proliferated (locust impact map). Satellite images and the associated geospatial technologies can provide timely data to assess the risk of impending locust outbreaks. This information will be used for targeted preventative management actions in the locust breeding areas under changing climatic conditions.
P174170-A2.name: satellite imagery and geospatial habitat mapping for locust risk targeting

P174170-A3.text: RAMSES GIS server sharing locust data with FAO regionally. Central server in Aden links DLERS to FAO for regional surveillance and data sharing. Data entered in the mobile devices will be instantly sent to the CDLCC, equipped with the custom RAMSES Geographic Information System application that is used in every locust-affected country for data analysis, locust infestation vulnerability mapping, and reporting. In addition to the central server in Aden, the DLERS will be linked to FAO to share up-to-date information on surveillance, equipment, and expertise with other countries in East Africa and MENA.
P174170-A3.name: RAMSES GIS server sharing locust data with FAO regionally

P174399-A2.text: LMS-hosted digitized curriculum content for core subjects. Digitizes core-subject curriculum and hosts it on openly accessible learning management systems for urban and rural schools. Practices: Digitized curriculum content hosted on learning management system; LMS-hosted digital content for schools; Openly accessible LMS hosting digital curriculum content for schools; LMS-hosted digital curriculum content for learning recovery; LMS-hosted digitized curriculum for core subjects. The main activities under the PfoR will include the development (and/or curation) of digital content on core subjects (English, Mathematics, Science, Dzongkha). These contents will be hosted on at least two platforms, one of which will be the learning management system, for easy access to students and teachers across the country, especially for the schools in urban poor and rural areas. The objective would be to make these contents accessible in at least 80 percent of schools in urban poor areas and at least 40 percent of schools in rural areas.
