P174484-A1.text: Dynamic NSER social registry with multi-entry access and big data targeting. The project uses MELA access points, big data analytics, an updated PMT algorithm and a hybrid-scheme beneficiary registry to keep NSER household data current and targeting accurate. Practices: Multi-entry localized access (MELA) system for social registry updates; Big data analytics and updated PMT algorithm integrated into NSER targeting; Multi-entry localized access (MELA) registry intake system; Big data analytics and updated PMT algorithm for targeting; BISP digital platform tracking hybrid savings scheme accounts; Beneficiary registry platform for hybrid scheme linked to NSER; Big data assessment to complement NSER targeting methods; NADRA unique ID linking social registry data across systems; NSER data exchange interface with signed data sharing agreements; Beneficiary registry and platform for hybrid social protection scheme; IVR pilot for localized climate-disaster targeting; Beneficiary registry and MIS platform for hybrid SP scheme; NSER data exchange interface under signed data sharing agreements; Functional beneficiary registry and platform for hybrid SP scheme; MELA dynamic NSER data update mechanism; Hybrid scheme beneficiary registry and MIS platform; NSER interface integrating NDMA and Met hazard data; Geospatial and telecom big data to improve NSER targeting. This includes the introduction of a multi-entry localized access (MELA) system that provides greater access to the social registry (NSER) to enable regular and timely updates, big data and analytics to improve targeting, and development of a hybrid SP scheme to gradually expand protection to the missing middle. Specifically, the program would: (i) Build-in greater innovation and technology within SP systems to improve the social registry’s capacity to maintain updated household data, exchange data with social programs, optimize use of cross- checks, improve data and analytics for targeting, and provide greater beneficiary choice in the biometric payment systems. This RA will support, among others, the more frequent intake and registration for the social registry through introduction of a multi-entry, localized, access system. The goal of the MELA mechanism is to (i) provide Page 10 of 50 The World Bank Pakistan Crisis-Resilient Social Protection (CRISP) (P174484) multiple points of entry (physical registration desks, door-to-door surveys, virtual services);
P174484-A1.name: Dynamic NSER social registry with multi-entry access and big data targeting

P174484-A2.text: Beneficiary-centric digital payments with competing payment service providers. The project pays safety net beneficiaries through a beneficiary-centric mechanism linked to the National Payment Gateway, letting them choose among competing payment service providers. Practices: Biometric payment system linked to National Payment Gateway; Beneficiary-centric digital payment mechanism with PSP choice and competition; Beneficiary-centric payment mechanism with PSP choice. It would also include the next generation of payment system reforms to link the BISP payment system to the National Payment Gateway. This RA will support advances in the biometric payment system, including technological innovations to promote greater financial inclusion and improvement in services. This would make the payment system more beneficiary centric, remove redundancy of the payment systems, and build resilience against service disruptions from climate shocks. P174546-A1.text: MIS and biometric payment system for emergency cash transfers. Delivers unconditional cash transfers to locust-affected households through SSSNP's existing MIS, grievance mechanism and biometric payment system, reducing fraud and error. Practices: SSSNP MIS and biometric payment mechanism for emergency cash transfers; Biometric and GIS-based cash payment system; biometric and GIS-based payment system for cash transfers. 27 In particular, safety net delivery tools such as the grievance redress mechanism (GRM), management information system (MIS), and biometric payment mechanism established and enhanced under the SSSNP will be used to ensure the effective and accountable delivery of the emergency direct income support of the ELRP. The emergency cash transfer will be provided through the existing operational tools, systems, procedures and arrangements established under the ongoing World Bank-funded SSSNP, implemented by the United Nations Office of Project Services (UNOPS). Delivery of the cash will be done using the payment system established under the SSSNP that uses biometric data and geographic information system data to minimize error, fraud, and corruption. The cash transfer amount will continue to be aligned with the SSSNP at US$2.70 per household per day and will be provided only for six months for a total of US$243.0 per household (15 average working days per month) to be paid monthly, as an emergency response aimed at addressing impacts of a shot-term acute crisis.
P174546-A1.name: MIS and biometric payment system for emergency cash transfers

P174546-A2.text: Earth observation and drone surveillance for pest monitoring. Uses earth observation satellite training and drone surveys to detect locusts, including in areas staff cannot safely reach. Practices: Earth observation satellite training for transboundary pest monitoring; drone surveillance for locust detection in insecure areas. This will also support access to a training program being developed in conjunction with the European Space Agency on using earth observation satellites for transboundary pest monitoring, what governments need to know, what services are available, and how best to access this information. Where possible, the project will make use of technology, like drones, to surveil for locusts even where staff cannot venture.
P174546-A2.name: Earth observation and drone surveillance for pest monitoring

P174546-A3.text: Biometric enrolment and authentication in MIS for payroll and payments. Registers beneficiaries' fingerprints and photos in a single biometric catalogue and authenticates them against the MIS before generating payroll and paying cash. Practices: SSSNP MIS and biometric payroll generation and verification; Biometric authentication against MIS database for cash transfers; Single biometric catalogue to avoid beneficiary duplication; biometric fingerprint and photo registration into MIS for payment. The ELRP will utilize the established and well-functioning SSSNP MIS and biometric system to generate payroll, verify payments, and conduct payment reconciliation to minimize error, fraud, and corruption. Following, a payroll will be generated through the MIS of all the enrolled beneficiaries at a given project location for the payment period. Cash will only be provided to the beneficiary households based on biometric authentication against the enrolled beneficiary database in the MIS to ensure that the intended beneficiaries receive the cash. Following the transfers, the financial service provider will share with UNOPS the list of paid beneficiaries, accompanied by biometric evidence of payment, which will then be reconciled against the payroll.
P174546-A3.name: Biometric enrolment and authentication in MIS for payroll and payments

P174593-A2.text: LiDAR and bathymetric surveys for embankment asset management. Project finances LiDAR, bathymetric and hydro-met surveys feeding forecasting and an embankment asset management plan. P174684-A1.text: digital case management and CRM for commercial justice and investment promotion. The project finances digital case management for commercial courts and a full CRM for investment promotion and investor aftercare services. Practices: Digital case management for commercial justice; Full CRM system for investment promotion and investor aftercare. Examples include support for the digitization of case management to streamline commercial justice. The project will develop and utilize digital solutions for government to business services (G2B) to facilitate activities for the private sector. The project will support the implementation of a full CRM system for the various services of EDBM, including the investment promotion activities. Such system will strengthen EDBM’s ability to track the investor services they provide (from first contacts, to lead to projects, to issues, reinvestment and linkages), thereby improving the quality of these services.
P174684-A1.name: digital case management and CRM for commercial justice and investment promotion

P174684-A2.text: Pilot digital tourism interventions: online booking, contactless payment, real-time data. Project pilots online booking and payment, contactless technology and real-time data collection in tourism. These activities will include (i) pilot interventions in digital technology for tourism, with examples that include online booking and payment, promotion of contactless technology, and the collection of real-time data; and (ii) digital agriculture initiatives that lower barriers to farmers and SMEs’ access to upstream and downstream market s, to services, and to information.
P174684-A2.name: Pilot digital tourism interventions: online booking, contactless payment, real-time data

P175594-A1.text: unified national social registry and interoperable MIS for multi-program targeting. The project builds a single social registry and shared MIS, linked to civil registry and social security databases, to target households across programs. Practices: Unique social registry (RSU) for cross-program targeting; Common MIS platform overseeing multiple social programs; Nationwide RSU deployment with continuous data refresh; Common MIS platform across social programs and databases; Interoperable MIS linked to civil registry and social security databases; National unique social registry with proxy means testing and community validation; Unique social registry (RSU) registering households nationwide; Integrated social registry MIS for multi-program targeting; TA to build unified social registry (RSU) and its MIS. Besides quarterly cash transfers20, the program also provides economic inclusion measures to beneficiary households to support their income and build their resilience in view of their exit from the PTMP.21 In addition to financing the PTMP, the PFSP has also been supporting the development of foundational elements of an adaptive safety nets system focusing on the poorest households: a unique social registry (Registre Social Unique, RSU), the PTMP’s Management Information System (MIS), a digital payment system, and a Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM). 9. A coordinated safety nets system could ensure better service delivery and more holistic interventions toward poor and vulnerable households. (i) Pillar (a): Harmonized tools are used by all social programs and mechanisms for targeting poor and vulnerable households are more efficient: The key focus of this pillar is to ensure the deployment of the RSU across the country, while also working on further developing key tools that can be leveraged across social programs for a functioning safety net system.

P175915-A1.text: digital ESIA monitoring and GIS-based ministry information systems. The project builds a digital system to monitor environmental and social impact assessments and overhauls ministry M&E with GIS and natural capital satellite accounts. Practices: digital ESIA/ESMP monitoring system; GIS-based ministry information systems and natural capital satellite accounts. This subcomponent will support: (a) strengthening management of E&S risks, including dissemination of a new Environment Code; preparation of related regulations and guidelines including on climate change risks and mitigation measures; development of an E&S management training program for key ministries, staff of the Project Implementation Units (PIUs), and young professionals; and development of a digital monitoring system for Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs) and Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs) and (b) enhancement of environmental monitoring systems, including the management of environmental emergencies in the regions (technical assistance, training, equipment, and information systems) and the expansion of the air quality monitoring system. The project will also support the overhaul of the M&E systems of the two ministries, through support for the development and modernization of information systems (for example, geographic information system [GIS]-based systems), statistical databases (for example, natural capital satellite accounts), and related analytical products (for example, on value chains). These systems will both reinforce the rationality of decision-making based on accurate and up-to-date information and increase transparency on natural resource capital and its management.

P175915-A4.text: national forest monitoring, timber traceability and digital patrol systems. The project builds a national forest monitoring and traceability system using remote sensing, inventories and labeling, and equips forestry staff with drones, camera traps and digital patrol planning. P176163-A2.text: waste data management and reporting system for EPBI eligibility. Municipalities must operate a waste data management, monitoring and reporting system to qualify for performance-based investments. Practices: waste data management and reporting system for municipal EPBI eligibility; Waste data management system as EPBI eligibility criterion. Municipalities will be eligible for EPBIs in accordance to eligibility criteria and procedures as set forth in the loan agreement and the EPBI Manual, which will include the obligations to (i) have established a waste data management, monitoring, and reporting system, to the Borrower’s and the Bank’s satisfaction; (iii) provide adequate technical waste management staff for planning and operations, as well as data management and monitoring functions; The minimum criterion for municipality eligibility is the establishment of a waste data management, monitoring, and reporting system which will be supported through TA from the project (sub-component 1.1). The provision of the EPBI investments will be based on how well each municipality performs on the following performance indicators which will be used to monitor progress: (a) percentage of waste collected/increased service coverage of population, (b) percentage of households covered by solid waste services, and (c) cost recovery of services at the municipality (local government unit) level.
P176163-A2.name: waste data management and reporting system for EPBI eligibility

P175731-A1.text: Big data, open data portals and microdata systems for official statistics. The project pilots big data, builds open data portals and harmonized transmission architecture, and publishes anonymized microdata to modernize statistical production. Practices: Piloting Big Data processing for official statistics; SADC Integrated Trade Statistics System; Open Data Portals for SADC statistics with map analytics; Harmonized data transmission architecture for member NSOs; Migration and Tourism Information Systems in Zambia; National data portals disseminating anonymized micro-data; SDCMicro-based microdata anonymization and cataloging for open data access; Big Data analyses and indicator production pilots; Phone-based quarterly high-frequency household and enterprise surveys; Open data microdata library with anonymized datasets and publication calendar; Online microdata access from ZamStats web portal; Satellite imagery for rapid monitoring data production; Satellite imagery for rapid monitoring and data gap filling; satellite and call-record big data for adaptive statistics. It will primarily support NSOs to improve their ability to collect and produce statistical information by developing guidelines and delivering technical assistance for data collection from administrative records, expanding the use of specialized software, assisting development and maintenance of Statistical Business Registers, piloting processing Big Data for statistical purposes, delivering trainings for accessing and use of spatial information to collect census and survey data (GIS) through cartographic work, providing advanced training on sampling techniques, develop harmonized survey modules to collect household-level surveys to generate more data on informal sector, poverty, labor statistics, gender, migration, and so on. Under this sub-component, the SADC Secretariat’s statistics department will develop and implement SADC’s Integrated Trade Statistics System; Open Data Portals for SADC Statistics with the latest dissemination technologies (analytics using maps, and so on); and develop and implement harmonized data transmissions procedures and architecture for Member country NSOs. Lastly, in Zambia the project will also support administrative data systems, such as the development of a Migration Information System and a Tourism Information system, and the compilation of climate statistics.

They include a) the creation of a platform for data exchange and interoperability with the various stakeholders in the statistical system; b) modernization of equipment, especially information and communication technologies to ensure efficient workflows for data collection, processing, analysis, dissemination, and archiving at INSTAT and DGEP.
P175731-A2.name: Interoperable data-sharing platform for statistical system stakeholders

P175731-A3.text: SWIFT module in quarterly LFS for poverty tracking. Project inserts a SWIFT module into the quarterly LFS to track poverty trends between living conditions surveys. P176633-A1.text: Geospatial least-cost electrification planning with remote mini-grid monitoring. The project uses geospatial least-cost rollout planning to site mini-grids in conflict-affected areas and a digital platform to remotely monitor their performance. Practices: Geospatial least-cost electrification rollout plan used to select sites in conflict-affected territories; Digital platform for remote mini-grid performance monitoring. This has been incorporated in the recently finalized geospatial electrification rollout plan and in the selection of sites to be electrified. One of the solutions identified is an adjustment to the spatial distribution of investments, through additional investment in neglected or marginalized territories, with potentially multisector projects supporting the deployment of infrastructure, services, and governance systems across territories, focusing on territorial and social inclusion. Communities in both conflict and high conflict risk territories will be provided with access to electricity under the project. It would support AMADER’s Technical assistance in project management and supervision of works, communication, and the development of the digital platform for the collection and analysis of data to ensure remote performance monitoring of individual mini-grids.

P176371-A1.text: interactive data portals, dashboards and big-data analytics for statistics dissemination. The project uses online portals, dashboards, geospatial platforms, phone surveys and satellite/machine-learning analysis to disseminate and modernize official statistics. Practices: One-stop-shop national data portals for statistics dissemination; Public Data Science Campus for big data analysis and access; Regional National Accounts System compilation software with built-in guidance; Online portals and dashboards for digital statistical dissemination; Emergency observatories with rapid phone surveys and big data analytics; Data dissemination tools and communication strategies for census and surveys; Interactive online data dissemination platform for statistics; Interactive integrated data visualization and mapping platform; Interactive census dashboard with mapping platform online; Rapid response phone survey observatory for high-frequency data; Remote sensing data to monitor agricultural output and urbanization; Machine-learning and geospatial poverty estimation; Remote sensor data analysis for agricultural statistics; Geospatial database from Census 2022 for users; Big data and technical innovation reports for statistics; Statistical Business Register with online metadata; Harmonized national data portal with recent survey data; Live dashboard of national socioeconomic indicators; Interactive web portal with FYDP indicator dashboard; Online anonymized microdata archive of household surveys; Interactive mapping platform for poverty and survey data; Interactive data portal generating custom census tables and charts; Interactive mapping platform for survey and census data; Rapid response phone observatory for high-frequency surveys; Satellite imagery analysis for agricultural and urbanization statistics; Geospatial poverty estimation tools; Census-based multi-layer geospatial database of enumeration areas; Big data and satellite imagery innovation reports for statistics; Big data, geospatial data and machine learning for official statistics production; Harmonized interactive data dissemination portals; Real-time census control center for logistics and data quality; Remote sensing and machine learning for poverty and statistics; Rapid Response Phone Survey Observatory; Integrated statistical information system linking national, regional, continental levels; Open Data Platform with SDMX for regional data dissemination; Regional price collection software modules for CPI. Consistent with the supported national programs for statistics, the Operation includes incentives in the form of Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLI) milestones for timely dissemination of statistics, e.g., according to advanced release calendars, in a user-friendly format, e.g., through setup of one-stop-shop data portals and translation into local languages. Similarly, DLI milestones incentivize advocacy and statistical literacy, e.g., outreach programs, communication strategies, infographics competitions and literacy training. It will also support Strategic Objective 6 under Pillar 2 to equip and operationalize a public Data Science Campus to facilitate data access, promote innovation, and build capacity in data science and big data analysis. This involves equipping the campus with specialized technology and software, as well as developing new workstreams in training and research.

P176371-A2.text: interoperable SDMX data exchange and modern data infrastructure for statistics. The project builds SDMX-based data exchange, interoperable data centres, cloud servers and tablet survey systems to link and share statistical data across agencies. Practices: SDMX-based automated administrative data exchange across agencies; SDMX data transmission systems linking countries, RECs and STATAFRIC; Modular data platforms linking administrative data to budget indicators; Tablet-survey IT infrastructure with on-the-fly data monitoring; Remote sensing facilities with satellite imagery and spatial data portal; Interoperable modern data centre across national statistical system; Interoperable integrated administrative-data database with tiered-access data portal; Upgraded remote sensing capacity with spatial data portal; Interoperable national data center for cross-sectoral statistical databases; Private cloud with secure remote analysis of statistical data; Big data ICT infrastructure for regional data science hub; IT systems for regional statistical data exchange. Support will also be provided to the development of protocols for improving automated sharing of administrative data among agencies, including through the NSS wide adoption of SDMX as the data exchange standard, enabling the integration of data through modular data platforms. Support under the first theme revolves around improving the regulatory environment, quality control procedures, the adoption and harmonization of data exchange standards, adoption and implementation of data quality assessment frameworks, and the harmonization and standardization of survey methodologies. This will be achieved by supporting African countries in setting up data transmission systems between countries, regional economic communities and STATAFRIC, using SDMX data exchange standards. Sub-component 2 of the grant to AU, Institutional development, capacity building and project management will provide support to establish an effective technological environment and build implementation capacity for STATAFRIC.
P176371-A2.name: interoperable SDMX data exchange and modern data infrastructure for statistics

P176371-A5.text: Public Data Science Campus for data access and big data analysis. Program equips and operationalizes a public Data Science Campus for data access, innovation and big data capacity. This involves equipping the campus with specialized technology and software, as well as developing new workstreams in training and research. P177722-A1.text: Automated deposit insurance payout and single customer view system. The project funds IDIF software that automates insured-depositor compensation and gives access to bank deposit data for monitoring and payouts. Practices: Payout automation system for deposit insurance compensation; Single Customer View software for bank deposit data access. The proposed project will address the identified gaps in Individual Deposit Insurance Fund (IDIF)’s capacity to perform its mandate.4 IDIF reforms include increasing its recovery ratios in future payouts and incorporating lessons learned from the TSB and AIB payouts - namely, the need for further automation to hasten the payout process and for raising public awareness on the deposit insurance scheme. This subcomponent will fund the partial replenishment of IDIF’s reserves that backup funding arrangements from the government will complement,9 and with the remaining gap to be gradually closed by the inflow of industry contributions. • Subcomponent 1.2: Payout automation (US$1 million). This subcomponent will provide IDIF with systems to access information on deposits from banks and monitor the banks’ deposit base (Single Customer View soft ware), 8 The World Bank provided technical assistance on deposit insurance until the end of 2019 and continues to provide technical assistance on the broader financial safety net to NBT focused on bank supervision and resolution.
P177722-A1.name: Automated deposit insurance payout and single customer view system

P176935-A1.text: ML satellite poverty maps with USSD self-registration for urban targeting. Uses machine-learning poverty maps from satellite and cellphone data to select wards, then SMS blasts invite households to self-register via USSD into a geotagged registry. Practices: ML poverty maps from satellite imagery for urban ward targeting; USSD self-registration via SMS blasts for urban cash transfers; Big-data targeting using satellite imagery and call detail records; machine-learning poverty maps from satellite imagery for ward targeting; SMS blast and USSD code self-registration for cash transfers; ML and call detail records to target assistance in real time; geotagged beneficiary roster linked to payment system for shock response; satellite imagery poverty maps and big-data targeting; satellite imagery and cellphone-data targeting for urban cash transfers; Rapid Response Registry with ML satellite-imagery targeting and cellphone self-enrollment; Machine-learning poverty maps from satellite imagery for urban ward targeting; USSD self-registration via targeted SMS blasts; USSD self-registration for urban COVID cash transfer registry; Payment delivery via NIN, national payments and NCTO MIS; BVN biometric authentication for beneficiary account onboarding; Machine-learning poverty map from satellite imagery for ward targeting; Localized SMS blasts inviting self-registration in selected wards. In the absence of a social registry with sufficient coverage in urban and peri-urban areas, the RRR is being developed through two key innovations: (a) geographic targeting based on poverty maps—1,163 of the poorest urban wards with a total population of over 20 million people were selected based on the ward-level poverty maps produced by applying cutting-edge machine learning algorithms to granular satellite imagery data,27 and (b) mobile-based self-registration—potential beneficiaries in the selected wards were invited to self-register through an unstructured supplementary service data (USSD) application through targeted and localized short message service (SMS) blasts in the selected wards. The USSD-based self-registration system provides a quick way to establish a registry in urban areas whereas the geographic targeting of wards ensures that most of the beneficiaries registered are poor and vulnerable. The USSD-based self-registration was launched in June 2021, and potential beneficiaries were given 10 days to self-register.28 To date, the system has received over 1.75 million successful registrations. For this project, an efficient and scalable targeting and registration system uses granular big data (such as satellite imagery and call detail records) to identify areas with high incidence of poverty and vulnerability and deploys a technology-aided system (for example, using mobile phones) to quickly register beneficiaries.
P176935-A1.name: ML satellite poverty maps with USSD self-registration for urban targeting

P176935-A2.text: Interoperable Tier-1 transaction accounts with straight-through G2P payments. Opens minimal-KYC interoperable accounts in bulk via PSPs using BVN/NIN, paying transfers straight-through and adding roaming access points where digital payment is limited. Practices: interoperable transaction accounts with straight-through electronic G2P transfers; Tier 1 minimal-KYC transaction accounts for unbanked beneficiaries; bulk transaction account creation from registration/enrollment data transmitted to financial institutions; digitized bulk payment delivery chain for cash transfers; interoperable transactional accounts for unbanked cash transfer beneficiaries; straight-through digital payments to beneficiary transaction accounts; PSP roaming access points for electronic benefit payments; PSP roaming access points for beneficiaries outside digital payments; Interoperable G2P payment process reusable across programs; NCTO field staff collect KYC data and share it with PSPs to open Tier-1 interoperable transaction accounts; PSPs bulk-create interoperable Tier-1/2 accounts and link holders via BVN/NIN registration; Straight-through electronic payments to bulk-opened transactional accounts. The proposed improvements include (a) opening interoperable transaction accounts for beneficiaries without an existing bank account (transaction accounts promote financial inclusion among unbanked beneficiaries and interoperability will save travel time for beneficiaries to access funds and increase utility of the account); (b) leveraging the national payments infrastructure to allow for electronic funds transfer to beneficiaries’ accounts using 39Potential mechanisms of selection could include geographic targeting of wards based on the poverty map, (updated) PMT scores, attributes collected during the enrollment process, or a combination of these approaches. Page 22 of 110 The World Bank National Social Safety Net Program - Scale Up (P176935) straight-through processing; The project will support opening of a Tier 1 transaction account with minimal know your customer (KYC) requirements for beneficiaries without an account.42 The accounts meet the program objectives of rapidly enrolling and distributing CTs to beneficiaries (expanding financial inclusion in the meanwhile).
P176935-A2.name: Interoperable Tier-1 transaction accounts with straight-through G2P payments

P176935-A3.text: API interoperability across NSR, RRR and NBR registries. Links social registries via APIs for data flow, de-duplication and cross-registry matching. In particular, the project will (a) strengthen the interoperability between the MISs supporting the NSR, the RRR, and the National Beneficiary Registry (NBR) to ensure smooth flow of data and information updates among the three databases through application programming interfaces; (c) support de-duplication within and across registries and linking of the registries to other administrative databases and registries (such as the national ID system, civil registry, and vehicle and property registries) at the national and state levels, as relevant and feasible;
P176935-A3.name: API interoperability across NSR, RRR and NBR registries

The project aims to lay a groundwork for data exchange and integration through development of the memorandum of understanding (MoU) framework for data sharing, the LSS Data Quality Assessment Framework (LSSQAF/DQAF), ICT infrastructure to support data exchange, and upgrading of the existing coordination mechanisms. In addition to improving data production and dissemination, the project will foster data exchange and integration within the LSS. P178002-A2.text: Integrated data platforms and geospatial tools for statistics production and access. The project pilots integrated platforms pooling census, survey and administrative data, adds geospatial and CAPI census tools, and opens portals and microdata libraries for public access. Practices: Integrated data platform accessing administrative data sources; Integrated data platform pilot for sectoral statistics; Online platform for SEZ investment data collection; Geospatial cartography for agricultural and social statistics; CAPI and digital census maps for population census; Geocoded census maps for hazard and service-access analysis; Integrated data platform pooling census, survey and administrative data; Centralized one-stop data portal linking fragmented statistical portals; Data-visualization portal with labor market monitoring interface and microdata library; Centralized data portal with online data access requests; Online microdata library on LSB website. The second PDO indicator is linked to the project’s support to production of real sector indicators and pilot of an integrated data platform, which will allow LSB to access administrative data sources in a more timely manner. P178545-A1.text: Offline-capable tablets with distance-learning YouTube channel for village facilitators. Provides weatherproof tablets with offline software and smartphone credit, plus YouTube distance learning, to youth groups and facilitators. It will expand a capacity-building approach successfully introduced for local PRF staff in the AF phase of PRF III, combining face-to-face sessions with distance learning via a YouTube channel. The project provides weatherproof tablets to the YGs, with software allowing offline sessions and smartphone credit to the Page 37 of 84 The World Bank Community Livelihood Enhancement And Resilience (P178545) village facilitators.
P178545-A1.name: Offline-capable tablets with distance-learning YouTube channel for village facilitators

P178347-A1.text: Machine-learning estimates of solar power used for groundwater pumping. Project will train and verify ML-based estimates of solar power deployed for groundwater extraction. The water sector assessment will consider opportunities to enhance access to drinking water through provision of submersible pumps, solar panels, water storage tanks, small desalination units, small water networks and water meters, and capacity‐building support to WUAs to ensure satisfactory maintenance of the water system, with a particular focus on the needs of women, and training and verification for machine learning‐based estimates of the amount of solar power deployed for groundwater extraction.
P178347-A1.name: Machine-learning estimates of solar power used for groundwater pumping

P178347-A2.text: Geospatial electrification plan covering grid, mini-grids and stand-alone systems. Project prepares a geospatial-based electrification plan and assesses public/private delivery models. (c) preparation of a geospatial‐based electrification plan consisting of grid‐based expansion, mini‐grids, and stand‐alone systems and assessment of the suitability of public sector and private sector delivery models; and (d) a diagnostic of the PEC to assess performance improvement needs including capacity building and structural and system enhancements such as improvements in metering, billing, and collection.
P178347-A2.name: Geospatial electrification plan covering grid, mini-grids and stand-alone systems

P178347-A3.text: GIS-based activity mapping and expenditure tracking portal. A GIS portal maps project activities and tracks expenditures in real time, with social media analysis, to enable public oversight and transparency. Practices: GIS-based portal mapping all project activities for transparency; GIS-based expenditure tracking and information dissemination system; Social media analysis for oversight and accountability. (c) maintains a GIS‐based portal mapping all activities supported under sub‐component 1.2 to promote transparency; To that end, UNOPS will establish a real‐time oversight, transparency, and accountability mechanism through a GIS‐based expenditure tracking and information dissemination system as well as the use of social media analysis. (e) establishing a real‐time oversight, transparency, and accountability mechanism through a GIS‐based expenditure tracking and information dissemination system; (f) providing updated GIS maps of the project areas to help monitor progress and enhance project supervision;
P178347-A3.name: GIS-based activity mapping and expenditure tracking portal

P177816-A1.text: e-vouchers and digital financial services for farmer input access. The project uses e-vouchers, digital financial services and automated SACCO systems to give farmers, including women, access to quality inputs and finance. Practices: e-vouchers for high-quality commercial agricultural inputs; Digital financial services and automated SACCO systems for farmers; e-voucher quotas and digital literacy training for women farmers. E-vouchers for high-quality commercial inputs; trade policy and rule harmonization (including food and trade standards, food safety management, and compliance) and trade negotiation capacity; and public food procurement. It will support: (a) the development and deployment of digital financial services to reduce information asymmetries, increase efficiency, and increase financial inclusion, which will help diversify livelihoods vulnerable to climate change impacts, supporting adoption of climate resistant varieties of crops and livestock; (c) financial management systems and capacities, through a combination of training for members and the automation of SACCOs' management and financial systems; and (d) revolving funds (the financial inclusion matching grants) where the CIG/VMG savings will be matched and will be administered in the eligible SACCOs and provided by CDDCs, and primarily supporting CIGs/VMGs’ adoption of climate-smart TIMPs and technologies and climate-resilient inputs. The project will engage with commercial banks, SACCOs, microfinance institutions, and digital financial service providers to build county-, regional- and national- level partnerships supporting sustainable and inclusive financial services, as well as to develop specialized credit products designed to support climate-smart agriculture.
P177816-A1.name: e-vouchers and digital financial services for farmer input access

P177816-A2.text: scaled digital agriculture data and advisory platforms. The project builds and scales digital platforms integrating weather, market, pest and land data to deliver climate and market advisories to farmers and planners. Practices: replicable multi-country digital agriculture platforms and solutions (data digitization, e-commerce platforms, incubating public/private digital agriculture initiatives); digitization of sector-relevant agricultural data and development of requisite data systems, platforms and policies; scaled digital agriculture data and advisory platform; Scaling KALRO big data platform for agricultural resilience planning; Big data platform integrated with KIAMIS for pest and climate advisory; digital agriculture platform delivering weather and market information; scale-up of decentralized meteorological information system for farmer climate-risk decisions; national digital climate advisory service for registered farmers; disruptive agriculture technology platform with hydromet data; scaled digital agriculture information systems with agrometeorological advisory; digital agriculture information systems for climate risk decisions; virtual one-stop service center linked to meteorological, NAMIS, LMIS and food-safety information systems; multi-source agricultural data streams (climate, farm, market, pest, water) for climate risk management; High-frequency data system tracking market, productivity and food security indicators; KALRO big data platform for agrometeorological and market advice. (b) develop replicable or multi-country digital agriculture platforms and solutions (Box 1); Phase 3 will help strengthen the foundations of digital agriculture in participating countries and the wider region by for example supporting the digitization of relevant data, including by helping develop the requisite systems, platforms, and policies, as well as helping incubate and accelerate public and private digital agriculture initiatives such as e- commerce platforms and other digital solutions across the region. This subcomponent will strengthen and scale up the existing pilot systems used to manage agricultural production, price, and weather data at the national and regional levels. Furthermore, this subcomponent would also build the right tools and strengthen advisory systems to support farmers’ and other value chain actors’ ability to access and use these data to better manage weather and market risk and make better-informed decisions.
P177816-A2.name: scaled digital agriculture data and advisory platforms

P177816-A3.text: geotagged MIS and digitized farmer registries for data-driven planning. The project uses KOBO, GIS-enabled MIS and digitized farmer and cooperative registries to map, monitor and inform agricultural policy and programming. Practices: GEMS KOBO Toolbox geotagged real-time investment mapping and monitoring; Digitization of farmer registries and agricultural statistics for data-driven programming; Web-based geotagged M&E/MIS with real-time monitoring images; GIS-enabled MIS mapping project and beneficiary information; automated cooperative registry; national farmer and pastoralist registry for data-driven policy. (b) using the Geo-Enabling Initiative for Monitoring and Supervision (GEMS) KOBO Toolbox to collect real-time and geotagged data for the project investment mapping and monitoring; The main M&E activities will be adjusted to each country’s needs and capacities, but will include the following main concepts: (a) a project-specific MIS using the country’s existing online M&E MIS platform and linked with the implementing agency’s broader database system; The subcomponent will also support the digitization of agricultural statistics, research outputs, and farmer registries, and build the capacity, within the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development (MoALD), Counties and KALRO, to use statistics and data science to enhance decision- making and enable more climate-adaptive programming, as well as monitoring climate trends, and assess impact of shocks on of rural areas. The web-based M&E and MIS will be set up for data collection and information sharing at the national, county, and community levels.
P177816-A3.name: geotagged MIS and digitized farmer registries for data-driven planning

P177816-A4.text: digital phytosanitary, trade and FPO management systems. The project develops harmonized digital phytosanitary and food safety systems and virtual one-stop trade services, and automates FPO financial management. Practices: harmonized regional phytosanitary data management and forecasting systems; Automation of FPO financial management systems and transactions; virtual one-stop service center for agri-investment and trade; digital sanitary, phytosanitary and food safety system. From the MFD perspective, important enabling activities to be undertaken by Page 28 of 181 The World Bank Food Systems Resilience Program for Eastern and Southern Africa (Phase 3) (P177816) Phase 3l include: (a) developing regulations for SPS services, harmonizing phytosanitary data management, and forecasting systems along with certified laboratories to improve regional trade; (c) the automation of FPO FM systems and transactions; (b) the training of FPO leadership in FM; (c) establishing a virtual one-stop service center for agricultural climate-informed investment and trade;
P177816-A4.name: digital phytosanitary, trade and FPO management systems

P177816-A5.text: digital traceability, surveillance and land monitoring systems. The project deploys animal disease surveillance, livestock traceability and land, forest and soil monitoring systems to support climate and GHG decisions. Practices: animal disease early warning and surveillance system; Land Management Information System for GHG decision-making; livestock identification and traceability system expansion; real-time forest cover, land degradation and soil health data for climate risk decisions. It will also help establish an early warning system for detecting and responding to animal pathology, linked to an animal disease surveillance system. The project will help establish the latter by building a network of border posts, laboratories, production centers, and other organizations in a position to work together to monitor the quality of livestock product imports (including the health of live animals) as well as emerging and cross-border diseases, which the country frequently faces, and by budgeting for a potential crisis. (e) scaling up the Land Management Information System developed under AGCOM (1.0), which will be used to support decision-making for GHG emission reduction; and (f) developing a digital sanitary, phytosanitary, and food safety system. (b) the expansion of the livestock identification and traceability system initiated under the DRIVE project;
P177816-A5.name: digital traceability, surveillance and land monitoring systems

P177816-A6.text: scaled Indian Ocean digital fisheries information systems. Scales up EU-supported digital information systems for Indian Ocean fisheries data (c) scale up ongoing EU-supported efforts to build digital information systems for the Indian Ocean under the SANOI50 project; and (d) support collaborative fisheries governance including coordination on policy measures related to climate adaptation. With respect to fisheries, it will facilitate (a) joint stock assessment and data collection;
P177816-A6.name: scaled Indian Ocean digital fisheries information systems

P177816-A7.text: multi-partner digital agriculture service platforms. The project scales partnerships among agri-tech providers, farmers and pastoralists on the One Million Farmer Platform and EU SANOI systems. Practices: Scaling DAT service-provider partnerships on the One Million Farmer Platform; scaling up EU SANOI digital information systems for Indian Ocean food resilience; One Million Farmer DAT platform for digital agriculture services. In order to scale up the uptake of digital solutions, the project will support the scaling up of existing partnerships involving disruptive agricultural technology 61Including manure composting and application, improved pastures management, drought-tolerant crop varieties and other techniques mentioned on Kenya’s CSA Country Profile (https://climateknowledgeportal.worldbank.org/sites/default/files/2019- 06/CSA%20KENYA%20NOV%2018%202015.pdf) Page 82 of 181 The World Bank Food Systems Resilience Program for Eastern and Southern Africa (Phase 3) (P177816) (DAT) service providers, farmers, pastoralists, and agro-pastoralists, building on the One Million Farmer Platform. This subcomponent aims to strengthen community engagement and enhance the uptake of digital solutions at the farm level with the objective of enhancing climate resilience and productivity, particularly among women farmers. (c) scaling up ongoing EU-supported efforts to build digital information systems for the Indian Ocean under the SANOI project; and (d) supporting collaborative fisheries governance, supporting both regional climate preparedness and risk management. This subcomponent will support direct collaboration with regional Research on low-carbon technologies or other technologies Regional Integration neighbors and organizations around food systems resilience instrumental to achieving full decarbonization Efforts (IDA US$0.3 research and policy, focusing on (a) supporting regional million) collaboration with other members of the IOC to strengthen early warning systems, climate risk management, and intra-regional trade;
P177816-A7.name: multi-partner digital agriculture service platforms

P178564-A1.text: integrated statistical data infrastructure for census, surveys and administrative records. The project uses multimodal census and survey collection, satellite cartography, data warehouses, viewers and secure access tools to modernize Ecuador's national statistics production and dissemination. Practices: Modular agricultural survey producing environmental indicators; multimodal census collection with ID capture for record linkage; Data warehouse and Data Ecuador inter-thematic viewer; multimodal CAPI/CAWI/CATI census data collection; satellite imagery for census cartography updates; self-reported web census with DDI/NADA microdata cataloging; census ID capture for Nordic-model record integration; Interoperability infrastructure for administrative-record statistics; Data warehouse and data viewer architecture for INEC; Census base registry built from administrative records; Administrative-record verification against census trends; Census-linked geospatial risk maps for disaster exposure; Inter-thematic statistical data warehouse with information cubes; Automated data anonymization and security monitoring tools; Integrated viewer with tiered user access to data warehouse; Multi-role public and specialized statistical data viewers; Virtualized laboratory for remote secure statistical data access; Cloud-server LPI microdata access platform for licensed researchers; satellite imagery and georeferenced cartography for census mapping; multimodal census and survey data collection via tablets, phone, web; free World Bank Survey Solutions CAPI toolkit for national statistics; data virtualization portal for administrative-data statistics. This proposed project will address most of these weaknesses, building on progress made to (i) improve agricultural surveys through innovative modular surveys that, among others, allow producing and monitoring environmental indicators; The VII Housing and VIII Population Census will be collected through a multimodal approach (tablets, telephone, Web, and paper). P178564-A1.name: integrated statistical data infrastructure for census, surveys and administrative records

P178564-A2.text: Simplified real-time composite statistical capacity score. Project builds a simplified 10-sub-indicator composite score from SPI, monitored in real time. Related to the first PDO level indicator, rather than directly using the SPI, the project proposes to use a simplified composite score created specifically for this program that will be measured and monitored in real-time by the project team. The proposed indicator is the sum of 10 sub-indicators included in the SPI, covering four out of the five pillars (Table 1).
P178564-A2.name: Simplified real-time composite statistical capacity score

P178564-A3.text: Virtual laboratories integrating sectoral administrative data. Builds virtual labs integrating sectoral data for consultation and analysis Likewise, the construction of virtual laboratories will integrate the sectorial data. Through the integration of these modules, it is possible to obtain information that contributes to the calculation of numerous SDG indicators, such as 2.3.1, 2.3.2, 2.4.2, 5.a.1, and 12.3.
P178564-A3.name: Virtual laboratories integrating sectoral administrative data

P178644-A1.text: geo-referenced climate risk and housing information mapping. Finances geo-referenced climate risk maps and a Housing Information System to guide territorial planning and investment design. Practices: Geo-referenced climate risk mapping for territorial planning; Housing Information System with geo-referenced housing data; geo-referenced climate risk mapping for municipal planning. The technical assistance for urban planning, under activity (i) above, shall include, inter alia: (i) providing support for the development of geo-referenced climate risks mapping to support informed territorial planning, and specific investments design to support streamlining the climate resilience requirements in all future government plans and investments; (ii) providing support for the development and implementation of a Housing Information System, launched under the SOE related Fiscal Management Project (P160796). This system is expected to provide geo- referenced information on the social, economic, legal and urban dimensions, with the objective of reducing the gap between demand and supply of housing in Cabo Verde. Similarly, this component will finance US$1.65 million towards Technical Assistance for municipal planning to support for the development of geo-referenced climate risks mapping to support informed territorial planning, and specific investments design to support streamlining the climate resilience requirements in all future government plans and investments.
P178644-A1.name: geo-referenced climate risk and housing information mapping

P178684-A1.text: Smart Labs with preloaded digital content and devices in schools. The project equips schools with Smart Labs of digital devices, projectors, local networks and solar charging, preloaded with digital textbooks and science content. Practices: Smart Labs with preloaded digital textbooks and science labs; Smart Labs with teacher and student digital devices in schools. The project will finance the procurement of IT equipment for a multi-purpose Smart Lab in approximately 388 schools in two phases. The Smart Lab will include digital devices, projectors, local network equipment, a solar charging system (if the school is not connected to the electrical grid), and other necessary equipment and materials. The student devices will be preloaded with digital textbooks and digital science labs developed under this sub-component, and teacher devices will be preloaded with teacher guides with structured lessons, teaching-learning resources and teacher professional development content also developed under this sub-component and sub-component 2.2. Number of schools that have been equipped with a Official Smart Lab with project Three reception financing.
P178684-A1.name: Smart Labs with preloaded digital content and devices in schools

P178684-A2.text: ICT monitoring tool and Allô Ecole mobile reporting platform. Inspectors use an annual ICT monitoring tool to track digital package adoption, while teachers and parents report fund misuse through the Allô Ecole mobile platform. Practices: ICT monitoring tool tracking adoption of digital package; Allô Ecole mobile platform for reporting fund misuse. Technical assistance will also be funded to: (i) support the development of an ICT in education policy and strategy to guide technology investments and align them with key education goals and the medium-term expenditure framework, and to develop a policy pertaining to student and teacher data security and privacy; and (ii) develop an annual ICT monitoring tool. The project will finance the training of inspectors in the five core focus provinces in the use of the tool, as well as logistics support to conduct a monitoring exercise during at least two years to determine the adoption and use of the digital package supported by the project, and to identify challenges and provide course-correction recommendations that will inform the roll-out of phase 2 schools. Mitigation measures will include rigorous monitoring of fund use with efficient traceability; periodic report submissions and internal controls; an external annual audit of project financial statements; use of the mobile platform Allô Ecole through which teachers, parents and other stakeholders will be able to report misuse of funds, which in turn will be subject to a case management protocol; and frequent World Bank fiduciary implementation support.
P178684-A2.name: ICT monitoring tool and Allô Ecole mobile reporting platform

P178684-A3.text: Digital devices loaded with classroom observation instrument. Supplies inspectors and school heads with devices preloaded with observation instrument and pedagogical resources for feedback. For each REP, the project will also fund the supply of a digital device for the trained inspector; and for each school, a digital device each for a CUP and the director of studies. Each device will be loaded with the classroom observation instrument (developed under component 3), as well as the associated pedagogical resources mentioned above. They will be trained using project funds on how to use the device to conduct classroom observations and provide feedback.
P178684-A3.name: Digital devices loaded with classroom observation instrument

P178566-A1.text: regional digital climate advisory and agricultural information systems. The project builds digital advisory, early-warning and geospatial information systems that give farmers and policymakers timely climate, crop and market data. Practices: national and regional agricultural information systems for climate adaptation; DCAS site-specific crop and risk advisory to farmers; Regionally harmonized food security MIS and geospatial data platforms; Agricultural intelligence analytics using remote sensing and precision agriculture tools; food system and hydromet information systems delivering early warning to farmers; Digital agricultural extension and advisory services delivery; agricultural weather, price and market data information systems; GEMS/KOBO toolbox for geotagged carbon-accounting data; ICPAC Resilience Analysis Hub food security early-warning services; Regional DCAS climate-data advisory architecture for countries; HoA food systems monitoring mechanism with data protocols; Regional agricultural information systems linking national systems; Crop suitability mapping under future climate scenarios; SADC-level digital climate advisory service (DCAS) for farmers; Regional georeferenced monitoring mechanism for landscape impacts; digital climate advisory services (DCAS) for farmers. Sub-pillar 2.1 will support the development of national and regional agricultural information systems for adaptation planning and resilience building. Well-functioning and widely adopted information systems can play an important role in helping equip agricultural producers, supply chain actors, and service providers for effective climate risk management. The first focuses on the development of national and regional information systems, and the second, on developing agricultural technologies and services and delivering them to farmers and other relevant stakeholders. Through DCAS, farmers can receive timely and site- specific recommendations on crop cultivars, soil preparation, optimal sowing, fertilization, and harvest time and 21Shocks are understood to be transitory adverse events such as natural disasters like floods, hurricanes, landslides, and acute drought events; crop, livestock, and human disease outbreaks;
P178566-A1.name: regional digital climate advisory and agricultural information systems

P178566-A2.text: digital market platforms and traceability systems for smallholders. The project scales digital marketplaces, mechanization platforms and traceability systems so smallholders reach buyers, inputs and compliant regional markets. Practices: regional agricultural information systems for real-time food, market and hydromet data; digital traceability systems for agrifood market compliance; scaling digital marketplace platforms for smallholder market access; digital platform linking farmers to mechanization services; integrated agricultural data platforms and traceability systems; Blockchain-based traceability in regional value chains. The agricultural information systems supported by this sub-pillar include ones that provide, often in real time, food price and market data; animal and plant health data (such as pest and animal disease outbreaks and management), soil data, hydromet data (based on real-time weather, water, early warning, and climate information), and agricultural production and food supply data. The agricultural information systems will enhance producers’ and other decision-makers’ preparedness by equipping them to adapt not only to seasonal variability in weather but also to longer-term trends in climate change. To help producers meet applicable market requirements, the Program will support (a) the analysis of standards and controls applied in domestic and international markets, (b) the adoption of relevant practices, (c) the development of traceability systems including ones that leverage digital technologies, and (d) quality infrastructure (standards and metrology, accreditation capacity, and more). In the case of digital technologies, the sub- pillar will seek to promote the scaling of digital solutions such as marketplace platforms that facilitate small- scale producers’ access to market information, inputs, buyers, storage, and transportation.
P178566-A2.name: digital market platforms and traceability systems for smallholders

P178566-A3.text: georeferenced monitoring and decision-support systems for agriculture. The project uses georeferenced M&E, GEMS geospatial tools and digitized food-reserve decision support to track landscape impacts and stock levels. Practices: georeferenced landscape-level M&E system for climate co-benefits; GEMS-enabled geospatial monitoring tools for FCV-affected implementation areas; Georeferenced landscape monitoring system for CCB impacts; Digitized decision-support system for food reserves. Funding will also be made available for climate co-benefits to be measured through a simple and effective georeferenced monitoring and evaluation (M&E) system designed and implemented to assess the impacts of decisions taken and actions carried out at the landscape level. To mitigate these risks, and with a view to systematically enhancing real-time access Page 53 of 161 The World Bank Food Systems Resilience Program for Eastern and Southern Africa (P178566) to the project’s implementation areas, the team will use and make available to borrowers the tools and technologies enabled by GEMS used in FCV-affected areas. It will do this by (a) establishing a regional mechanism that consists of a simple and effective georeferenced monitoring system designed and implemented to assess the impacts of decisions taken and actions carried out at the landscape level; (c) developing a digitized information and decision-making support component for food reserves;
P178566-A3.name: georeferenced monitoring and decision-support systems for agriculture

P178566-A4.text: regional cooperation on agricultural data exchange, remote sensing and precision agriculture. Promotes regional cooperation on digital agricultural technologies, data exchange, remote sensing, mapping and precision agriculture (b) promoting regional cooperation around DATs and improved data exchange on agriculture, food security, climate vulnerability, women in food systems, and related topics; and (c) promoting green mechanization, data infrastructure, remote sensing and mapping technologies, precision agriculture, and capacity building of a cadre of national and regional experts to effectively deploy and disseminate this technology.
P178566-A4.name: regional cooperation on agricultural data exchange, remote sensing and precision agriculture

P178566-A5.text: Platform for private start-ups delivering digital agricultural services. Project builds a platform enabling private start-ups to deliver digital services to beneficiaries. (c) upgrading of the MoA’s data systems and infrastructure; and (d) a platform that facilitates private sector start-ups’ delivery of digital services to project beneficiaries. To help achieve the government’s vision of digitizing agricultural systems and support the “last-mile delivery” of digital agricultural services to farmers (men, women, and youth), this subcomponent will stimulate the development of a vibrant digital agricultural innovation ecosystem in Ethiopia.
P178566-A5.name: Platform for private start-ups delivering digital agricultural services

P178750-A1.text: digital platforms, supercomputing and scholarship tracking for higher education. The project digitizes ISEP curricula, strengthens IT networks, boosts supercomputer use for big-data research, and runs SENBOURSE to track scholarships transparently. Practices: Digitized program-content platform consolidating ISEP curricula and IT networks; Supercomputer capacity for big-data research and training; SENBOURSE system tracking higher education scholarships transparently. This platform would be improved to consolidate digitized contents of programs; the design of strategic plans and economic models to strengthen the sustainability of ISEPs; the implementation of quality assurance standards; the reinforcement of IT networks for the information system; the establishment of a human resource strategy and of the related legal framework; the setting of a mechanism for teachers’ frequent immersion into companies to allow adaptation to market needs; and planning for sustained capacity building for teachers, technicians, and managers. The project will make specific investments to enhance research capacity within the country by supporting improved use of big data. This includes supporting better utilization of Senegal’s supercomputer which in its current state, is not being fully exploited for research and training. (b) Improve operationalization of the Integrated Higher Education and Research Information System (Système Intégré de Gestion de l’Enseignement Supérieur et de la Recherche, SIGESR) by building on the previously developed infrastructure and digital applications (including ensuring functionality of SENBOURSE which is meant to transparently track higher education scholarships); and (c) Provide support to the growing network of Open Digital Spaces that are being designed to deliver a set of teaching modules for distance learning and are meant to be collectively shared by universities.
P178750-A1.name: digital platforms, supercomputing and scholarship tracking for higher education

P178750-A2.text: Integrated management platform for 3FPT training fund operations. Project finances an integrated platform for internal control, monitoring and faster processing with stakeholders. In addition, institutional support will be provided to the 3FPT, including (a) establishment of an integrated management platform and other tools to support system functioning, internal control, monitoring of implementation, and optimization of processing times with the various stakeholders;
P178750-A2.name: Integrated management platform for 3FPT training fund operations

P178750-A3.text: Shared Open Digital Spaces delivering distance-learning modules across universities. Project supports a network of Open Digital Spaces collectively shared by universities for distance-learning modules. (b) Improve operationalization of the Integrated Higher Education and Research Information System (Système Intégré de Gestion de l’Enseignement Supérieur et de la Recherche, SIGESR) by building on the previously developed infrastructure and digital applications (including ensuring functionality of SENBOURSE which is meant to transparently track higher education scholarships); and (c) Provide support to the growing network of Open Digital Spaces that are being designed to deliver a set of teaching modules for distance learning and are meant to be collectively shared by universities.
P178750-A3.name: Shared Open Digital Spaces delivering distance-learning modules across universities

P179024-A1.text: integrated social protection IT modules and beneficiary tracking systems. Links UBK, Social Contract, youth employment and migrant modules through electronic data exchanges and tracks beneficiaries' labor market outcomes after placement. Practices: employment information system adjusted to track beneficiaries' labor market trajectories after job placement; labor migrant registry integrated with Labor Market Information System; electronic data exchanges across social protection IT modules. First, the information system will be adjusted to monitor beneficiaries even after they complete the job experience opportunity to track their labor market trajectories. To achieve these objectives, the subcomponent will support the development, implementation, and integration of a registry of prospective and returning labor migrants from the Kyrgyz Republic. The registry will collect detailed information on both prospective and returning migrants to provide relevant information about them to public employment services to support this specific population. The implementation of the migrant registry and its links with the Labor Market Information System (LMIS) will allow to refer migrant individuals to support interventions provided by the public employment agency or Page 22 of 61 The World Bank Strengthening Social Assistance and Labor Market Programs Project (P179024) other entities and tailored to their specific needs, such as intermediation services, orientation programs, or skill training, among others.
P179024-A1.name: integrated social protection IT modules and beneficiary tracking systems

P179024-A2.text: data exchange protocols between social protection systems and TUNDUK. Establishes data exchange protocols linking the new social protection software architecture to the national TUNDUK system. It will achieve the goals specifically by (a) Establishing data exchange protocols between the new software architecture and national data exchange system TUNDUK;
P179024-A2.name: data exchange protocols between social protection systems and TUNDUK

P179242-A1.text: digital stock assessment tools and AI catch monitoring. The project deploys data management systems, electronic tags, low-cost radars and AI to collect, analyze and enforce fisheries catch data. Practices: data- and capacity-limited stock assessment tools and fisheries data management systems; electronic tags, low-cost radars and AI for catch reporting and enforcement. (b) improving the stock assessments through the implementation and expansion of tools and capacity for the application of data- and capacity-limited approaches to the production of stock assessment and fisheries management advice, at national and regional level; (c) supporting the adoption of sustainable systems and processes for managing and accessing information and statistics on data-poor and capacity-limited fisheries, covering most steps of the fisheries data process, from collection to analysis, as well as data management, and recovering and making available relevant data from previous projects in the SWIO region; This subcomponent will include: (a) applying enhanced catch reporting, innovations such as electronic tags, low-cost radars and artificial intelligence, and undertaking scientific studies to support implementation, periodic evaluation and updating of climate-resilient fisheries management plans already prepared such as the grouper management plan, the diamond squid management plan, and the bait fish management plan;
P179242-A1.name: digital stock assessment tools and AI catch monitoring

P179242-A2.text: regional fisheries dashboard for data analysis and sharing. The project builds an operational SWIOFC regional dashboard to analyze and share fisheries data, stock findings and management plan evaluations across SWIO countries. Practices: regional fisheries dashboard for sharing management plan evaluations; regional fisheries dashboard for data analysis and sharing; Regional fisheries database dashboard for stock and M&E data sharing. (c) sharing of evaluation reports from the implementation of aforementioned management plans with all SWIO countries through the regional fisheries dashboard of the SWIOFC, establishing information exchange with maritime fusion centers in the Indian Ocean Region, and organizing annual dialogue forums to determine use and applicability of such plans and actions in other SWIO countries and the likeminded coastal G-16 countries; and (d) preparing and implementing climate-resilient management plans for other important fish stocks in Maldives Page 9 of 48 The World Bank Transforming Fisheries Sector Management in South-West Indian Ocean Region and Maldives Project (P179242) in due consideration of the principles and methods discussed in the SWIO country dialogue forums and the relevant outputs of the SWIOFC innovative science program.
