P180496-A1.text: Regulated indirect SPEI participation scheme for payment institutions. Prior action sets rules letting financial entities join SPEI indirectly, cutting cost of digital payments The PA supports regulatory reforms to enhance the availability of digital payment services through clear rules for the indirect participation of financial institutions in SPEI while also enhancing the consumer experience for SPEI and CoDi services and ensuring a robust and modern payments system. The regulations establish rules for indirect participation in SPEI and set out the specific parameters under which direct participants will offer indirect participation services. The new regulated indirect participation scheme is expected to have a positive impact on financial inclusion by enabling greater and more affordable46 access to SPEI for financial institutions and thus improving accessibility and affordability of SPEI-enabled digital payment services (for example, international remittances and CoDi payments) for their customers.
P180496-A1.name: Regulated indirect SPEI participation scheme for payment institutions

P180334-A1.text: land productivity map and land use decision tool. Finances a land productivity map and decision tool to guide agri-food land use decisions. It will finance: (i) a food system diagnostic, including agricultural and industrial censuses, and agri-food related surveus;35 (ii) a land productivity map and a land use decision tool; (iii) digitizing the MoA’s agricultural services, process and communication, including digitalization of extension services and support for the farmers registry and building the capacity of MoA on the use of remote sensing tools;
P180334-A1.name: land productivity map and land use decision tool

P180334-A2.text: digitized MoA extension services and farmers registry. Digitizes Ministry of Agriculture extension services, processes and farmers registry, with remote sensing capacity. (iii) digitizing the MoA’s agricultural services, process and communication, including digitalization of extension services and support for the farmers registry and building the capacity of MoA on the use of remote sensing tools; This sub-component aims to improve the knowledge base for decision-making in the agri- food sector, including for policy makers, farmers, and agribusinesses, and to accelerate the use of digital innovations and tools in areas such as land use monitoring and agricultural extension system.
P180334-A2.name: digitized MoA extension services and farmers registry

P180334-A3.text: SPS e-Certification system integrated with ePHYTO. Finances digitization of agri-food certificates and licenses via SPS e-Certification linked to ePHYTO. (b) the digitization of agri-food related certificates and licenses, including the establishment of (i) an SPS e-Certification system and integration into the ePHYTO system; (ii) the registration and administration system for food business operators including food exporters;
P180334-A3.name: SPS e-Certification system integrated with ePHYTO

P180076-A1.text: interactive early warning and disaster risk information platform. The project uses an EDRMC-hosted online platform, automated weather stations, SMS and media channels, and an expanded MIS to publish risk profiles and deliver early warnings. Practices: Interactive online platform hosting woreda disaster risk profiles; Multi-hazard impact-based early warning and early action system rollout; Automated weather stations for climate information services; SMS and local media channels for last-mile early warning; expanded MIS linking early warning, GRM SMS and GEMS; Automated woreda disaster risk profiles for contingency planning. Experienced international organizations, such as the International Institute for Rural Reconstruction (IIRR), will facilitate the process and prepare a report using an interactive online platform to be hosted by the EDRMC. To strengthen the early warning and response system, the project will finance the preparation of WDRPs. WDRPs will be prepared or updated (where they already exist) for all 120 of the project woredas in the eight regions and outline the major vulnerabilities of each woreda. (b) support the EDRMC in rolling out the new Multi-Hazard, Impact-Based Early Warning and Early Action System (MH-IB-EW-EAS) roadmap for 2023–2030, in the lowlands, including by helping it develop region-specific implementation plans;
P180076-A1.name: interactive early warning and disaster risk information platform

P180076-A2.text: satellite-based national rangeland monitoring system with community ground-truthing. The project finances a national rangeland monitoring system fusing remote sensing and satellite imagery with community ground-truthing to issue rangeland advisories. Practices: national rangeland monitoring system fusing satellite and ground data; Interactive satellite-based rangeland monitoring system (RMS) integrated with project MIS and digital extension services; National rangeland monitoring system (RMS) synthesizing remote sensing and satellite imagery with community ground-truthing to issue rangeland advisories. The subcomponent will finance the establishment and operationalization of a national RMS that monitors the overall health of national rangeland and related trends. In collaboration with the MoA, Agricultural Transformation Institute (ATI), Alliance Biodiversity International and International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT), and ILRI, the project will develop the system and ensure its capacity to (i) synthesize remote sensing data and leverage it to generate usable products or reports; (ii) conduct ground- truth analysis derived from satellite-based imagery in ways that draw on communities’ insights (including women’s); and (iii) disseminate rangeland-related information and advisories to different users in a timely fashion by leveraging user-friendly digital platforms and public and private delivery channels. (e) seek more technical backstopping from international organizations; and (f) introduce more technologies and innovations, including in the preparation and automation of WDRPs and DPRSIPs (for example, interactive and satellite-based RMS, digital banking and fintech, private and digital extension services, collar-mounted tsetse fly control, adaptation and livelihood resilience tracking tool, and integration of the GEMS Kobo toolbox in the project MIS).
P180076-A2.name: satellite-based national rangeland monitoring system with community ground-truthing

P180076-A3.text: livestock traceability, market information and resilience tracking systems. The project promotes ET-LITS animal traceability, links livestock markets to the DRIVE-supported LMIS, and adapts ILRI's tool to track pastoralist resilience. Practices: Ethiopian Livestock Identification and Traceability System for herds; livestock market information system linked to upgraded markets; Tracking Adaptation in Livestock Systems resilience tool. The subcomponent will collaborate with Subcomponent 3.2 in promoting the Ethiopian Livestock Identification and Traceability System (ET-LITS) for animals of targeted households. (iii) based on a gap assessment, link newly constructed or upgraded livestock markets facilities to the livestock market information system (LMIS) supported by the DRIVE Project (P176517) wherever the projects overlap and finance activities to strength the LMIS in the project regions and woredas including through provision of materials, IT equipment, trainings, and so on; LLRP II will also work with ILRI and AICCRA to increase data quality and adapt the ILRI’s Tracking Adaptation in Livestock Systems tool to track adaptation and resilience to climate change among targeted PAP households.
P180076-A3.name: livestock traceability, market information and resilience tracking systems

P180085-A1.text: satellite, geospatial and digital tools for national statistics production. The project equips statistical offices with satellite imagery, geospatial data, CAPI, drones and open data platforms to modernize survey, census and indicator production. Practices: satellite data and high-frequency phone surveys in statistical offices; Bridge survey experiment for poverty comparability; drone aerial surveys for statistical data collection; electronic platform for enterprise DSF tax-statistical declarations; GIS-based natural resource accounts for Green GDP; CAPI-based CPI price collection replacing paper interviews; Harmonized PHOENIX CPI software adopted across CEMAC countries; Geospatial and remote-sensing climate data collection; UNSD climate indicator questionnaires embedded in national surveys; Geospatial data and satellite imagery for vulnerability mapping; CDR and satellite data for high-frequency poverty and agriculture statistics; NSO call centers repurposed for rapid shock and LFS data collection; national open data system archiving and distributing long time series; online microdata access and query mechanisms; integrated agricultural censuses with geospatial and remote sensing data; CAPI-based data collection with computerized data checking; Upgraded NSO data platforms for archiving and dissemination; Tailored SPI monitoring dashboard with faster score updates; Harmonized UNSD climate questionnaire modules in national surveys and censuses; Geospatial and satellite climate data integration (Google Earth Engine, CHIRPS) for NSOs; Integrated household survey program with geospatial and longitudinal climate modules; Geospatial mapping linking census location data with surveys to identify climate-vulnerable areas; Green data centers certified under IFC EDGE efficiency standard; CAPI-based real-time verification of enumerator performance; Regional emergency observatories for rapid high-frequency data collection; satellite imagery population estimates in cartography phase. Innovative approaches based on satellite data and High Frequency Phone Surveys (HFPS) are now incorporated in the statistics offices’ tools. In that case, the survey design and funding will include a survey experiment which will serve as a bridge survey to allow comparability. In the case of the methodological change between the previous household survey and the new one, it will be challenging to compare the new poverty estimates with past poverty numbers. Participating countries will purchase drones to support survey ac tivities under “innovative technologies”.
P180085-A1.name: satellite, geospatial and digital tools for national statistics production

P180831-A1.text: AI forecasting and outage management for grid operations. The project deploys an AI tool for daily renewable generation forecasting and dispatch plus an outage management system to speed post-disaster grid restoration. Practices: AI-based daily projection and dispatch tool for RE; outage management system for post-disaster grid restoration. RREIIF will finance specifically in this phase (i) tools for operation and planning including, modelling tools to build a more resilient transmission network, such as the installation of an outage management system to more efficiently restore infrastructure after natural disasters, Artificial intelligence-based daily projection and dispatch tool; assistance in building complete model for different islands, (iii) elaboration of standards to improve resilience and training in T&D construction, and (iv) supply and installation of 6 MWh BESS and T&D for the BESS integration in the utility grid as well as SCADA system to monitor RE dispatch.
P180831-A1.name: AI forecasting and outage management for grid operations

P180884-A1.text: geospatial land information systems and digital records for land administration. The project uses CORS networks, satellite imagery, KoBo Toolbox M&E, and digitized land registries to support surveying, hazard modeling, and post-disaster tenure evidence. Practices: CORS network densification for geospatial positioning; Digital M&E system on KoBo Toolbox and geospatial platform for real-time monitoring of project-affected people and assets; Land Information System (LIS) in Wouri and Mfoundi land offices; Satellite imagery and geospatial modeling of climate hazards; Digitized land registry archives with climate risk data; Digitized land records for post-disaster tenure evidence. (v) densify Cameroon’s Continuously Operating Reference Station (CORS) Network; Building on the use of KoBo Toolbox and an electronic platform for land acquisition and resettlement screening, census, and valuation of Page 14 The World Bank Sustainable Cities and Land Project (P180884) affected assets in the preparation of RAPs, the creation of a digital M&E system can support real-time monitoring of implementation progress and project-affected people and assets. GEMS could help build the capacity of the PIU and government agencies to use low-cost, open-source geospatial platforms such as KoBo Toolbox for digital data collection and analysis. The project will use the Geo-Enabling Initiative for Monitoring and Supervision (GEMS).
P180884-A1.name: geospatial land information systems and digital records for land administration

P180872-A1.text: Integrated PFM platform with interoperable modules and cybersecurity architecture. The project builds an integration framework linking IFMIS, payroll, customs and investment systems, adds budget tagging, enterprise architecture and a Security Operations Center. Practices: PFM integration framework and platform linking core IFMIS to other PFM systems; Payroll system migration to SaaS with gender analytics; Integrated customs management platform interoperating with MEF systems; Public investment information management system across project cycle; Integration platform and framework for PFM system interoperability; Modular multi-vendor PFM software linked by common integration framework; Payroll system integration enabling gender-disaggregated pay analysis; Information systems embedding climate screening in public investment appraisal; Security Operations Center at MEF for cybersecurity; Enterprise architecture development for MEF systems; Budget tagging in IFMIS for gender, climate, social inclusion; Security Operations Center at MEF for cyber threat detection; Data governance model and enterprise architecture for PFM systems; New customs administration platform with cargo, clearance and control modules. (ii) design and implementation of the PFM integration framework; and (iii) acquisition and implementation of an integration platform. This subcomponent seeks to improve integration between the core IFMIS and the rest of the PFM ecosystem. Activities include: (i) migration of the payroll management system to a Software as a Service Platform; (iii) integration of the payroll system to the core PFM systems at the MEF; and (iv) development of data analytics tools and reports, including gender reporting on employment and compensation practices in the public sector.
P180872-A1.name: Integrated PFM platform with interoperable modules and cybersecurity architecture

P180872-A2.text: Security operations center and CSIRT for cyberattack response. The project creates a MEF Security Operations Center and CSIRT cell linked to the government-wide CSIRT to detect and respond to cyberattacks. Practices: MEF Security Operations Center and subsidiary CSIRT; SOC and AIG CSIRT cell for cyberattack detection at MEF; Data governance model and enterprise architecture for PFM systems. Activities include: (i) support for the creation and mobilization of a Security Operations Center (SOC) at the MEF, including the provision of office equipment and minor refurbishment works within existing government buildings; (ii) support the creation and mobilization of a cell (subsidiary) CSIRT at the MEF that adheres to the policies and procedures set by the government wide CSIRT at AIG; and (iii) implementation of cybersecurity certification and external audit program. The MEF will strengthen its capabilities to prevent, monitor, detect, and react to cyberattacks in close coordination with AIG. The MEF data protection strategy includes management of historical data, updating and improving the SOC at the MEF, creation of a cell of the AIG CSIRT at the MEF, building internal capacity and implementing an external auditing program.
P180872-A2.name: Security operations center and CSIRT for cyberattack response

P181248-A1.text: Displacement tracking data and spatial IDP database for targeting. Uses IOM displacement tracking data and a national spatial IDP registration database to select target areas and beneficiaries. Practices: IOM-DTM displacement data for targeting IDP beneficiaries; National spatial IDP database from registration and displacement surveys. The International Organization for Migration (IOM)-Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) data will be considered to select the target communities at the LGA and ward levels.22 IOM-DTM data will be the basis for the identification of project beneficiaries. MDAs = Ministries, Departments, and Agencies. (ii) financial and technical support to address the data gaps concerning IDPs, including women, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups; and (iii) financial and technical support to carry out a registration and profiling process of IDPs, including conducting the displacement surveys elaborated in the PIM and building a spatial database for IDPs in participating states that identify IDPs as one of their key development challenges.45 States will finance the state-level work while the project will finance the coordination of the states’ efforts and the development of a national database. The component will also allocate US$2 F ’ operationalize the National IDP Policy, including the following: (i) TA to facilitate overall programmatic and policy coordination between federal, state, and local governments;
P181248-A1.name: Displacement tracking data and spatial IDP database for targeting

P181248-A2.text: Geo-Enabled Monitoring System for project monitoring and feedback. Project uses GEMS plus beneficiary feedback/GRM to monitor activities and capture complaints. (ii) project monitoring which includes a Geo-Enabled Monitoring System (GEMS) and beneficiary feedback/Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), including a specialized GRM for cases of SEA/SH;
P181248-A2.name: Geo-Enabled Monitoring System for project monitoring and feedback

P181248-A3.text: Geotagged activity mapping in GEMS with beneficiary phone surveys. State PCUs map activities and collect data via GEMS, complemented by geotagging and beneficiary phone surveys. The state PCUs will be responsible for operationalizing the state-level Results Framework and results monitoring system and leveraging GEMS for activity mapping and data collection. Data collection through geotagging will be supported by regular beneficiary phone surveys to track social cohesion, levels of participation in project activities, satisfaction, and so on. The World Bank project team will provide support to state PCUs in using GEMS in Fragility, Conflict, and Violence (FCV)-sensitive areas to ensure data collection can proceed and be verified.
P181248-A3.name: Geotagged activity mapping in GEMS with beneficiary phone surveys

P502128-A1.text: Teacher database as a GPE results-financing disbursement trigger. Creates a teacher database, a disbursement trigger under GPE results financing (b) the creation of a database on teachers (US$3.50 million in total); and (c) the recruitment and integration of 1,500 teachers each year into public service from 2024 to 2028 (US$3.69 million). Three triggers that unlock this part of the financing have already been agreed with the government: (a) the recruitment of statisticians at the level of the central administration and academic inspections to guarantee reliable data collection;
P502128-A1.name: Teacher database as a GPE results-financing disbursement trigger

P181174-A1.text: Digital credentialing, assessment and career information platforms for students. Deploys blockchain micro-credentials, digital assessment and career information systems to certify competencies and guide student choices. Practices: Blockchain-backed micro-credentials for student employability skills; Classroom diagnostic tools with preventive early-warning protocol; National virtual learning platform with unified LMS and competency certification; Agile digital assessment platform with automated item bank; Blockchain-based micro-credentials for student competencies; Online information system on technical career rates of return; Digital formative assessment information system for classrooms; Career information digital platform for technical students; Digital micro-credentials for English proficiency certification; Digital career information platform for technical secondary students. 23 23 The Project will support block-chain backed micro-credentials (these are authenticated digital certificates, with the block-chain ensuring the authenticity). The information infrastructure and outreach to employers required to bring micro-credentials into regular use is an end in itself as a precursor to a digitally founded lifelong learning trajectory for students. Indicator 4: Percentage of technical stream secondary education students with micro-credentials registering English proficiency (all these indicators will be disaggregated by gender and by indigenous and refugee/migrant status). This component includes the following: (i) Diagnostic tools for the classroom that will provide a teacher with an accurate understanding of the level of literacy and numeracy of each student and of the classroom as a whole - the diagnostic will help the teacher understand objectively the need for learning recovery from school disruptions and other causes as well as a preventive early-warning protocol to help prevent students falling behind in the future;
P181174-A1.name: Digital credentialing, assessment and career information platforms for students

P181174-A2.text: Modular interoperable education systems and teacher development app. Builds MEP systems as interoperable micro-services with RESTful APIs and a teacher app generating real-time usage statistics. Practices: Modular micro-services and RESTful API architecture for MEP systems; My Foundational Learning professional development app for teachers. A modular approach towards the building of Information Systems will ensure steady functionality improvements, while avoiding the risks of waiting for a single giant system architecture. Drawbacks like different identification numbers for schools can be fixed through a disciplined development of inter- operable systems, using compatible micro-services and RESTful API architecture (Representational State Transfer Application Programming Infrastructure). Student fronting systems will be prioritized, together with systems that have an end purpose of transparency in the use of public funds. P181174-A2.name: Modular interoperable education systems and teacher development app

P505158-A1.text: digital platforms for youth employment and entrepreneurship services. The project uses online application, e-learning, job intermediation and MIS platforms, plus possible machine-learning growth predictors, to select, train and place youth. Practices: Online application platform with entrepreneurial aptitude test for preselection; Enhanced INEFOP MIS tracking implementation progress and beneficiaries; E-learning platform delivering employability training; INEFOP portal for youth job placement intermediation; INEFOP e-learning platform for online skills training; Machine-learning predictors of firm growth to complement business plan analysis. Digital tools to be adopted in this phase will include a website and IT platform to manage receipt of applications through an online questionnaire and development or adoption of a simple test measuring entrepreneurial aptitude to facilitate preselection. INEFOP will enhance its computerized Management Information System (MIS) to incorporate additional features that track implementation progress. P505158-A2.text: pilot connecting youth to gig jobs and microtasks. Pilots access to gig jobs and microtasks for 5,000 youth at CINFOTEC Talatona and Huambo. Finally, this subcomponent includes the promotion of access to technology-based digital jobs (such as gig jobs and microtasks) as part of a pilot project at CINFOTEC in Talatona and Huambo. This pilot intervention aims to benefit 5,000 youth by offering them new opportunities in the rapidly growing digital economy. This pilot intervention will evaluate the feasibility of scaling digital job access in other regions, paving the way for more youth to participate in the global digital economy.
P505158-A2.name: pilot connecting youth to gig jobs and microtasks

P505158-A3.text: Platform connecting young entrepreneurs to additional funding opportunities, built under the systems-strengthening component. Creates a platform linking young entrepreneurs with additional funding opportunities. It will standardize processes, automate tasks, enhance the LMIS (Labor Market Observatory and INEFOP Portal) to provide information to various stakeholders and monitor impact across interventions, implement energy-efficient technologies in INEFOP centers, and support other components as needed, including creating a platform to connect young entrepreneurs with additional funding opportunities.
P505158-A3.name: Platform connecting young entrepreneurs to additional funding opportunities, built under the systems-strengthening component

P504629-A1.text: DHIS2 rollout and meteorological data integration into EWARS surveillance. The project reactivates and rolls out DHIS2 at health facilities and hospitals, and adds weather data to EWARS to link climate with outbreaks. Practices: DHIS2 rollout at project health facilities; DHIS2 rollout at selected hospitals and referral centers; Meteorological data integrated into EWARS outbreak alert system; Meteorological data integration into EWARS outbreak surveillance. UNICEF will be responsible for: (a) oversight and coordination of health services and information systems, including reactivation and rollout of District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2) at project facilities; The WHO will be responsible for: (a) oversight and coordination of health services and information systems including reactivation and rollout of DHIS2 at selected hospitals/first level referral centers; (f) climate change risk communication activities to highly climate vulnerable communities; and (g) integration of meteorologic data into the Early Warning, Alert, and Response System (EWARS) to better understand the relationship between outbreak prone infectious diseases and climate change. Page 46 of 49 The World Bank Sudan Health Assistance and Response to Emergencies (P504629) Subcomponent Climate activity • Climate change risk communication activities to highly climate-vulnerable communities will provide information on climate and health, focusing on climate shock emergency preparedness and response and the health impacts of climate change and how to reduce these to remote, highly climate-vulnerable populations. • Integration of meteorologic data into EWARS to better understand the relationship between outbreak-prone infectious diseases and climate change will expand EWARS to include meteorological data.
P504629-A1.name: DHIS2 rollout and meteorological data integration into EWARS surveillance

P504629-A2.text: Telemedicine, tele-consultation and AI e-learning for health workers. The project deploys tele-consultation platforms with patient feedback and an AI-driven e-learning platform to train and support primary health care workers. Practices: Telemedicine for referral hospital service delivery; Tele-consultation platform with patient feedback collection; AI-driven e-learning platform for PHC worker capacity building; Tele-consultation digital health platform with climate-vulnerable rollout. (f) support to vaccination campaigns to reach under-vaccinated populations and raise awareness about its benefits; and (g) implementation of telemedicine where possible. (b) a platform dedicated to digital health services, providing tele-consultations for patients and collecting valuable feedback from patients on the availability and quality of services; and (c) an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven platform specifically designed for capacity building and continuous e-learning for PHC workers. (b) dedicated mechanisms for communications during emergencies; and (c) priority rollout to climate change-vulnerable areas, to be identified based on climate vulnerability maps. • The digital health services platform for patient tele-consultations will embed the following: (a) dedicated plans to ensure additional capacity for consultations during periods when road transport is not possible and the need for remote consultations is higher due to climate shocks and flooding; (b) dedicated mechanisms for health workers to respond to emergency needs to due to climate shocks or climate change (that is, flood based injuries and outbreaks of climate-sensitive diseases) during emergencies; and (c) priority rollout to areas vulnerable to climate change, to be identified based on climate vulnerability maps. • The AI-driven platform for PHC worker capacity building and e-learning will embed (a) training on climate change emergency response and the health impacts of climate change (based on the curriculum developed in Subcomponent 1.3) and (b) priority rollout to areas vulnerable to climate change, to be identified based on climate vulnerability maps.
P504629-A2.name: Telemedicine, tele-consultation and AI e-learning for health workers

P504629-A3.text: Digital communication and GEMS real-time third-party monitoring platforms. The project uses a multi-directional digital platform linking health workers to supervisors and GEMS to give near-real-time access to third-party monitoring field data. Practices: Multi-directional digital platform linking health workers to senior levels; GEMS platform for near-real-time third-party monitoring field data; GEMS platform for real-time third-party monitoring field data. This subcomponent will include support to the following: (a) a multi-directional digital platform to strengthen health system governance to facilitate seamless and instant communication, interaction, networking, and feedback between health workers and their respective senior levels; Page 23 of 49 The World Bank Sudan Health Assistance and Response to Emergencies (P504629) GEMS will enable the World Bank to “monitor the monitors” and get access to direct field data in near real time rather than solely receiving aggregated periodic reports. Using GEMS, the project will seek to further build the local capacity to use technologies to collect and analyze data on the ground to improve accountability for TPM and enhance transparency and accuracy of M&E activities. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the TPM agent, the project will integrate support from GEMS.
P504629-A3.name: Digital communication and GEMS real-time third-party monitoring platforms

P504629-A4.text: Joint data dashboards and multi-directional governance platform. The project combines EWARS, DHIS2 and TPM data into joint dashboards and finances a platform linking facilities, leaders, patients and workers. Practices: Joint data analysis and dashboards across EWARS, DHIS2 and TPM; Multi-directional digital platform for health system governance. The organizations will collect and analyze data from relevant sources, including EWARS, DHIS2, Health Resources and Service Availability Monitoring System, TPM, and other data sets. The three organizations will jointly develop knowledge management products (for example, journal articles, briefs, and dashboards) and will also work closely with the TPM agency to ensure high-quality data collection that will inform data analysis. Subcomponent 1.5: This subcomponent will finance digital activities to support improved communications between Integrating Digital health facilities and senior leaders, patients and health facilities, and health workers and Solutions to Service learning platforms. This will embed concrete and structured mechanisms to respond to climate change-based needs as follows: • The multi-directional platform to strengthen health system governance will embed the following: (a) dedicated plans to ensure enhanced support for health care workers during the rainy season and climate shocks, with consideration of greater needs for communication via electronic platforms during periods when road transport is not possible and emergency response needs are higher due to climate shocks and flooding;
P504629-A4.name: Joint data dashboards and multi-directional governance platform

P506142-A1.text: digital extension and remote-sensing GHG monitoring for climate-smart agriculture. The project uses digital agricultural extension tools and remote-sensing mapped production areas with local emission factors to monitor greenhouse gases and spread climate-smart technologies. Practices: Digital ATER (digital agricultural extension) tools for disseminating CSA technologies to family farmers and technicians; remote-sensing GHG emission monitoring for production chains. The component has four main activities: (a) foster agrifood climate-smart innovations, through activities such as research and development on CSA26, GHG emissions monitoring, monitoring of climate changes in the State, water resilience practices and extension services and trainings towards family farmers and agricultural technicians to foster the dissemination and adoption of CSA technologies, including through digital tools (e.g. Digital ATER). Methodology for The indicator is counted when the system is available to end users, In the final evaluation, quantify the number of accesses Data Collection to the systems used by farmers and the reduction of the time in the procedures (collect baseline data, if possible) Responsibility for SAR, EPAGRI Data Collection Structuring the State's Greenhouse Gas emission monitoring system in the State's priority production chains The GHG monitoring system will consist of 1) Determination of local emission factors in the livestock, grains, horticulture and Description fruit production chains (measured on site); 2) Production areas determined through remote sensing mapping technology;
P506142-A1.name: digital extension and remote-sensing GHG monitoring for climate-smart agriculture

P506142-A2.text: Digital business platform matching demand and supply of environmental assets. Project supports a digital platform linking buyers and sellers of environmental assets to create a PES market. 29 Financing through the PES will support recovery of degraded areas, recovery of Permanent Preservation Areas, conservation of natural areas, support for the development of PES projects, support for the development of carbon projects, and development and implementation of a digital business platform for the dissemination of information and the link between demand and supply of environmental assets, enabling the creation of a market.
P506142-A2.name: Digital business platform matching demand and supply of environmental assets

P506142-A3.text: integrated agricultural information systems and data warehouse for policy monitoring. The project expands the SIIA agricultural information system and builds a data warehouse linking state databases and public policy systems to monitor policy implementation and emissions. Practices: Expanded SIIA agricultural information system for policy monitoring; integrated data warehouse linking state agri information systems. The Component has four main activities: (a) support the provision and analysis of data on the agrifood system and on natural resources management to provide accurate information for the elaboration of public policies and programs, through the expansion of the Integrated Agricultural Information System (Sistema Integrado de Informações Agrícolas - SIIA31) and the development of new systems to monitor the implementation of public policies and programs through diagnostics and analyses on the various challenges the agrifood system is facing. Collected data will include exposure to major climate threats (droughts/floods in particular), GHG emissions factor per region as well as the implementation of a monitoring system for GHG emissions within the agrifood system in the State.32 Those analyses will be shared with the other states participating in the MPA as part of its Learning Agenda; Methodology for Preparation stages and Publication in the official journal Data Collection Responsibility for SAR, EPAGRI Data Collection Structuring public policy management and monitoring systems (Number) The project will support the development and evolution of at least 7 information systems. 4_Data Warehouse (database integration) - SAR/SEE;
P506142-A3.name: integrated agricultural information systems and data warehouse for policy monitoring

P505923-A1.text: national digital forest information, traceability and MRV systems. The project deploys and upgrades digital forest information, timber traceability and MRV systems to verify legality, monitor carbon and biodiversity, and share data in real time. Practices: national wood traceability and legality verification systems; digital MRV for forest inventories and carbon data; geospatial tools for biodiversity and forest status monitoring; Piloted satellite connectivity and digital MRV for forest monitoring; Digital NTFP statistics application for data collection and monitoring; SIGIF 2.0 forest information system with real-time data sharing; Third multi-resource National Forest Inventory with MRV software; Forest Information and Management System for coverage assessment; SIVL digital timber legality and traceability system modules; National forest inventory, monitoring system and forest cadaster; Earth observation, data analytics and AI for regional forest and biodiversity monitoring; SIGIF 2.0 and SIVL timber traceability systems for legality verification; Forest Information System for carbon stock and deforestation monitoring in CAR. Subcomponent 1.2: Traceability, Certification, and Information Systems. National traceability and legality verification systems will be improved to facilitate the entry of legally sourced timber into domestic and export markets and to update forest inventories for more accurate management planning. Financial support will be allocated for (i) hardware, software, and technical expertise for the development of forest inventories and data on forest carbon, where feasible, using digital Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV); and (ii) improved traceability and legality verification systems, including equipment, connectivity, hardware, software, training, and support for SMEs. Investments will be aligned with the needs identified in each management plan and may encompass habitat restoration, biodiversity and forest status monitoring using geospatial tools and community engagement;
P505923-A1.name: national digital forest information, traceability and MRV systems

P505923-A2.text: B2B e-commerce platform for timber and NTFP SMEs. Project acquires and manages a B2B e-commerce platform to market and sell SME wood and NTFP products. (c) acquire and manage a B2B e-commerce platform for marketing and sales; and (d) support business structuring, sustainable eco-management, production optimization, marketing, and accounting. (iv) Support market discovery and sales of new products: (a) facilitate access to national, regional, and international markets for SMEs in the timber and NTFPs sectors through B2B matchmaking, business promotion, and showcasing local products;
P505923-A2.name: B2B e-commerce platform for timber and NTFP SMEs

P506528-A1.text: individual electronic free health care system rollout. Project finances rollout of electronic free health care records to keep services running amid insecurity According to Doctors Without Borders, more than 500 health facilities had closed or were operating at minimal capacity as of 2023.59 Under Component 2, the project will support the rollout of the individual electronic free health care system to enhance access to health services. The system will ensure business continuity by preventing loss of data records and ensuring citizens and healthcare workers can complete services online.
P506528-A1.name: individual electronic free health care system rollout

P506422-A1.text: geospatial portfolio monitoring with mobile data collection for M&E. Uses GEMS geospatial monitoring and Kobo Toolbox smartphone tools to capture progress data in text, images and geocodes for real-time portfolio supervision. Practices: GEMS geospatial monitoring for portfolio supervision; Kobo Toolbox mobile data collection for real-time M&E. (iv) investments in emerging technologies for innovative solutions to improve operational efficiency and monitoring through Geo-Enabling Initiative for Monitoring and Supervision (GEMS) and other approaches; and (v) financing the operations of the CIUs and CSAs including technical surge support through the transition period. Through GEMS, the project will support the governments to digitize data collection and M&E processes and enhance real-time monitoring. More specifically, under GEMS, the Bank will provide technical advice and work to develop customized data collection tools and approaches based on open-source platforms (for example, Kobo Toolbox) that will allow for capturing data on implementation progress in multiple formats (for example, text, numbers, images, geocodes) via simple technologies such as smartphones or tablets, allowing for increased adaptive capacity to respond to climate challenges being addressed through the project portfolio.
P506422-A1.name: geospatial portfolio monitoring with mobile data collection for M&E

P506422-A2.text: cloud contract registry with e-signatures for contract execution. Deploys a shared cloud-based contract registry and e-signatures between departments to speed inter-departmental contract signing and execution. Practices: Cloud-based contract registry across CIU and ministries; E-signatures for inter-departmental contract execution. Implement streamlined contract registry across all CIU and experiences. ministries via cloud-based software. ii. E-signatures for contract signings between departments for execution.
P506422-A2.name: cloud contract registry with e-signatures for contract execution

P506551-A1.text: Nationwide digitalization of higher education administrative processes. Scales digitalization of administrative and management processes across universities and ministry, building on TEEP pilot (US$10 million) will support the digital transformation of the higher education and scientific research system. This will entail expanding the digitalization of all administrative and management processes nationwide, at both central and institutional levels. It will build on the digitalization effort piloted under the TEEP project and advance the implementation of MOHESR's digital transformation strategy roadmap to digitalize higher education and research administrative systems and platforms.
P506551-A1.name: Nationwide digitalization of higher education administrative processes

P506551-A2.text: digital university platforms for virtual mobility, services and AI orientation. Funds virtual labs, distance learning, digitalized admissions, scholarships, assessments and research databases, plus AI labor-market orientation for students. Practices: Virtual labs and distance learning infrastructure for inter-university mobility; Digitalized university service systems: career guidance, simulators, digital assessments, admissions, research proposal/scholarship systems and centralized research database; Digitalized registration, scholarship management and diploma certification systems; Virtual labs and distance learning for inter-university virtual mobility; AI-assisted student orientation system projecting labor market trends. Building on a successful pilot under TEEP that digitalized registration, scholarship management, and diploma certification, it will provide funding for more institutions to acquire equipment and software for virtual labs and distance learning. Enhanced digital infrastructure will support remote learning, ensure continuity during climate-related disruptions, and facilitate inter- university virtual mobilities, enabling experienced professors from coastal universities to teach students in interior institutions remotely. Description The list of services might include, but not be limited to: i) students accessing enhanced digital career guidance system; ii) students benefiting from digitally-enabled training such as simulators; iii) students benefiting from innovative ditially enabled assessment methods; iv) students that enroll into courses using newly digitalized admissions systems; iv) students that use newly established or improved digital research proposal or scholarship systems ; vi) university teachers who use the centralized research database. The list of digitally enabled services will be defined in the MOP.
P506551-A2.name: digital university platforms for virtual mobility, services and AI orientation

P506551-A3.text: Nationwide digitalization of higher education administrative and management processes. Finances digitalization of all administrative and management processes across central and institutional levels of higher education Support the digital Support the development of Adaptation: The development of the systems digital infrastructure will help enhance remote learning and ensure transformation of the higher the system digital learning continuity in the face of climate-related disruptions (such as extreme heat in the interior regions or the high education and scientific research infrastructure and increase the vulnerability to floods of costal universities). system number of procedures done online Mitigation: The digitalization of all administrative and management processes for higher education and scientific (US$10 million) research nationwide, at both central and institutional levels that is supported through this subcomponent constitutes the first transformation of its kind in the country. This subcomponent will reduce GHG emissions by expanding digitalization across all administrative processes, cutting paper use and minimizing physical trips to educational centers.
P506551-A3.name: Nationwide digitalization of higher education administrative and management processes

P506691-A1.text: interoperable digital government platforms and analytics for statistics, tax, planning and audit. The project builds interoperable data platforms, analytics tools and automated systems across statistics, revenue, planning, procurement and audit agencies to digitize government processes. Practices: Integrated National Statistical System with interoperable open data ecosystem; Advanced data analytics tools digitizing the government data life cycle; web-based data dissemination platform for microdata and indicators; data analytics and automation system for tax administration; end-to-end automated income tax business processes; interoperable revenue administration systems architecture; automated taxpayer call center; upgraded PPS platform integrated with e-PMIS; microservices-based unified planning platform with analytics; MYPIP/GCR tools embedded in upgraded PPS; API interoperability between PPS, AMS and e-PMIS; e-GP enhancements for OCDS compliance and budget integration; cloud-ready microservices e-GP 2.0 deployment study; FIMA digital campus / virtual learning hub with sector-specific digital content for OCAG auditor professionalization; API-based interoperable audit data infrastructure with AI audit; Centralized data analytics tool integrated with five government IT systems; Blockchain-based audit interface for decentralized auditees; Real-time AI/ML audit and e-vouching verification; IT audit system interfacing with e-GP procurement data; Digital platform integrated with iBAS++ for financial statements; digital microdata downloads from BBS platforms; digitized Project Preparation and Appraisal System integrated with Planning Division IT; website analytics tracking microdata downloads from BBS; CAAT and AI/ML-based audit analytics interfaced with government IT systems. Subcomponent 1.1.1 (US$6 million) aims to integrate official statistics into the government’s digital data agenda by establishing an integrated NSS that produces and enables sharing and use of reliable official statistics to improve policy making and service delivery and (b) supporting a transparent data ecosystem by ensuring that key data are open, accessible, and interoperable. This component, to be implemented by BBS, complements the transparency reforms supported by the SGIR DPC through the adoption of digital data ecosystems and statistical capacity enhancement and modernization. This objective will be achieved through (a) investing in advanced data analytical tools to improve the use of indicators and microdata across government and tap into new data sources to produce next-generation indicators and microdata and support the integration of data sources and the application of data analytics to digitize the data life cycle and (b) enhancing coordination and data governance across agencies and strengthen and clarify roles and responsibilities around Governmentwide data leadership.6 Building on existing memorandums of understanding (MoUs) with administrative data-producing agencies within the NSS, the project will operationalize and enhance the efficacy of data sharing across these agencies while also establishing new MoUs with additional agencies. (c) improving data dissemination platforms for timely and regularly updated web-based access to statistical publications, microdata, and time series indicators;9 (d) establishing mechanisms for systematic citizen engagement through user- producer dialogue, including organizing Data Users Forums to monitor and promote improved data transparency and access; and (e) supporting statistical capacity building at the division, zilla, and upazila levels to meet the growing demand for subnational economic statistics.
P506691-A1.name: interoperable digital government platforms and analytics for statistics, tax, planning and audit

P506691-A3.text: OCDS-format open procurement data with analytics. Publishes procurement data in OCDS format and applies analytics to track system performance and bidder quality. To improve transparency, the project will support better collection, maintenance, analysis, and dissemination of public procurement data and information to the government, civil society, private sector, and citizens at large in OCDS format which will leverage advanced data analytics in procurement to track and measure performance of the public procurement system. This open contracting approach will make the procurement processes and outcome transparent to Page 11 The World Bank Strengthening Institutions for Transparency and Accountability (SITA) (P506691) the public. It would also facilitate analysis of bidder’s performance and quality of the product/service.
P506691-A3.name: OCDS-format open procurement data with analytics

P507209-A1.text: integrated national digital health information and surveillance systems. The project deploys interoperable health information, surveillance, laboratory, emergency and telemedicine systems to track patients and threats nationwide. Practices: Integrated One Health digital surveillance system for human and animal health; Nationwide electronic medical records for continuous patient monitoring; Telemedicine and tele-appointment systems for underserved areas; Integrated pre-hospital and hospital coordination system with bed management; Integrated early warning system consolidating health, animal and environmental data; Laboratory Information Management System for test result tracking and sharing; AI pattern-recognition diagnostics and point-of-care testing in labs; National PHC management information system deployment; Multi-level PHC indicator dashboard from health information system; Mobile and telemedicine services for primary care CSBs; Integrated health MIS with data-protection-by-design; CSB connectivity for DMI and EVAX vaccine tracing; National health identifier for interoperable health MIS; Integrated DMI, e-pharmacy and cold-chain systems at CSB; Computer-aided dispatch with priority algorithms and real-time GIS; Automated ambulance fleet management system; Emergency department triage information system; Bed management information system for patient transfers; Geo-mapping analysis of climate-vulnerable health access disparities; Early warning systems for emerging infectious diseases; National information system for medical equipment lifecycle management; bed management system in hospitals; PHC information systems deployed in CSBs; laboratory information system scaled to regional hospitals and CSBs; national disease surveillance and response management system; GIS geomapping of emergency service 30-minute coverage; unique ID system connecting CSB patient records; national integrated surveillance system capturing all cases; PHC information systems (DMI, Evax, ePharmacie, HRH) in health centers; hospital bed management system across 33 hospitals; climate-sensitive disease early warning system linked to shock alerts; geomapping methodology for climate-vulnerable PHC access planning; digitized medical records and EVAX immunization system at PHC; CHVA-data-driven pre-hospitalization and SMUR coverage design; Digitized bed management system for specialized care. Component 1 focuses on strengthening health system resilience to protect citizens' health through the implementation of an integrated One Health surveillance system for both human and animal health. This digital approach enables better monitoring and response to health threats, directly supporting the PNS goal of citizen protection. Within this component, digital health serves as a key enabler: telemedicine development facilitating specialized care access in underserved areas; nationwide electronic medical records implementation for continuous patient monitoring; generalized tele-appointment systems across health establishments; and digitalization of frontline structures including electronic medical records for chronic disease management and vaccination tracking. Component 3 reinforces emergency and hospital services by implementing a coordination system for pre-hospital and hospital services that integrates bed management.
P507209-A1.name: integrated national digital health information and surveillance systems

P507209-A2.text: emergency operations centres and electronic patient grievance platform. The project upgrades public health emergency operations centres and adds an electronic platform for patients to report and track complaints. Practices: National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre with regional satellites; e-people electronic grievance platform at PHC level. This subcomponent aims to improve the existing system for coordination and preparedness, and response and efforts in the event of a public health emergency, currently embedded with the SHOCROOM. The SHOCROOM will be 19 The exact Pandemic Fund financing amount is US$17.16 million Page 7 established by the Government as Tunisia’s National PHEOC along with its 6 regional satellites. This subcomponent will build the institutional capacity of the PHEOC through the following key activities: • Enhancing Capacity: Upgrading both the central and regional infrastructure through investments in hardware, software, and communication systems. Baseline is measured in accordance with the scope of this Data Collection project at inception Responsibility for MOH-DSSB and CIMS Page 30 The World Bank Tunisia Health System Strengthening Project (P507209) Data Collection Component 2: Supporting reorganization of preventive and primary health services percentage of grievences received and adressed through the electronic platform at the PHC level This indicator measures the proportion of complaints and issues reported by patients that have been successfully Description resolved Frequency Annual Data source Annual report of Bureau de relation avec les citoyens (BRC) using the platform e-people Methodology for Annual report of Bureau de relation avec les citoyens (BRC) using the platform e-people.
P507209-A2.name: emergency operations centres and electronic patient grievance platform

P507865-A1.text:
digital assessment and EMIS for tracking learning outcomes and out-of-school children. The project builds digital classroom assessment, an upgraded Shiksha Setu EMIS and digitized student records to track learning, flag dropouts and reach out-of-school children. Practices: Digitally enabled classroom assessment system for literacy and numeracy milestones; Enhanced Shiksha Setu EMIS tracking learning outcomes and dropout early warning; Digitized student and household records for out-of-school mobilization and tracking. The project will support: (i) the development of a digitally enabled classroom assessment system
to capture age-appropriate milestones for literacy (such as letter name and sound knowledge, vocabulary, oral reading
fluency and comprehension) and numeracy development for different stages of primary education; The assessment and analysis tools will utilize advanced analytics to enable real-
time monitoring and insights to improve program design and delivery. Shiksha Setu, the state's EMIS, will be enhanced to align with
the Vidya Samiksha Kendra guidelines issued by the Ministry of Education, GoI. Enhancements will include: (i) tracking of
student learning outcomes data collected through periodic formative assessments, annual summative assessments, and
other state level assessments;
P507865-A1.name: digital assessment and EMIS for tracking learning outcomes and out-of-school children

P508313-A1.text: PLP EdTech platform with AI language model for teachers. Project expands the PLP digital learning platform to all primary schools and integrates an AI language model to assist teachers. BEIP will leverage this work and support expanding the use of the PLP EdTech platform to all primary schools and further integrate the AI language model to assist teachers. The PLP is a learning platform that provides digital learning content aligned with the national curriculum. Teachers can assign tasks, monitor student progress, provide feedback, create additional content, and communicate with parents through the platform.
P508313-A1.name: PLP EdTech platform with AI language model for teachers

P508698-A1.text: regional systems-change dashboard for WASH sector reform tracking. A regional dashboard monitors WASH systems-change indicators across participating countries, supported by AUDA-NEPAD capacity building, to track sector reform. Practices: Systems change dashboard for WASH sector reform tracking; Regional systems-change dashboard tracking WASH sector transformation. The AUDA-NEPAD, the implementing agency for the regional phases, will provide support to capacity building, the systems change dashboard, and partnerships with civil society and other non-state stakeholders for Pillar 1 activities. The Project will support the regional dashboard for sector transformation (that is, Systems Change) , governance reforms, institutional capacities and regulations and service delivery improvements. 41 Specifically, the Agriculture, Rural Development, Blue Economy and Sustainable Environment department.
P508698-A1.name: regional systems-change dashboard for WASH sector reform tracking

P508698-A2.text: Regional WASH benchmarking dashboard with systems-change KPIs. Finances a regional dashboard tracking WASH systems-change KPIs and an online knowledge platform for MPA countries. This will include, among others, i) the development of a regional benchmarking dashboard with KPIs for WASH systems change monitoring, ii) support for capacity building and annual data collection and analysis of KPIs, iii) support to organize high-level events and engagement activities to review progress on the WASH acceleration agenda, including ministerial WASH summits and head of states engagement activities during AU summits, iv) support for regional civil society forums and capacity building of civil society organizations to strengthen effective dialogue on WASH at national level, and iv) technical assistance, workshops and training to develop an on-line knowledge platform, hosted by the AIP-Water Secretariat, v) the implementation of peer-learning activities for countries in the AFE region, including, South-South knowledge exchanges and multi-country learning events These knowledge exchanges will showcase best practices in areas such as PPPs utility transformation, rural water sustainability, a and urban sanitation governance. Subcomponent 1.1: Regional Benchmarking on Systems Change and Knowledge Platform for WASH (US$1.5 million).This subcomponent will finance activities to carry out regional benchmarking, complementing the AIP-Water Scorecard46 to monitor performance of countries in AFE region on implementing the systems change approach for WASH through a series of KPIs47 and to engage high-level decision makers at regional level to pursue the WASH systems change and acceleration agenda. The regional benchmarking activities and the digital knowledge platform will be implemented by AUDA-NEPAD through contracting the GWP-SA48 as Secretariat for AIP-Water.
P508698-A2.name: Regional WASH benchmarking dashboard with systems-change KPIs

P508698-A3.text: digital monitoring, benchmarking and verification platforms for water utilities and dams. Digital platforms, GIS analysis and remote dashboards collect, benchmark and verify utility, dam and groundwater data to improve performance and investment oversight. Practices: Digital benchmarking platform (NewIBNET) for utility performance; RUWASA data monitoring and visualization platform for CBWSO performance reporting; RUWASA digital monitoring platform for O&M data submission; MIS cataloging dams' safety and operational data; GIS census analysis to verify population served per water point; Geolocated timestamped photos verifying scheme investments; data monitoring and visualization platform for CBWSO performance reporting; live remote monitoring dashboard for PPP scheme verification; national groundwater information system with aquifer mapping. This subcomponent finances: i) technical assistance to enhance the participation of utilities/service providers in countries in the AFE region in a digital benchmarking platform (NewIBNET 51 ) to improve data-driven decision making, share best practices and performance metrics, improving data integrity and reliability, and enhance skills in data management and analytics, ii) capacity development for utilities in the Eastern and Southern region through regional training programs, with a focus among others on utility turnaround, leadership development, customer and community engagement, digitalization, regulation and climate resilient service delivery, iii) technical assistance and training for the development of PIAPs for utilities in the MPA participating countries, including adequate citizen feedback mechanisms, iv) technical assistance for utilities to carry out gender equality diagnostics52 and adopt management practices to improve gender equality, and v) technical assistance for the MPA participating countries to develop strategic plans and actionable roadmaps to enhance professional management and sustainability of rural water operators, including through private sector 7-7: Enhanced Water Services Delivery Data Management and Reporting: RUWASA has published on annual reports, for at least 4 years of the Program, the performance and financial data collected monthly from CBWSOs through the data monitoring and visualization platform under the RUWASA Service Delivery and Management System. Frequency Annual reporting during implementation Data source Digital system usage logs, CBWSO data submission records, RUWASA monitoring dashboards Methodology for Data is extracted from the RUWASA digital monitoring platform, which tracks submission Data Collection frequency, completeness, and accuracy of O&M data. CBWSOs are required to submit data on Page 67 Official Use Only The World Bank Sustainable Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Program Phase 2 (P508698) key indicators such as system functionality, revenue collection, and maintenance activities.
P508698-A3.name: digital monitoring, benchmarking and verification platforms for water utilities and dams

P508698-A4.text: Public CBWSO performance and financial data visualization platform. RUWASA publishes CBWSO performance and financial data via a digital monitoring and visualization platform. Responsibility for RUWASA Data Collection CBWSOs for which RUWASA has published in annual reports, for at least 4 years of the Program, their performance and financial data (Number) This indicator measures the number of CBWSOs for which RUWASA has published in annual reports, for at least 4 years of the Program, the performance and financial data, through the data Description monitoring and visualization platform under the Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Service Delivery and Management System, according to DLR 7-7. It reflects the institutionalization of digital tools for performance monitoring and decision-making in rural water service delivery.
P508698-A4.name: Public CBWSO performance and financial data visualization platform

P509488-A1.text: fiber-optic SCADA/EMS and automated metering for regional grid control. The project deploys fiber-optic communication, SCADA/EMS, automated load-frequency control and metering data systems to enable real-time cross-border grid monitoring, balancing and trading. Practices: Learning-pilot market platform generating transaction data to calibrate algorithms; fiber-optic cables on transmission lines for SCADA/EMS; Fiber optic cable on regional transmission lines; Automated grid stabilization and metering systems; Automated Commercial Metered Data Management System for regional trading; Regional fiber optic network for energy market services; Optical fiber on 220-500 kV lines for real-time grid management; Fiber optic networks along new transmission lines; Advanced metering infrastructure and automated metering data management; Automated load-frequency control and contingency management tools; Automatic Load-Frequency Control for regional grid stability. Phase 1 is a deliberate learning pilot that generates the technical, operational, and behavioral evidence to refine market design in Phases 2 and 3. By standing up a simplified regional platform and core “soft” rules (governance, scheduling, settlement) alongside “hard” enablers (automated metering/MDMS, grid digitalization, fiber communications), Phase 1 produces real transaction, performance, and user‑experience data to calibrate product scope, algorithms, and standards. These lessons are codified into Phase 2 entry conditions and milestones, guiding the advanced day‑ahead/intraday market design and, subsequently, the fuller market (including regional balancing) in Phase 3—ensuring solutions are Central Asia‑fit before scaling. These lines will be equipped with fiber optic cables that will facilitate the implementation of a modern Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition/Energy Management System and establishment of an optical communication network.
P509488-A1.name: fiber-optic SCADA/EMS and automated metering for regional grid control

P509243-A1.text: SIRAGE EMIS for school mapping, identifiers and refugee statistics. Uses the SIRAGE education management information system to map schools, assign linked unique identifiers, and track refugee enrollment for planning. Practices: SIRAGE EMIS data used for school mapping (Carte Scolaire) and infrastructure/teacher deployment planning; Operationalization of SIRAGE for real-time collection, reporting and analysis of enrollment, teacher, infrastructure and learning data; SIRAGE unique identifiers linked to national ID and Khidmety; SIRAGE refugee module for education statistics; climate vulnerability indicators in school mapping data systems; SIRAGE refugee module tracking refugee children enrollment. SIRAGE presents a valuable opportunity to address this issue, particularly by leveraging its data to revive school mapping (Carte Scolaire) and ensuring that infrastructure investments prioritize the completion of existing schools and the efficient deployment of teachers. The Education Management Information System (EMIS, Système d'Information de Gestion de l'Éducation, renamed SIRAGE), deployed through the World Bankfinanced Basic Education Sector Support Project (P163143), is an important tool for managing the education system and informing data-driven decision-making. The operationalization of SIRAGE32 will enable real-time data collection, reporting, and analysis. By covering areas such as student enrollment, teacher deployment, school infrastructure, and learning outcomes, SIRAGE will provide actionable insights to education policy makers and ensure that resources and interventions are tailored to local needs.
P509243-A1.name: SIRAGE EMIS for school mapping, identifiers and refugee statistics

P509243-A2.text: Hybrid digital and AI teacher training platform. Delivers continuous teacher training and coaching through the Tenwir hybrid platform and AI, including a refugee-specific module, tracked in SIRAGE. Practices: AI and digital hybrid teaching/coaching platform (Tenwir); continuous teacher training digital platform; Hybrid distance teacher training via CFED tracked in SIRAGE/Tenwir; Refugee-specific module in hybrid distance teacher training; Hybrid online plus in-person teacher training model; Tenwir digital platform for teacher training delivery. The Program will leverage the use of digital technology and artificial intelligence for teaching and coaching, using 30 Targeted communities are the highest concentration areas for refugees in the country: Wilaya of Hodh El CHarqi, Wilaya of Nouakchott South, Wilaya of Nouakchott West, Wilaya of Nouakchott North and Wilaya of Dakhlet Nouadhibou. Page 9 Official Use Only The World Bank Mauritania Improving Education Quality, Results, and Access for All Operation (IQRAA, P509243) the hybrid approach and platform (Tenwir) developed under the Basic Education Sector Support Project (P163143). To address this, a strategic approach involves implementing a continuous training digital platform, as successfully established by the ongoing Basic Education Sector Support Project (P163143). This platform facilitates ongoing professional development for teachers, making training more accessible and engaging.
P509243-A2.name: Hybrid digital and AI teacher training platform

P509243-A3.text: SIRAGE unique identifier for refugee enrollment DLI. A DLI counts refugee children only if they hold a SIRAGE unique identifier and national-curriculum enrollment. A dedicated DLI will incentivize the enrollment of refugee children in the national education system. To be counted, a child must hold a unique identifier in SIRAGE, be registered in a public or accredited private school, and receive instruction under the Mauritanian national curriculum.
P509243-A3.name: SIRAGE unique identifier for refugee enrollment DLI

P509243-A4.text: Edutainment and AI pilot in literacy and numeracy programs. Pilots edutainment and artificial intelligence tools in literacy and numeracy teaching. Additionally, this component will support the expansion of scripted lessons to upper grades of primary education, following successful pilot implementations, the pilot program on the inclusion of edutainment and artificial intelligence in literacy and numeracy programs, and the establishment of a robust learning assessment system to ensure that the National Evaluation Unit (Cellule Nationale d'Évaluation, CNE) conducts regular assessments34 and generates high-quality data to effectively measure learning poverty in alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals monitoring framework.
P509243-A4.name: Edutainment and AI pilot in literacy and numeracy programs

P509243-A5.text: SIRAGE as single sector management and verification tool. Makes SIRAGE the single sector management tool, with yearbook production and DLI data verified by an independent agency. Practices: SIRAGE as single sector management tool with timely yearbook production as a DLI; SIRAGE-sourced DLI data verified by an Independent Verification Agency. The Basic Education Sector Support Project (P163143) has supported the establishment of a strong management system, known as SIRAGE, which the Government is committed to using as a singular management tool for Page 17 Official Use Only The World Bank Mauritania Improving Education Quality, Results, and Access for All Operation (IQRAA, P509243) the sector. The Program has incorporated the timely production of yearbooks as a DLI, emphasizing the importance of leveraging SIRAGE capabilities. This strategic action aims to ensure that SIRAGE is effectively utilized and that necessary data are collected timely, thereby reinforcing the system's capacity to support informed decision-making. To ensure impartiality, the achievement of DLIs will be verified by an Independent Verification Agency (IVA), a firm contracted by the PCU under terms satisfactory to the World Bank.
P509243-A5.name: SIRAGE as single sector management and verification tool

P509243-A6.text: SIRAGE data and yearbooks as results-based financing triggers. Uses real-time SIRAGE data and published statistical yearbooks to verify DLIs and trigger disbursements under results-based financing. Practices: SIRAGE real-time data feeding results-based financing monitoring and DLI verification; SIRAGE-generated statistical yearbooks as disbursement trigger; DLI rewarding deployment of SIRAGE ECE, refugee, inclusive modules. The Program is designed to drive system-wide change, leveraging results-based financing to incentivize institutional reform and achieve sustainable educational improvements. A robust M&E framework will underpin Program implementation, utilizing SIRAGE for real-time data collection and monitoring. For subsequent years (Year 2–Year 5), US$500,000 is disbursed each year when the statistical yearbook generated by SIRAGE has been produced and published on MERSE's Formula website no later than December 15 of the calendar year in which the school year to which it relates ends and used for sector planning and monitoring. The statistical yearbook must include at least the following five key chapters for each education cycle (preprimary, primary, and secondary): (a) synthetic data and global indicators (enrollment rate, transition rate, success rate in national examinations);
P509243-A6.name: SIRAGE data and yearbooks as results-based financing triggers

P510090-A1.text: centralized housing information system for stock and needs. A unified digital system tracks housing stock and demand, including displaced persons, to guide investment decisions. Practices: centralized housing information system for stock and needs; Unified Housing Information and Analytical System for housing stock monitoring. To support the creation of a private housing market, the law mandates the creation of market-enabling mechanisms, such as a centralized housing information system with details on the available housing stock and needs, thereby allowing the planning and identification of investment opportunities. Throughout, the law emphasizes digitalization and digital solutions, including digitizing records. It also provided for the creation of a Unified Housing Information and Analytical System to monitor the housing stock and demand, as well as the development of a State Housing Policy Strategy to meet the needs of vulnerable groups and internally displaced persons, thereby ensuring the participation of the private sector in housing reconstruction.
P510090-A1.name: centralized housing information system for stock and needs

P510090-A2.text: transparent digital payment systems for state agricultural support. A paying agency uses digital payment systems, linked to the State Agrarian Registry, to disburse state support transparently. Practices: digital payment systems for state agricultural support via paying agency; transparent digital payment systems for state agricultural support.
