P510090-A3.text: unified emissions register for MRV reporting and verification. Requires monitoring, verification and improvement reports submitted through the unified national digital emissions register. It further mandates the submission of monitoring, verification, and improvement reports through the unified register of emissions (established through prior action 8), which serves as the national digital platform for emissions accounting. One of two ministerial orders (i) harmonizes how industrial installations report emissions data by specifying the structure, units, and indicators for carbon dioxide and other GHG emissions; and the other (ii) updates the methodology for calculating national GHG emissions to align with the International Panel for Climate Change and EU guidelines. Expected results: Reignited MRV system, captured in the results framework as an increase in the share of production sites covered by the new MRV system to 60 percent.
P510090-A3.name: unified emissions register for MRV reporting and verification

P510198-A1.text: compliance monitoring system with scoring for pollution enforcement. Builds a system scoring Category 2 projects' environmental compliance and tracking fines Development of a compliance monitoring system for air and water pollution control enforcement housed in MAE. The project will support the development and deployment of a compliance monitoring system for air and water pollution control enforcement to help the GoL better monitor and enforce environmental protection measures, especially for Category 2 investment projects.18 The system will comprise procedures for monitoring and evaluation (M&E) and reporting of compliance with environmental regulations, a compliance scoring system to track and report performance of Category 2 projects’ environmental obligations, and a system for monitoring fines and penalties. (d) cause EPF to establish and thereafter maintain, throughout Project implementation, a Project Coordination Team within EPF, which shall be responsible for carrying out v The World Bank Lao PDR Pollution and Waste Management Project (P510198) PROJECT APPRAISAL DOCUMENT the implementation of Part 1 of the Project, including inter alia financial management, procurement and environmental and social management, monitoring and evaluation and preparation of progress reports and annual work plans and budgets for Part 1 of the Project; and (e) cause MAE to establish and thereafter maintain, throughout Project implementation an Environmental and Social Monitoring Coordination Committee with the mandate to oversee and coordinate environmental and social aspects around the KM32 Landfill and adjacent Vientiane Waste Management Company concession area and at the KM16 and Naxaythong transfer stations as further described in the POM.
P510198-A1.name: compliance monitoring system with scoring for pollution enforcement

P510198-A2.text: waste database and infrared landfill fire monitoring. The project builds a standardized waste and plastics database piloted in Vientiane Capital and installs infrared monitors at the KM32 landfill for early fire warning. Practices: waste and plastics database piloted with Vientiane Capital; infrared monitors for early warning of landfill fires. Development of a basic waste and plastic information collection database housed in MAE. The database will be cost-effective with a user-friendly interface and standardized protocols for information providers and users, including national and subnational government and waste operators. The database will receive waste information from cities and districts, with a pilot phase planned in collaboration with the VC government. (ii) equipment – a weighbridge and washing, crushing, and pelletizing equipment at the waste management community center for IWWs, a small solar plant for on-site electricity generation, infrared monitors for early warning on potential landfill fires, and trucks and other equipment for landfill operation.
P510198-A2.name: waste database and infrared landfill fire monitoring

P510198-A3.text: online citizen feedback app on waste service quality. Finances an online feedback mechanism for real-time citizen complaints on waste collection, feeding tariff design. The project will support an online feedback mechanism, allowing real-time feedback on service quality and complaints. Subcomponent 2.1 will facilitate engagement with waste collection users; their feedback will be incorporated into the designs of the tariff structure. Survey results and data from the app will be reviewed by the recipient annually to determine adjustments needed to Component 2 activities.
P510198-A3.name: online citizen feedback app on waste service quality

P510476-A1.text: digital bookkeeping tools for community groups. Introduces community groups to digital bookkeeping and financial management tools for transparency and data. To enhance sustainability, community groups will be introduced to financial management and digital bookkeeping tools, ensuring efficiency, transparency, and availability of quality data for potential partner institutions, including banks and microfinance institutions.
P510476-A1.name: digital bookkeeping tools for community groups

P510476-A2.text: digital loans scored on transaction history. Introduces digital banking and payments enabling collateral-free digital loans based on transaction history. The project will introduce digital financial services, including digital banking and payments, to support access to low-risk, collateral- free digital loans based on transaction history.
P510476-A2.name: digital loans scored on transaction history

P510476-A3.text: interoperable MIS data sharing across projects. Links DRDIP II MIS with related projects to share beneficiary data and prevent overlap. (c) data sharing will be facilitated through interoperability between the DRDIP II management information system (MIS) and related projects;
P510476-A3.name: interoperable MIS data sharing across projects

P511696-A1.text: digital ambassador training and public middle-mile fiber for rural connectivity. Trains local Digital Ambassadors to deliver internet safety training and builds public middle-mile fiber where private investment is unviable. Practices: Digital Ambassadors train-the-trainer digital literacy delivery; public middle-mile fiber network enabling private ISP retail expansion. Furthermore, the DAIP has trained 3,500 people, adopting a train-the-trainer approach in its implementation by leveraging local talent (as ‘Digital Ambassadors’) in the connected municipalities to deliver trainings and contribute to beneficiary mobilization. Other digital literacy projects like the EU- funded Rural Development through Digital Inclusion (REDI) program are using these trainers for follow-up activities, ensuring continued support to rural communities. As a middle mile network aiming to provide access to fiber optic middle mile infrastructure to rural settlements that are financially unviable for the private sector, the Parent and AF Project enable private capital by: (i) stimulating parallel expansion of middle mile fiber optic networks to the more viable rural areas, given that least viable are being covered by the ON network; (ii) expansion of retail networks by ISPs and mobile operators to connect people and businesses in connected rural settlements; and (iii) upgrading retail network infrastructure for existing subscribers.
P511696-A1.name: digital ambassador training and public middle-mile fiber for rural connectivity

P511696-A2.text: underground middle-mile fiber network with Ookla speed monitoring. Deploys ~1,200 km of underground middle-mile fiber to rural settlements and uses Ookla subnational data to monitor broadband speeds. Practices: underground fiber deployment as climate-resilience measure; middle mile fiber network to 79 rural settlements; Ookla subnational data for broadband speed monitoring. For example, to mitigate the risks of landslides or high snowfall in mountainous areas, the network is deployed underground (at higher cost) instead of aerially. A major telecom operator in Georgia faced a country-wide outage in January 2025 due to damage to cross-border links with Türkiye, with heavy snowfall limiting repair capabilities.29 As such, the project will continue to deploy underground fiber as a climate resilience measure to mitigate the risk of leaving rural population unconnected due to snowstorms, landslides or flash floods. More specifically, the AF will finance the remaining network in Eastern Georgia by deploying the middle mile connectivity to the areas of Kvemo Kartli, Samtskhe-Javakheti, Mtskheta-Mtianeti, and Kakheti to cover 79 rural settlements, requiring approximately 1,200 km of middle mile infrastructure, completing the pan-national network in all regions as designed. Proceeds of the AF will be utilized to complete extending access to broadband services coutrywide as per the Open Net Program.
P511696-A2.name: underground middle-mile fiber network with Ookla speed monitoring

P510607-A1.text: AI-assisted airborne geophysics and digital drill core data for mineral prospectivity mapping. The project uses airborne geophysical surveys, sensor-scanned drill cores and AI/ML predictive models to map and rank mineral exploration targets. Practices: High-resolution airborne geophysics and prospectivity mapping datasets; Mineral systems approach for national geological prospectivity mapping; Sensor-scanned digitization of national drill core collections; AI/ML-assisted mineral prospectivity mapping from airborne surveys; groundwater resource assessments and geological hazard mapping feeding territorial planning and mining screening; probabilistic geoscience mapping products to prioritize exploration targets; Predictive modeling and airborne surveys to de-risk exploration; Digital drill core library database for geological samples; Airborne geophysical and remote-sensing mineral datasets. High-resolution airborne geophysics and surface mapping datasets published and accessible (km²). Target: 310,698 km² airborne (≤500 m spacing); 128,645 km² airborne (≤250 m, covering 24 smaller selection or targeted blocks); these 128,645 km² will include detailed geochemistry, field geological mapping validation and final prospectivity mapping (probabilities of exploration success) at higher-resolution scales of 1:50,000. This investment represents a strategic innovation in Peru’s mining sector, moving from conventional geological mapping toward a modern mineral systems approach that strengthens national geoscience capacity and supports diversification into critical minerals.
P510607-A1.name: AI-assisted airborne geophysics and digital drill core data for mineral prospectivity mapping

P510607-A2.text: Interoperable digital one-stop shop for mining permitting. The project builds a transactional VUD platform interlinking over ten permitting entities, automating workflows and integrating water, environmental and consultation data. Practices: Ventanilla Única Digital (VUD) online mining permitting platform; Interinstitutional Mining Digital One-Stop Shop (VUD) for permits; Interoperable automated workflow platform for MINEM regulatory processes; Interoperable digital one-stop shop for mining permits (VUD MINEM); Interoperable permitting platform linking permits, water and consultation modules; Fully transactional VUD-MINEM platform scaling piloted informative tool; Interoperable digital platforms integrating water authorizations, environmental information and socio-environmental commitments into permitting and oversight; VUD digital one-stop shop for mining permits; Digitalization and integration of core MINEM permitting workflows into centralized platforms; VUD one-stop shop consolidating mining permit steps. The digital transformation of the MINEM is essential to operationalize an effective Ventanilla Única Digital (VUD) that streamlines permitting, reduces uncertainty, and restores investor confidence. This component will strengthen MINEM’s capacity to lead sectoral modernization through three integrated interventions: (i) the digital transformation of its regulatory and administrative processes, (ii) the implementation of an interinstitutional Mining Digital One-Stop Shop VUD to centralize and streamline authorization procedures from exploration through mine closure, and (iii) the establishment of Technical Training Centers for ASM to improve skills, productivity, and compliance. Designed as a coherent package, these measures will equip MINEM and partner agencies with modern tools, efficient workflows, and specialized services that work in concert to reduce permitting times, strengthen oversight and territorial coordination, and expand technical training for ASM miners. Building on the identified gaps, the subcomponent will digitalize core administrative and regulatory procedures, integrate dispersed information into interoperable platforms, and establish standardized, automated workflows to ensure consistent and transparent 7 This subcomponent corresponds to Improvement of geochronology research services in the district of San Borja, Province of Lima, Department of Lima from the client’s public investment system [invierte.pe] 8 This subcomponent corresponds to Improvement and expansion of operational or institutional mission services in the information systems of the Ministry of Energy and Mines, District of San Borja, province of Lima, Lima department from the client’s public investment system [invierte.pe] Page 10 application of regulations.
P510607-A2.name: Interoperable digital one-stop shop for mining permitting

P512475-A1.text: integrated digital PFM, HRMIS payroll and statistics systems. Deploys modular FMIS/HRMIS with identity-verified payroll, hybrid cloud storage, digitized data transmission, business registers and satellite-machine-learning estimates. Practices: Automated payroll with identity-verified employee database and direct bank payment; Hybrid on-premise plus cloud data storage for statistics office; Digitized administrative data transmission systems for national accounts; Business register with unique tax-aligned business IDs; Satellite imagery and machine learning for production estimates; Incremental modular FMIS/HRMIS for PFM and payroll; Hybrid local hosting with cloud backup and hot disaster recovery; HRMIS verifying employee identity and establishment records for payroll; HRMIS identity verification and establishment record updates for payroll. Improve and automate HRM core processes: (a) Intervention: Improve, streamline, and automate critical HRM functions, including updating the public sector employees database and identity verification, and automating salary payment direct to bank accounts. Automated controls and direct payment will enable more timely and efficient payroll processing, provided there is fiscal space. Investments include installation of a hybrid data storage and transmission system that combines a physical location with a cloud solution, hybrid solar power systems, local Official Use Only Page 10 The World Bank Modernizing Public Institutions and Systems in Yemen (P512475) PROJECT APPRAISAL DOCUMENT and wide-area connectivity, laptops, IT hardware, and statistical software (including a comprehensive IT statistical system, provided by an appropriate peer national statistical office). (b) Digitizing administrative data and expanding data sources for SNA.
P512475-A1.name: integrated digital PFM, HRMIS payroll and statistics systems

P512475-A2.text: Web-based data user satisfaction survey with public feedback loop. Runs annual web survey of data users and publishes feedback and how it is used on CSO website. Frequency Annual Data source CSO-Aden’s website: https://demo2.cso-ye.org/ Extracted from the CSO-Aden website statistics Methodology for Data Collection Responsibility for Data UNDP and to be verified by the TPM Collection Improved data user satisfaction (Percentage) Data user satisfaction survey capturing satisfaction in the following areas: Availability of data relevant to needs, Description Timeliness of data publication, Ease of accessing data, Clarity of metadata and documentation, Consistency and reliability of statistics, Usefulness of data for decision‑making /analysis, in addition to trust in official statistics. The data user satisfaction data is collected and the summary of feedback and how the feedback is used are made available to the public via CSO website.
P512475-A2.name: Web-based data user satisfaction survey with public feedback loop

P512516-A1.text: single procurement portal and budget transparency portal publishing fiscal data. The project builds a single procurement portal publishing plans, tenders and awards plus a budget portal posting reports and answering citizen queries. Practices: Single Procurement Portal for public procurement transparency; Single Procurement Portal publishing procurement plans, notices and awards; Single Procurement Portal as gateway to e-GP adoption; Phased SIFMIS rollout from recording to workflow mode; Budget transparency portal publishing in-year reports and statements; Phased SIFMIS rollout prioritizing highest-payment governorate finance offices; Single Procurement Portal publishing tenders and contract awards; Budget Transparency Portal with Citizen's Budget Helpdesk. It also supports establishing a Single Procurement Portal (SPP) that will be critical for promoting transparency and providing all necessary information on public procurement to the government, the private sector, and the public. Additionally, a Complaint Handling Mechanism aims to build trust with the private sector and encourage competition; 3 https://syria-report.com/directory/association-of-syrian-certified-accountants/ 4 https://www.ifac.org/knowledge-gateway/audit-assurance/publications/statements-membership-obligations-1-7 5 300 external students admitted for 2024/2025 7 The World Bank Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516) PROJECT APPRAISAL DOCUMENT (b) Establishing a Single Procurement Portal (SPP) to serve as a gateway to all information about the procurement system and processes (procurement plans, notices, bidding documents and contract award decisions, and other procurement documentation). The SPP will be critical for promoting transparency and providing all necessary information on public procurement to the government, the private sector, and the public.
P512516-A1.name: single procurement portal and budget transparency portal publishing fiscal data

P512516-A2.text: integrated SIFMIS with biometric payroll, banking interfaces and secure infrastructure. The project deploys a web-based SIFMIS with biometric payroll, bank interfaces, digital signatures, disaster recovery and blockchain grant tracking. Practices: Web-based PFM e-learning with online testing and self-certification; SIFMIS payroll module with biometric registration; API linking SIFMIS to CBS core banking and SYGS; Digital signature with PKI for secure fiscal transactions; Centralized payroll module with biometric entry/exit controls; SIFMIS core financial management modules for central government entities; Resilient SIFMIS infrastructure with solar backup and tiered data centers; On-premises hot disaster recovery center with real-time SIFMIS replication; blockchain Funds Chain platform tracking grant proceeds; SIFMIS processing of budget payments and payroll; Biometric registration of staff in SIFMIS payroll module. The same could be made available for officials from remote areas. This will be a web-based learning program using the same study material as for the PFM courses as a computer-generated study program with on-line testing at end of each subject with self-certification to complete each module. The envisaged Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) SIFMIS will support procedural and control systems to ensure the legality, accuracy and timelines of fiscal information in the following core PFM functions: budget preparation, budget execution, human resource/payroll with biometric registration (including robust data protection and privacy safeguards), expenditure control, cash management, purchasing, revenue management, fixed asset registration, inventory management, accounting, reporting, audit trails, and financial reporting/analytics with in-built dashboards for online publication. The project will support development of an Application Programming Interface (API) or the use of file transfer to exchange data (where API is not technically possible) between the CBS in-house developed core banking system (Nahas) and the in-house Syrian Gross Settlements System (SYGS) for interbank transfers, with the SIFMIS for revenue, expenditure, and automated bank reconciliation.
P512516-A2.name: integrated SIFMIS with biometric payroll, banking interfaces and secure infrastructure

P512516-A3.text: Syria Budget Transparency Portal with geo-mapped outputs and citizen helpdesk. Designs a public budget dashboard publishing execution reports, GEMS geo-mapped outputs and a citizen helpdesk Drawing from this framework, the project will provide support to design the Syria Budget Transparency Portal -a public budget dashboard to serve diverse types of users, including citizens (The Timor-Leste Transparency Portal12 is a good example). To enhance fiscal transparency, budget execution reports (BERs) will be published on this dashboard, as well as geo-mapped project outputs with SIFMIS fiscal data when applicable, by leveraging the Geo-Enabling initiative for Monitoring and Supervision (GEMS). To foster citizens’ interest and ownership of the public budget, the dashboard will also incorporate a “citizen’s budget helpdesk” to respond to citizens’ queries and suggestions regarding Syria’s budget .
P512516-A3.name: Syria Budget Transparency Portal with geo-mapped outputs and citizen helpdesk

P513127-A1.text: Ministry-wide MIS digitalizing permitting and operational processes. Project rolls out a ministry-wide Management Information System to digitize MoPWRH permitting and operational processes. Within the MoPWRH, the Project will carry ongoing capacity building activities in World Bank-financed SHIIP and SURP II projects forward, such as the development of an Axle Load law and rollout of a ministry wide Management Information System to allow for the digitalization of several permitting and operational processes.
P513127-A1.name: Ministry-wide MIS digitalizing permitting and operational processes

P513127-A2.text: ADS-B/VSAT ground surveillance for Somali airspace. Project supplies, installs and commissions ADS-B/VSAT surveillance to improve air traffic control visibility. The Project will supply, install, integrate, commission, and provide technical support for Automatic Dependent Surveillance – Broadcast/Very Small Aperture Terminal (ADS-B/VSAT). ADS-B (1090 Megahertz Mode S Extended Squitter) ground surveillance system will enhance air traffic control and improve visibility of commercial and private aircraft operating in Somali airspace.
P513127-A2.name: ADS-B/VSAT ground surveillance for Somali airspace

P513127-A3.text: FundsChain platform integrated with SFMIS for fund traceability. Project adopts FundsChain, integrated with SFMIS payment flows, to track funds and fixed assets end-to-end. This project will adopt the FundsChain platform to enhance transparency, traceability, and efficiency in the Project financial management. FundsChain will be integrated with Somalia Financial Information Management System (SFMIS), using payment flows alongside FundsChain's reporting capabilities. In addition, the platform will be used to track built and procured fixed assets, enhancing the expenditure reporting and end-to-end traceability of project resources within the three implementing entities.
P513127-A3.name: FundsChain platform integrated with SFMIS for fund traceability

P517113-A1.text: web and mobile digital grievance redressal system for bus passengers. Program establishes accessible continuous feedback via a digital web and mobile grievance system. It will establish citizen-centric service delivery through accessible and continuous feedback mechanisms, including a digital grievance redressal system (web and mobile).
P517113-A1.name: web and mobile digital grievance redressal system for bus passengers

P513322-A1.text: Unified digital system for processing and distributing social benefits. Project creates a single system to process and pay all social benefits, replacing fragmented administration. (iv) modernization of disability assessment and improvement of disability support aligned with international standards; and (v) improved administrative efficiency through the creation of a unified system for processing and distributing social benefits. The proposed SPIRIT project advances a cohesive and transformative social protection agenda across five interconnected priorities: (i) introduction of Basic Social Assistance (BSA) with integrated case management linking cash transfers to social and employment services;
P513322-A1.name: Unified digital system for processing and distributing social benefits

P513080-A1.text: integrated government management information systems with predictive analytics and data lake. Deploys integrated asset, payroll, pension, investment and procurement systems plus a state data lake and predictive analytics to centralize and audit government data. Practices: Integrated asset management system with comprehensive inventory; Predictive analytics and automated auditing of state payroll; Integrated pension management system interoperable with HR system; Predictive actuarial analytics tool for pension liabilities; Automated auditing of pension and retirement payroll; Integrated public investment project management system; Geolocation tools for monitoring state real estate assets; Government data lake centralizing and de-duplicating agency data; Automated IFR reporting via i-Gesp integration with SGI and target platform; State data lake integrating agencies for whole-of-government management; Pension management system SISPREV integrated with HRMIS and FMIS; Management analytics product on audit data flagging payroll nonconformity risk areas for control; State data lake integrating agency systems; New e-GP tool with management dashboards; People analytics on gender-disaggregated HR and pension data; AI pilots detecting fraud in public procurement. Implementing a robust asset management strategy, supported by a comprehensive inventory and integrated system, will strengthen asset management, enabling states to optimize their portfolios and improve revenue generation. The lack of reliable data and integrated systems hampers lifecycle management, covering inventory, valuation, maintenance, and disposal, while limited methodologies and insufficient training reduce consistency and oversight. (c) improving payroll management, including regulatory review, process automation, and deployment of advanced analytics for automated auditing and predictive payroll growth; (b) implementing a new or upgraded integrated pension management system, with interoperability to the existing human resources management and information system;
P513080-A1.name: integrated government management information systems with predictive analytics and data lake

P513080-A2.text: integrated procurement and enterprise architecture with citizen feedback tracking. Connects procurement, contract and financial systems through enterprise architecture and logs citizen feedback on investment proposals in the Ombudsperson system. Practices: Integrated procurement platform with analytics and contract management tools; Enterprise systems architecture and integration across government systems; Citizen feedback on public investment proposals logged via Ombudsperson system, with acknowledgement/response tracked as results indicator. (b) procuring planning workflows and contract management tools through the deployment of technological solutions and integrating it to an existing financial management system; Through the integration of digital platforms, data analytics, and strategic sourcing tools, it will improve transparency, value for money, and expenditure control across the procurement cycle. (g) developing the Borrower’s enterprise systems architecture, including technology standards; (f) mapping existing systems, including identifying the data stored by each system, overlaps in information, and the services and processes each system supports;
P513080-A2.name: integrated procurement and enterprise architecture with citizen feedback tracking

P513080-A3.text: Intergovernmental transfers module linked to federal transfer system. Implements a transfers management module integrated with the federal government's transfer system (e) implementing an intergovernmental transfers management module, including integration to the federal government’s transfer system;

P513080-A4.text: education infrastructure management and cost planning dashboards. Builds an education infrastructure management system with contract tools and analytics dashboards for cost and school network planning. P513080-A4.name: education infrastructure management and cost planning dashboards

P513080-A5.name: Integrated management system for tracking SUAS intergovernmental transfers

P513080-A6.name: Intergovernmental transfers system with public monitoring dashboard

P514107-A1.text: social registry MIS with API interoperability and hazard-data targeting. A management information system holds socio-economic data on about 10 million people, shared via secure APIs and overlaid with flood models for targeting. Practices: RSU social registry MIS for multi-program targeting; Flood hazard mapping overlaying RSU data with FATHOM risk models; coverage diagnostic mapping underserved areas for RSU expansion; API interoperability between RSU MIS and social program systems; API-based secure data exchange between RSU MIS and social program systems; RSU-MIS registry of rural household socio-economic data via outreach. The RSU Management Information System (MIS) is now fully operational and contains socio-economic data of about 1.7 million households (close to 10 million individuals) as of June 2026. Eight programs use the RSU for targeting. A large survey drive in 1,000 villages and a campaign in urban areas were completed in early September 2026; the information is being processed and the operation is expected to result in 2.1 million households registered by December 2026 (PDO-level indicator target), supported by 1,200 trained professionals across 31 regions and an expanded network of 354 fixed registration points (guichets) for on-demand registration. In conjunction to the implementation of the PforR, as part of the Bank’s technical assistance, a flood hazard mapping exercise – overlaying RSU household data with FATHOM risk models – was conducted in the Cavally region to showcase the potential of geographic targeting.
P514107-A1.name: social registry MIS with API interoperability and hazard-data targeting

P514107-A2.text: digital cash transfers and mobile-wallet savings for poor households. Digital payments and savings accounts via mobile operators, with literacy training and operator-data verification, replace cash-based transfers and savings for beneficiaries. Practices: Pre-protocol digital cash transfers for flood-affected households; Multi-operator G2P payment mechanism with beneficiary provider choice; remunerated digital savings accounts with literacy training and nudges; piloted digital savings model scaled up for PTMP beneficiaries; digital savings accounts scale-up via mobile wallets; digital financial inclusion pilot with rigorous evaluation and scale-up roadmap; trigger-based digital cash transfers to flood-affected households; mobile-operator data verification of digital account ownership; TrésorPay/TrésorMoney government payment platform assessment. Shock response framework defined and operationalized, with tangible results achieved including a pilot providing digital cash transfers, according to preestablished protocols, to 1,731 poor households affected by flooding in the Cavally region – demonstrating the Program's operational readiness to respond rapidly to covariate shocks. The operational protocol and manual were designed, and the mechanism was successfully piloted in 2024. On payment systems, the AF will continue supporting the transition toward a multi-operator G2P payment mechanism and towards introducing beneficiary choice among payment providers. The dynamics among operators in the mobile payments sector in Côte d’Ivoire makes beneficiaries choice possible.
P514107-A2.name: digital cash transfers and mobile-wallet savings for poor households

P514107-A3.text: API and web-service interoperability of the social registry. Secure API and web-service connections let partner social programs share and use the registry's targeting data. Practices: API/web-service interoperability of social registry with partner programs; API interoperability between RSU MIS and social program systems. Under DLI 2, the Program will consolidate the existing foundations by: (i) progressively updating data that is more than three years old and rolling-out an institutional mechanism for continuous updates relying on an expansion of existing guichets, with particular focus on exiting PTMP cohorts and areas prone to climate and other risks; DLR Indicator Name NEW DLR 2.10 : Interoperability and secure data exchanges through an application programming interface between the RSU management information system and three other social program’s information systems are operational Formula Scalable and not timebound. USD 1,000,000 per social program information system connected Description Data source/ Agency BCPFS and RSU partner programs The World Bank First Additional Financing to the Côte d'Ivoire Productive Social Safety Nets System Strengthening Program (P175594) Page 70 Official Use Only Verification Entity IVA Procedure The IVA will very that interoperability and secure data exchanges through API between the SIG-RSU and at least three other government programs, projects or otherwise identifiable development interventions are operational. Verification will review technical documentation and system logs, and confirm whether data exchanges are secure, as evidenced by compliance with data protection and security protocols outlined in the RSU Operations Manual.
P514107-A3.name: API and web-service interoperability of the social registry
